dambis-dubins-schwarz-theorem — Dambis–Dubins–Schwarz time-change theorem [theorem]
  A real continuous local martingale M starting at0 can be represented as B_{⟨M⟩_t} for a Brownian motion on its quadratic-variation clock, after extension by independent Brownian noise if the terminal bracket is finite.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: False
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Quadratic covariation of continuous semimartingales [both]: The clock is the quadratic variation ⟨M⟩ of the continuous local martingale M and its terminal value ⟨M⟩_∞; the proof time-changes by its right inverse σ_t.
  <- Independent family of random elements [statement]: If ⟨M⟩_∞<∞ with positive probability, the representing Brownian motion uses additional Brownian noise independent of the original probability space.
  <- Product measure [statement]: The extension of the probability space by independent noise is the product of the original probability space with a space carrying a Brownian motion.
  <- Lévy characterization of Brownian motion [proof]: The time-changed process M_{σ_t} is shown to be a continuous martingale with bracket t and then identified as Brownian by Lévy characterization.
  <- Optional sampling for a uniformly integrable càdlàg martingale [proof]: The stopped process M^{σ_t} is a uniformly integrable continuous martingale closed at time infinity; optional sampling at σ_s≤σ_t (after a homeomorphic compactification of the time axis to a finite horizon) gives E[M_{σ_t}|F_{σ_s}]=M_{σ_s}.
  <- Quadratic-variation isometry for continuous martingales [proof]: Lemmas 3.5-3.6 and the L²-boundedness of M^{σ_t} use E[M²_{τ}]=E⟨M⟩_{τ} for localized stopping times, showing M is constant on intervals of constancy of ⟨M⟩ and ⟨M^{σ_t}⟩_∞=t.
  <- Usual conditions for a filtration [proof]: The selected proof uses right continuity of the filtration so that σ_t=inf{s:⟨M⟩_s>t} are stopping times.

riemann-darboux-criterion — Darboux criterion for Riemann integrability [theorem]
  A bounded function on a compact rectangle is Riemann integrable if and only if for every ε>0 there is a rectangular partition whose upper and lower Darboux sums differ by less than ε.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: False
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Riemann integral [statement]: The defining data or statement explicitly presuppose riemann-integral.
  <- Greatest lower bound [statement]: The defining data or statement explicitly presuppose greatest-lower-bound.
  <- Riemann integral over a box in ℝᵏ [statement]: The criterion concerns Riemann integrability of a bounded function on a compact coordinate rectangle in ℝⁿ, with upper and lower sums over partitions into subrectangles of the rectangle-partitions used by that integral.
  explains in trench-introduction-real-analysis-2013, Theorem 3.2.7 (interval) and Theorem 7.1.12 (rectangles), pp. 133, 447 — Statement; the rectangle proof is left as Exercise 7.1.12. Not a priority claim.
  Related: Equivalence of the Riemann and Darboux integrals — Both relate Riemann integrability to Darboux sums; the criterion is the ε-partition form on rectangles.

davies-simon-log-sobolev-ultracontractivity — Davies–Simon logarithmic Sobolev criterion for ultracontractivity [theorem]
  Let a symmetric Markov semigroup have a strongly local Dirichlet form E on L²(μ). If for every normalized f in its form domain and0<ε≤1, ∫f²log(f²)dμ≤εE(f,f)+C₀+C₁|logε|, then its operators map L²(μ) boundedly into L∞(μ) at every positive time. The criterion applies to the ground-state-transformed elliptic forms here.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Ultracontractive symmetric Markov semigroup [both]: The conclusion is that the semigroup maps L² boundedly into L∞ at every positive time, i.e. it is ultracontractive; the proof bounds ‖e^{−Ht}‖_{2→∞}≤e^{M(t)}.
  <- Strong locality of a symmetric Dirichlet form [statement]: The record states the criterion for strongly local forms (the Davies–Simon setting); the inspected proof does not use strong locality.
  <- Closed symmetric form–semigroup correspondence [both]: “Its Dirichlet form” refers to the form attached to the self-adjoint generator; Lemma 2.2.6 uses Q(f)=lim t⁻¹⟨(1−e^{−Ht})f,f⟩.
  <- Beurling–Deny criteria for positivity-preserving and sub-Markov semigroups [proof]: Lemma 2.2.6 proves Q(g^{p/2})≤p²/(4(p−1))⟨Hg,g^{p−1}⟩ using the symmetric-measure representation of e^{−Ht} from the proof of Theorem 1.3.3 (Beurling–Deny conditions).
  <- Hölder’s inequality [proof]: Inequality (2.2.9) is proved with the Schwarz inequality for ∫s^{p/2−1}ds.
  <- Derivative of a real function [proof]: Theorem 2.2.7 differentiates log(e^{−N(s)}‖f_s‖_{p(s)}) along the ODE dp/ds=p/ε(p) using Lemma 2.2.2.
  <- Fatou’s lemma [proof]: Note 2.2.9: the hypothesis on a form-norm dense class extends to the needed f by Fatou’s lemma; density of D₊ in L² ends Theorem 2.2.7.

davis-local-martingale-decomposition — Davis decomposition of a càdlàg local martingale [theorem]
  For a real càdlàg local martingale M starting at0, write S_t=sup_(s≤t)|ΔM_s|. After localization with E S_∞<∞, M=K+L with K a finite-variation martingale, E TV(K)_∞≤4 E S_∞, and L a local martingale with |ΔL_t|≤4S_(t−). The decomposition is used locally when the expectations are not globally finite.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Local martingale [statement]: M is a real càdlàg local martingale; L is a local martingale.
  <- Function of bounded variation on an interval [statement]: K has finite total variation TV(K)_∞ with E TV(K)_∞≤4E S_∞.
  <- Compensator of an adapted process of integrable variation [proof]: K² is the compensator of K¹=∑_(s≤t,|ΔM_s|≥2S_(s−))ΔM_s, whose variation is at most 2S_∞; E Var(K²)≤2E S_∞ and K=K¹−K² is a martingale.
  <- Totally inaccessible stopping time [proof]: Jump bounds for L are checked separately at totally inaccessible and predictable times.
  <- Predictable càdlàg processes do not jump at totally inaccessible times [proof]: K² is predictable, so L and L¹ have the same jump at a totally inaccessible T, bounded by 2S_(T−).
  <- σ-algebra strictly before a stopping time [proof]: At predictable T the jump of L² is computed as −E[ΔL¹_T|F_(T−)].
  <- Zero conditional mean of a martingale jump at a predictable time [proof]: Since L is a martingale, E[ΔL_T|F_(T−)]=0 at predictable T, so ΔL²_T=−E[ΔL¹_T|F_(T−)].
  <- Measurability of a predictable process at a stopping time [proof]: ΔL²_T and S_(T−) are F_(T−)-measurable at predictable T, giving |ΔL²_T|≤2E[S_(T−)|F_(T−)]=2S_(T−).
  <- Accessible and totally inaccessible parts of a stopping time [proof]: Every stopping time splits into a totally inaccessible part and an accessible part covered by predictable times, so the two cases control |ΔL_T| at every stopping time.
  <- Optional section theorem [proof]: “D’après le théorème de section”: the optional set {|ΔL|>4S_−} is evanescent because it carries no stopping-time graph.
  explains in meyer-dual-h1-bmo-continuous-1973, Appendix, p. 145 — Continuous-time construction of the Davis decomposition; the discrete-time decomposition is Davis 1970.

de-franchis-finiteness-characteristic-zero — De Franchis finiteness in characteristic zero [theorem]
  For fixed smooth projective geometrically connected curves D and C over a characteristic-zero field k with g(C)≥2, there are only finitely many nonconstant k-morphisms D→C. The characteristic-zero qualification excludes the infinite Frobenius iterates possible in positive characteristic.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Genus of a smooth projective curve [statement]: The named input specifies the objects in the statement or definition.
  <- Characteristic of a field [statement]: The theorem is stated over a field of characteristic zero; in characteristic p Frobenius iterates give infinitely many nonconstant maps.
  <- Intersection number of divisors on a smooth projective variety [proof]: The proof computes intersection numbers on the surface X=C′×C: Γ_φ·(C′×{P})=d, Γ_φ·({P′}×C)=1, Γ_φ·K_X and the self-intersection Γ_φ².
  <- Adjunction formula for a curve on a smooth projective surface [proof]: The adjunction formula Γ·K_X=2g′−2−Γ² for the graph Γ_φ≅C′ gives Γ_φ²=−(2g−2)d<0, and identifies its normal sheaf degree with Γ_φ².
  <- Riemann–Hurwitz formula in characteristic zero [proof]: The Hurwitz formula 2g′−2=d(2g−2)+(ramification) bounds the degree d of every nonconstant map by (g′−1)/(g−1), using g≥2 (over an algebraic closure; characteristic zero).
  <- Hilbert scheme of a projective scheme [proof]: Graphs of maps of bounded degree are closed subschemes of X with finitely many Hilbert polynomials, hence points of finitely many projective Hilbert schemes Hilb_P(X).
  <- Tangent space of the Hilbert scheme at a subscheme [proof]: Each graph has normal sheaf of negative degree Γ_φ², so H⁰(Γ_φ,N)=0 and its Hilbert-scheme point is isolated; finitely many components then give finitely many graphs.
  <- Degree of a generically finite dominant morphism [proof]: The degree d of φ appears as #φ⁻¹(P) for a general point, giving Γ_φ·(C′×{P})=d.
  <- Degree of a coherent sheaf on a projective curve [proof]: The normal sheaf of the graph is a line bundle of degree Γ_φ²<0, so it has no nonzero global sections.
  <- Riemann–Roch theorem for smooth projective curves [proof]: Implicit step: with respect to the ample class of fibers, the graph Γ_φ≅C′ has degree d+1 and genus g′, so its Hilbert polynomial (d+1)t+1−g′ takes finitely many values as d is bounded.

  Distinct field homomorphisms σ₁,…,σ_n:E→L are linearly independent over L as L-valued functions on E: if ∑a_iσ_i(x)=0 for every x∈E with a_i∈L, then every a_i=0.

ring-integers-dedekind — Dedekind property of the ring of integers [theorem]
  The ring of integers of a number field, and every localization at finitely many primes, is a Dedekind domain: it is noetherian, integrally closed and has dimension1. In particular its finitely generated algebras are finitely presented.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Ring of integers of a number field [both]: The theorem is about the ring of integers; the proof identifies it with the integral closure of ℤ in K.
  <- Dedekind domain [both]: The conclusion is the Dedekind property; the proof checks its three defining conditions.
  <- Finitely presented commutative algebra [both]: The final clause asserts finite presentation.
  <- Integral closure of a Dedekind domain in a finite separable extension [proof]: Milne proves the result for O_K by Theorem 3.29 with A=ℤ, L=K (separable in characteristic zero); ℤ is a Dedekind domain because its ideals are nℤ, pℤ is maximal and ℤ is integrally closed (Example 2.10(a)).
  <- Localization of a Dedekind domain [proof]: The localized rings O_K[1/S] are Dedekind by Proposition 3.4 (via Proposition 3.5 for Noetherianity and integral closedness).
  <- Hilbert basis theorem [proof]: A finitely generated algebra over a Noetherian ring is a quotient of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables, which is Noetherian by the Hilbert basis theorem, so the kernel ideal is finitely generated.

  For a group G and a field F, every finite set of distinct group homomorphisms χ₁,…,χ_m:G→F× is linearly independent over F as F-valued functions on G: if ∑a_iχ_i(g)=0 for every g∈G, with a_i∈F, then all a_i=0.

deformation-to-normal-cone — Deformation to the normal cone [construction]
  For a closed subscheme Z⊂X, the deformation space M°_Z X→𝔸¹ is glued from the spectra of the extended Rees algebras ∑_(n∈ℤ)s^(−n)Iⁿ⊂A[s,s^(−1)] (with Iⁿ=A for n≤0) over affine opens Spec A of X with I the ideal of Z. Its restriction over s≠0 is X×(𝔸¹∖0) and its fibre over s=0, a principal divisor, is the normal cone C_Z X.

elliptic-isogeny-degree-positive-definite-quadratic-form — Degree as a positive definite quadratic form on elliptic homomorphisms [theorem]
  For elliptic curves E₁,E₂ over a field, set deg 0=0. Then deg:Hom(E₁,E₂)→ℤ is a positive definite quadratic form: deg(nφ)=n²deg φ, deg φ>0 for φ≠0, and (φ,ψ)↦deg(φ+ψ)−deg φ−deg ψ is ℤ-bilinear. Bilinearity comes from the dual isogeny, with φ̂φ=[deg φ].

degree-generically-finite-morphism — Degree of a generically finite dominant morphism [definition]
  For a dominant morphism f:X→Y of integral schemes of finite type over a field with dim X=dim Y, the function field K(X) (the fraction field of the coordinate ring of any nonempty affine open) is a finite extension of K(Y) via f, and deg f=[K(X):K(Y)]. Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, a general point of Y has exactly deg f preimages.

nilrotation-minimality-density-criterion — Density criterion for minimality of a two-step nilrotation [theorem]
  Let X=G/Γ with G a two-step nilpotent Lie group and Γ closed cocompact, T the translation by τ∈G, and suppose G is generated by its identity component and τ. Then (X,T) is minimal iff the subgroup generated by τ and Γ is dense in G, iff the subgroup generated by τ and ΓG₂ is dense. In that case the Kronecker factor of (X,T) with Haar measure is the rotation by the image of τ on the compact abelian group G/G₂Γ.

  Let E be an elliptic curve over a field K and ℓ a prime different from char K. For every endomorphism ψ of E, the induced ℤ_ℓ-linear map ψ_ℓ on the rank-two Tate module T_ℓE satisfies det ψ_ℓ=deg ψ and tr ψ_ℓ=1+deg ψ−deg(1−ψ), with deg 0=0. In particular both are integers independent of ℓ.

diagonal-uniqueness-analytic-kernel — Diagonal uniqueness for a sesquiholomorphic kernel [theorem]
  If K(z,w) is holomorphic in z and antiholomorphic in w on a connected disk product, and K(z,z)=0 throughout the disk, then K is identically zero. Thus such a kernel is determined by its diagonal.

  <- Fourier coefficient of an integrable circle function [proof]: Near any point expandK(z,w)=Σa_mn(z−z₀)^m(w̄−z̄₀)^n. On the diagonalz=z₀+re^{it}, integrate each Fourier mode m−n. Its power series inr is identically zero, and its exponentsm+n are distinct for fixedm−n, so everya_mn vanishes. K vanishes on a product neighborhood; apply the one-variable identity theorem successively in the two variables to obtain global vanishing.

gowers-block-diagonal-decomposition — Diagonal-plus-strictly-singular decomposition on Gowers block subspaces [theorem]

The coordinate inequality and unconditionality give∥P_kx∥≤K2^(−k)∥T_kx∥, contradicting that estimate for largek. ThusT_k is strictly singular; the remainingR has zero overlap with its own input block. If off-block image coordinates vanish, the residualR vanishes. Unconditionality constants are absorbed rather than assumed exactly1.

smooth-quadratic-pencil-diagonalization — Diagonalization of a smooth pencil of quadrics [theorem]
  Let A,B be symmetric k×k matrices over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from two, with k≥3. If their two projective quadratic equations define a smooth codimension-two intersection, then an invertible change of variables makes both matrices diagonal, diag(a_i),diag(b_i), with every pair(a_i,b_i) nonzero and all ratios[a_i:b_i] distinct. Equivalently det(sA+tB) has k distinct projective roots; in particular every nonzero pencil member has rank at least k−1.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

  Over a field of characteristic different from two, every symmetric matrix A admits an invertible matrix P with PᵀAP diagonal. Over an algebraically closed field, it is congruent to diag(I_r,0), where r=rankA.

hencl-pratelli-w11-approximation — Diffeomorphic approximation of planar W¹,¹ homeomorphisms [theorem]
  For an open Ω⊆ℝ², every homeomorphism f∈W¹,¹(Ω,ℝ²) admits smooth diffeomorphisms and locally finitely piecewise affine homeomorphisms arbitrarily close both uniformly and in W¹,¹. If f extends continuously to ∂Ω, approximants can have the same boundary values. On a polygonal domain, when f is piecewise affine on the boundary, the affine approximant can use a finite triangulation.

dominated-differentiation-under-integral — Differentiation under an integral with an integrable derivative bound [theorem]
  Let I be an open real interval, (X,μ) a σ-finite measure space and f:I×X→ℝ measurable. number-field-order-discriminant-index — Discriminant index formula for number-field orders [theorem]
  For a number field K and a subring A⊂O_K containing1 and of finite index, the trace discriminants satisfy disc(A/ℤ)=[O_K:A]² d_K, where d_K is the integral-basis field discriminant. The discriminant of A is computed using any ℤ-basis of A.

complete-intersection-discriminant-locus — Discriminant locus of projective complete intersections [definition]
  For a field K, integers N≥1 and 1≤c≤N+1, and degrees d₁,…,d_c≥1, let V be the affine space of c-tuples (F₁,…,F_c) of homogeneous polynomials in N+1 variables with deg F_i=d_i. The discriminant locus D⊂V is the Zariski-closed set of tuples for which {F₁=⋯=F_c=0}⊂P^N over an algebraic closure is not a smooth complete intersection of codimension c: either the codimension is smaller or the Jacobian matrix (∂F_i/∂x_j) has rank <c at a common zero. It carries its reduced structure; when D is a hypersurface its equation is the discriminant.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

  <- Zariski topology on an affine variety [statement]: D is a Zariski-closed subset of the affine space V, with its reduced structure.
  Related: Discriminant of equal-degree complete intersections — The equal-degree discriminant theorem describes the equation of this discriminant locus when all d_i=d≥2 (its primitive integral equation, irreducibility and multidegrees).

  <- Reflection principle for Brownian motion [proof]: Under zero drift, reflection gives the endpoint density on {M_t≥a}: it is the ordinary Gaussian densityφ_t(y) for y≥a andφ_t(2a−y) for y<a. Tilt this density by exp(μy−μ²t/2). Integrating y≥a gives1−Φ((a−μt)/√t). In the reflected integral substitute z=2a−y to obtain exp(2μa)Φ((−a−μt)/√t). Their sum is the upper-tail crossing probability; subtract from one to obtain the stated maximum distribution. Conditioning at an intermediate Brownian time uses the barrier displacement a=u−X_t and the remaining horizon; it cannot reuse u unchanged as the erroneous local formula afterQMC(9) does.

divisibility-commutative-ring — Divisibility and units in a commutative ring [definition]

doob-strong-feller-irreducible-mixing — Doob’s strong-Feller irreducible mixing theorem [theorem]
  A stochastically continuous Markov semigroup on a Polish space which is strong Feller and topologically irreducible at each positive time has at most one invariant probability measure; if it exists, P_t(x,·) converges to it in total variation for every x. Strong Feller means bounded Borel functions become continuous, and irreducibility means P_t(x,O)>0 for each nonempty open O.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Polish space [statement]: The state space is Polish.
  <- Stochastically continuous Markov semigroup [statement]: The hypothesis is a stochastically continuous Markov semigroup; this also supplies the Markov transition semigroup.
  <- Strong Feller Markov kernel [both]: Each P_t, t>0, is a strong Feller kernel; the proof feeds this into Khas’minskii’s criterion.
  <- Topologically irreducible Markov semigroup [both]: Irreducibility P_t(x,O)>0 at each positive time; the proof feeds it into Khas’minskii’s criterion.
  <- Invariant probability for a Markov semigroup [both]: The conclusion concerns invariant probability measures; the proof uses invariance of μ for the time-t₀ skeleton chain.
  <- Total variation distance between probability measures [both]: Convergence is in total variation; the proof bounds ‖P_n(x,·)−P_n(y,·)‖ and uses its monotonicity in time.
  <- Limit of a real sequence [statement]: Convergence as t→∞; since t↦‖P_t(x,·)−μ‖ is nonincreasing, this is the limit along integer multiples of a fixed time.
  <- Khas’minskii’s regularity theorem for strong Feller irreducible semigroups [proof]: Strong Feller at s and irreducibility at t give (s+t)-regularity: all P_{s+t}(x,·) are equivalent, the hypothesis (2) of Kulik–Scheutzow Theorem 1 for the skeleton chain.
  <- Time-homogeneous Markov chain on a measurable state space [proof]: The argument works with the time-t₀ skeleton chain and with Markov chains on E×E.
  <- Invariant probability of a Markov kernel [proof]: Invariance of μ for the skeleton kernel gives the triangle-inequality passage from (5) to (3) and the stationary version in Lemma 2.
  <- Coupling inequality for total variation [proof]: Inequality (6): ‖ν₁−ν₂‖≤2P(ξ₁≠ξ₂) for any coupling, applied to the constructed chain Z.
  <- Maximal coupling of probability measures [proof]: Lemma 1 is a measurable kernel version of the maximal coupling (splitting) construction.
  <- Radon–Nikodym theorem for finite measures [proof]: Lemma 1 takes jointly measurable Radon–Nikodym densities of P(x_i,·) with respect to their average.
  <- Stopping time for a filtration [proof]: The coupling attempts occur at the successive hitting times τ_k of the set C, which are stopping times.
  <- Strong Markov property of a discrete-time Markov chain [proof]: After an unsuccessful coupling attempt the chain restarts at the stopping time τ_k+1 by the strong Markov property.

douglas-factorization-theorem — Douglas range inclusion and factorization theorem [theorem]
  For bounded maps A:H₁→H₀ and B:H₂→H₀ between Hilbert spaces, Ran A⊆Ran B, AA*≤λBB* for some λ≥0, and A=BC for some bounded C are equivalent. The least possible ∥C∥ is the square root of the least such λ.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True

geometric-drift-geometric-regularity-characterization — Drift characterization of geometric regularity of a Markov chain [theorem]
  For a ψ-irreducible Markov chain: if an everywhere finite V≥1, a petite set C, β>0 and b<∞ satisfy PV≤(1−β)V+b1_C, then for every B with ψ(B)>0 there are r>1 and c(B)<∞ with E_x[∑_{k=1}^{τ_B}V(X_k)r^k]≤c(B)V(x) for all x. Conversely, if for some petite C and κ>1 the quantity E_x[∑_{k=0}^{τ_C−1}f(X_k)κ^k] is finite for every x and bounded on C, with f≥1, then such a drift inequality holds for some everywhere finite V≥f.

  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: False

drinfeld-center-dual-category — Drinfeld center as the dual category of C⊠C^op [theorem]
  Let C be a finite multitensor category, regarded as a module category over C⊠C^op by (X⊠Y)⊗M=X⊗M⊗Y. The dual category Fun_{C⊠C^op}(C,C) of module endofunctors is canonically tensor equivalent to the Drinfeld center Z(C): a bimodule endofunctor −⊗Z corresponds to Z with the half-braiding given by its right module structure.

drinfeld-center — Drinfeld center of a monoidal category [definition]
  For a monoidal category C, its center Z(C) has objects (X,c), where c is a half-braiding on X, and morphisms f:X→X′ compatible with the half-braidings. Tensoring these pairs makes Z(C) braided; C itself need not be braided.

drinfeld-jimbo-quantum-group — Drinfeld–Jimbo quantum group U_q(𝔤) [construction]
  For the Cartan matrix (a_ij) of a reduced root system, with d_i=(α_i,α_i)/2 and q_i=q^(d_i), U_q(𝔤) is the associative algebra over the rational-function field ℚ(q) (or ℂ(q)) generated by E_i,F_i,K_i^(±1) with K_iK_j=K_jK_i, K_iK_i^(−1)=1, K_iE_jK_i^(−1)=q_i^(a_ij)E_j, K_iF_jK_i^(−1)=q_i^(−a_ij)F_j, E_iF_j−F_jE_i=δ_ij(K_i−K_i^(−1))/(q_i−q_i^(−1)), and the quantum Serre relations ∑_(r=0)^(1−a_ij)(−1)^r[1−a_ij choose r]_(q_i)E_i^(1−a_ij−r)E_jE_i^r=0 and likewise for F, for i≠j, with Gaussian binomials built from quantum integers. It is a Hopf algebra with Δ(K_i)=K_i⊗K_i, Δ(E_i)=E_i⊗K_i+1⊗E_i, Δ(F_i)=F_i⊗1+K_i^(−1)⊗F_i. It deforms the universal enveloping algebra of the corresponding semisimple Lie algebra; normalizations of q and of the coproduct vary between authors.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

  <- Rational function over a field [statement]: The ground field is the rational-function field ℚ(q) or ℂ(q).
  <- Quantum integer [statement]: Quantum Serre relations use Gaussian binomials built from quantum integers [n]_q.

drury-teardrop — Drury’s teardrop theorem [theorem]
  If w(T)≤1 and f∈A(𝔻) satisfies ∥f∥∞≤1, then W(f(T)) lies in the convex hull of the closed unit disk and the closed disk centered at f(0) with radius 1−|f(0)|². Consequently w(f(T))≤1+|f(0)|−|f(0)|²≤5/4.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

dual-abelian-variety — Dual abelian variety [construction]

dual-module-hopf-algebra — Dual of a module over a Hopf algebra [definition]
  For a finite-dimensional module V over a Hopf algebra H with antipode S, the dual space V*=Hom_k(V,k) is an H-module by (h·f)(v)=f(S(h)v), and evaluation V*⊗V→k is H-linear. For finite-dimensional modules U and W, the canonical isomorphism Hom_k(U,W)≅W⊗U* identifies H-module maps with H-invariant vectors of W⊗U*.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: False

newform-galois-representation-dual — Duality between the Galois representations of a newform and its conjugate [theorem]
  For a newform f of weight k with complex-conjugate newform f*, and a finite prime λ of the coefficient field, the λ-adic representation of f* is isomorphic to Hom(V_λ(f),F_λ)(1−k) as a G_ℚ-representation. Hence lattices T in V_λ(f)(r) have duals T*(1) that are lattices in V_λ(f*)(k−r).

nondegenerate-pairing-finite-dimensional-duality — Duality for a nondegenerate pairing with a finite-dimensional factor [theorem]
  Let b:V×W→F be a bilinear pairing of vector spaces over a field F such that only v=0 pairs to zero with all of W and only w=0 pairs to zero with all of V. If V is finite-dimensional, then w↦b(·,w) is an isomorphism of W onto the dual space of V, so dim W=dim V. Consequently, for a nondegenerate bilinear form on any vector space and a finite-dimensional subspace A, the vectors orthogonal to all of A^⊥ form exactly A.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: False
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: False
  Prerequisite frontier: elementary ingredients not expanded here.

  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

  <- Extension of bounded linear maps from dense subspaces [proof]: Two bounded functionals agreeing on the dense subspace of bounded functions agree on L¹ (uniqueness of the continuous extension).

dynkin-system-sets — Dynkin system (λ-system) of subsets [definition]
  A Dynkin system, or λ-system, on a set Ω is a family of subsets of Ω that contains Ω and is closed under complements in Ω and under countable unions of pairwise disjoint members. Equivalently, it contains Ω, contains B∖A whenever A⊆B are members, and contains the union of every increasing sequence of members.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Complement of a subset [statement]: Closure under complements in Ω, or under proper differences B∖A in the equivalent form.
  <- Disjoint sets [statement]: Closure is required only for unions of pairwise disjoint members.
  <- Union of a family of sets [statement]: Closure under countable disjoint unions, or increasing unions in the equivalent form.
  <- Sequence in a set [statement]: The countable disjoint unions and increasing unions are indexed by sequences of members.

khayutin-effective-bowen-separation-state-equidistribution — Effective equidistribution from average Bowen-ball separation [theorem]
  Let Γ be a lattice in a second-countable locally compact group G, Y=Γ∖G with Haar probability m, K compact, X=Y/K, and S(y)=ya⁻¹. Assume the Markov module property and0<λ=‖T‖_(L²₀(X))<1. For X-measurable0≤φ≤1 put u=μφ. In the lower-semicontinuous case put p=m(esssup_(b∈B₀)φ(·b)), η=(u−1+κ)/κ, q=θ+(1−θ)p; in the upper-semicontinuous case put p=m(essinf_(b∈B₀)φ(·b)), η=u/κ, q=(1−θ)p. If p,u∈(0,1),0<κ<μΩ, k≥1 and θ=λᵏ, with p≤η and θ≤(η−p)/(1−p) in the first case, or η≤p and θ≤(p−η)/p in the second, then C(μΩ−κ)²e^(−n(h−α))/4≤k e^(D(u‖p))e^(−nD(η‖q)/k).

ehrenfest-chain — Ehrenfest urn chain [definition]

  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

ehrling-lemma — Ehrling’s lemma [theorem]
  If X₀ embeds compactly into a Banach space X and X embeds continuously into X₁, then for every ε>0 there is C_ε with ‖v‖_X≤ε‖v‖_{X₀}+C_ε‖v‖_{X₁} for all v∈X₀.

  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Banach space [statement]: The three spaces X₀⊂X⊂X₁ are Banach spaces with their norms.
  <- Compact linear operator [both]: X₀ embeds compactly into X: the inclusion is a compact linear map. The proof extracts from the X₀-bounded normalized sequence a subsequence converging in X.
  <- Continuous linear embedding of normed spaces [both]: X embeds continuously into X₁ with ∥y∥_{X₁}≤Λ∥y∥_X; the proof uses this to pass X-convergence to X₁-convergence, and injectivity of the embedding to conclude the X-limit vanishes.
  <- Sequential characterization of compact metric spaces [proof]: Schikorra's sequential form of compact embedding (bounded sequences have convergent subsequences) is obtained from the catalogue's relatively-compact-image definition through sequential compactness of the compact closure of the image of the X₀-ball.

Elementary nilsequences are uniform limits of basic ones; by convention every almost periodic sequence is also elementary.

finite-dimensional-equivalence-of-norms — Equivalence of norms in finite dimensions [theorem]
  Any two norms on the same finite-dimensional real vector space bound one another by positive constant multiples. They therefore induce the same topology and the same notions of boundedness and convergence.

  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True

  <- Topology induced by a metric [both]: Same topology is compared through open balls; Theorem 2.1(⇐) shows constant-multiple bounds give the same open sets.
  <- Convergence of a sequence in a metric space [statement]: The statement asserts the same notion of convergence for the two norm metrics.

  <- Continuous map between topological spaces [proof]: Step 2 shows the given norm is (uniformly) continuous for the reference-norm topology.

  <- Minimum attainment for lower semicontinuous functions on compact sets [proof]: A continuous positive function on the compact unit sphere attains its minimum, giving a positive lower bound A.

ergodic-decomposition-compact-continuous-map — Ergodic decomposition for a continuous map of a compact metric space [theorem]
  For a continuous self-map T of a compact metric space, every invariant Borel probability μ is a mixture of ergodic invariant Borel probabilities: μ=∫ν dη(ν), with ∫f dμ=∫(∫f dν)dη(ν) for every bounded Borel f. The component law is unique modulo the usual almost-everywhere convention.

ergodic-decomposition-standard-borel — Ergodic decomposition on a standard Borel probability space [theorem]
  If T is a probability-preserving measurable self-map of a standard Borel space (X,B,μ), there is a probability kernel x↦μ_x with μ=∫μ_xdμ(x), and μ_x is T-invariant and ergodic for μ-almost every x. It can be chosen as a regular conditional distribution of the identity given the invariant σ-algebra I, so ∫f dμ_x=E_μ[f|I](x) almost surely for every bounded Borel f; the kernel is unique up to a common μ-null set.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True

euclidean-logarithmic-sobolev-inequality — Euclidean logarithmic Sobolev inequality with a parameter [theorem]
  For d≥1 there is C_d such that every real u∈H¹(ℝᵈ) with ‖u‖₂=1 satisfies ∫u²log(u²)dx≤ε∫|∇u|²dx+C_d−(d/2)logε for ε>0, with the usual0log0 convention.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- First-order Sobolev space W¹,ᵖ [both]: u ranges over H¹(ℝᵈ)=W^{1,2}(ℝᵈ) with weak gradient ∇u and L² norm; this is the form domain of −Δ in the proof.
  <- Gauss–Weierstrass heat kernel on Euclidean space [proof]: Example 2.1.3: the heat semigroup has kernel (4πt)^{−N/2}e^{−|x|²/4t}, so ‖e^{Δt}‖_{2→∞}=‖K_t‖₂=(8πt)^{−N/4}, i.e. M(t)=−(N/4)log(8πt).
  <- Logarithmic Sobolev inequality from ultracontractivity [proof]: Theorem 2.2.4 with M(t)=−(N/4)log(8πt) gives ∫f²log₊f≤εQ(f)+(c−(N/4)log ε)‖f‖₂²+‖f‖₂²log‖f‖₂; since log≤log₊ and f²log f²=2f²log f, rescaling ε gives the parameter form.
  <- Lipschitz composition in W¹,ᵖ [proof]: The theorem is applied to f=|u|≥0, which lies in H¹ with |∇|u||≤|∇u|, so Q(|u|)≤Q(u) for real u.
  <- Hölder’s inequality [proof]: ‖e^{Δt}f‖∞≤‖K_t‖₂‖f‖₂ by the Schwarz inequality, identifying the ultracontractivity bound.
  <- Gaussian integral on the real line [proof]: ‖K_t‖₂²=(8πt)^{−N/2} is a Gaussian integral.

euler-beta-gamma-integral-real — Euler beta–gamma integral for positive real parameters [theorem]
  For real a,b>0, Γ(a)Γ(b)=Γ(a+b)∫₀¹t^(a−1)(1−t)^(b−1)dt.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Gamma function on the positive real axis [both]: Both sides are gamma values and an improper integral with real powers (inherited through the gamma definition); the proof starts from the gamma integrals.
  <- Tonelli’s theorem for nonnegative functions [proof]: The product Γ(a)Γ(b) of two nonnegative integrals is rewritten as a double integral over (0,∞)² and later split again as an iterated integral.
  <- Change of variables theorem for Euclidean integrals [proof]: The C¹ diffeomorphism (s,t)↦(st,s(1−t)) of (0,∞)×(0,1) onto (0,∞)² with Jacobian s transforms the double integral.
  <- Agreement of Riemann and Lebesgue integrals [proof]: Γ and the beta integral are improper Riemann integrals; on compact subintervals they agree with Lebesgue integrals, which is needed to apply Tonelli and change of variables.
  <- Monotone convergence theorem for Lebesgue integrals [proof]: Exhausting (0,∞) or (0,1) by compact intervals identifies the nonnegative improper Riemann integrals with Lebesgue integrals.
  explains in wikipedia-beta-function-rev-1384863197, "Proof of the relation" — Iterated-integral proof with u=st, v=s(1−t). Learning reference, not an origin claim.

euler-characteristic-triangulated-space — Euler characteristic of a finite triangulated space [definition]
  For a finite simplicial complex K, χ(K)=∑_n(−1)ⁿs_n, where s_n is the number of n-simplices; in dimension two this is vertices − edges + triangles. A space homeomorphic to the geometric realization of K has Euler characteristic χ(K), independent of the chosen triangulation because it equals the alternating sum of the ranks of homology. For example, a closed disc has χ=1.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

  <- Integer [statement]: χ is an alternating integer sum.

  For every z∈ℂ, sin(πz)=πz∏_(n≥1)(1−z²/n²), where the products converge locally uniformly in z.

  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True

  <- Complex sine function [both]: The statement concerns sin(πz) for complex z; the proof applies factorization to the entire function sin(πz)/z.
  <- π [statement]: The statement evaluates sine at πz and has the factor πz.
  <- Infinite product of complex numbers or functions [statement]: The identity is an infinite product ∏_(n≥1)(1−z²/n²).
  <- Uniform convergence on compact subsets [statement]: The statement asserts locally uniform convergence of the product in z.
  <- Hadamard factorization theorem for entire functions of finite order [proof]: Corollary 8.9 (Hadamard factorization for order one) gives sin(πz)/z=e^(A+Bz)∏_(n≠0)(1−z/n)e^(z/n) with an absolutely convergent product.
  <- Entire function of finite order [proof]: The bound |sin(πz)/z|≤2e^(π|z|) for |z|≥1 shows the function has finite order (exactly one).
  <- Riemann’s removable singularity theorem [proof]: sin(πz)/z is extended across z=0 to an entire function with value π.
  <- Exact sequence of the complex exponential [proof]: The zeros of sin(πz) are exactly the integers, since e^(2πiz)=1 exactly for z∈ℤ.
  <- Order of vanishing of a holomorphic function [proof]: All zeros of sin(πz)/z are the nonzero integers and are simple, which fixes the multiplicities in the factorization.
  <- Nonvanishing of an absolutely convergent complex product [proof]: After pairing n and −n, local uniform convergence of ∏(1−z²/n²) follows from uniform convergence of ∑|z|²/n² on compact sets (Corollary 2.4 in the notes).
  <- Convergence criterion for a real p-series [proof]: The bound ∑_(n≥1)|z|²/n²≤R²∑n^(−2)<∞ on |z|≤R gives the uniform absolute convergence needed for local uniformity.

quadratic-exponential-gauss-evaluation — Evaluation of the complete quadratic Gauss sum [theorem]
  For a positive integer N, ∑_(a modN)exp(2πia²/N) is(1+i)√N if N≡0 mod4, √N if N≡1 mod4,0 if N≡2 mod4, and i√N if N≡3 mod4, with positive real square roots.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Complex exponential function [both]: The summands are exp(2πia²/N); the proof computes Fourier coefficients and Fresnel-type integrals of complex exponentials.
  <- π [statement]: The exponent is 2πia²/N.
  <- Congruence modulo an integer [statement]: The sum runs over residues a modulo N and the answer depends on N modulo 4.
  <- Nonnegative real square root [statement]: The values are multiples of the positive square root √N.
  <- Pointwise convergence of Fourier series of piecewise C¹ periodic functions [proof]: The periodized function φ(x)=∑_{−x≤n<N−x}e((x+n)²/N) is continuous and piecewise C¹, so its symmetric Fourier partial sums at 0 converge to the Gauss sum.
  <- Improper Riemann integral [proof]: The even and odd Fourier coefficients assemble into the conditionally convergent improper integral ∫_{−∞}^{∞}e(Ny²)dy.
  <- Integration by parts for C¹ real functions [proof]: Convergence of ∫e(Ny²)dy is proved by substituting t=y² and integrating by parts (applied to real and imaginary parts).
  <- Change of variables theorem for Euclidean integrals [proof]: The coefficients are rescaled by x=Ny and y=N^(−1/2)z, and convergence uses t=y².

complex-exponential-exact-sequence — Exact sequence of the complex exponential [theorem]
  The complex exponential is surjective C→C× with kernel2πiZ, giving0→2πiZ→C→C×→1. Coordinatewise this sequence respects conjugation and integer monomial actions.

  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True

  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

  <- Exact sequence of modules [statement]: 0→2πiℤ→ℂ→ℂ×→1 is an exact sequence of abelian groups (ℤ-modules), the last written multiplicatively.
  <- Multiplicative group of a field [statement]: The target is the multiplicative group ℂ× of nonzero complex numbers.

haar-existence-locally-compact-group — Existence and uniqueness of Haar measure on a locally compact group [theorem]
  Every locally compact Hausdorff group admits a left Haar measure, a nonzero left-invariant Radon measure (finite on compact sets, outer regular on Borel sets, inner regular on open sets), and any two left Haar measures differ by a positive constant factor.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Haar measure on a locally compact group [both]: The theorem asserts existence and uniqueness up to a positive constant of a left Haar measure; the proof constructs a nonzero, left-invariant, regular Borel measure finite on compacts.
  <- Tychonoff’s theorem [proof]: The approximate measures μ_U are points of X=∏_(K compact)[0,(K:K₀)], compact by Tychonoff.
  <- Finite-intersection characterization of compactness [proof]: The closed sets C(V)={μ_U:U⊆V} have the finite intersection property, so their intersection in the compact X is nonempty.
  <- Compact subsets of Hausdorff spaces are closed [proof]: Lemma 3.3 splits a compact set covered by two open sets into two compact pieces using that compact subsets of a Hausdorff space are closed; it gives countable subadditivity on open sets.
  <- Outer measure [proof]: The extension μ(A)=inf{μ(U):A⊆U open} is shown to be an outer measure.
  <- Carathéodory’s theorem on outer-measurable sets [proof]: Open sets are shown Carathéodory measurable, so the Carathéodory σ-algebra contains the Borel sets and μ restricts to a Borel measure.
  <- Urysohn lemma for locally compact Hausdorff spaces [proof]: Uniqueness fixes a nonnegative g∈C_c(G) that is not identically zero; its existence on a locally compact Hausdorff group is supplied by Urysohn’s lemma (used implicitly).
  <- Monotone convergence theorem for Lebesgue integrals [proof]: Lemma 4.5 extends left invariance of the integral from simple to nonnegative measurable functions by monotone convergence.
  <- Compactness of a finite product [proof]: K×Ū⁻¹ is compact as a product of two compact sets, used for continuity of x↦∫g(tx)dμ′(t).
  <- Continuous image of a compact space [proof]: KŪ⁻¹ is compact as the image of K×Ū⁻¹ under the continuous map (a,b)↦ab.
  <- Fubini theorem for compactly supported continuous functions on locally compact products [proof]: The iterated integrals of h(x,y)=f(x)g(yx)/∫g(tx)dμ′(t)∈C_c(G×G) against μ and μ′ are interchanged (Cohn’s generalization of Fubini, cited as [1] pp. 243–244).
  <- Uniqueness of Radon measures from continuous tests [proof]: Two Radon measures (Folland convention: finite on compacts, outer regular on Borel sets, inner regular on open sets) giving the same integral to every compactly supported continuous function coincide (Riesz representation, uniqueness part, cited from Cohn pp. 209–210); applied to μ and μ′/a, which are such measures by Gleason Definition 2.8.
  <- Closed subsets of compact spaces are compact [proof]: Lemma 3.3 (used in Step 10): L_i=K∖U_i and K_i=K∖V_i are closed subspaces of the compact set K, hence compact.
  <- Disjoint compact sets in a Hausdorff space have disjoint neighbourhoods [proof]: Disjoint compact sets are separated by disjoint open sets: L₁,L₂ in Lemma 3.3 and K₁,K₂ in Step 8 (additivity of μ on disjoint compacts).
  <- Monotonicity of the Lebesgue integral [proof]: Uniqueness Step 2 bounds ∫f dμ≥∫_V f dμ≥aμ(V)>0 and Step 4 bounds |I(x)−I(x₀)|≤δμ′(KŪ⁻¹) by monotonicity of the integral.
  <- Approximation of nonnegative measurable functions by simple functions [proof]: Lemma 4.5 Step 3 approximates a nonnegative measurable f by an increasing sequence of simple functions before applying monotone convergence.
  explains in gleason-haar-existence-uniqueness-reu-2010, Theorems 4.3 and 4.6, pp. 6–13 — Student exposition of the classical existence and uniqueness proof (covering numbers, Tychonoff, Carathéodory; Fubini and Riesz uniqueness). Not an origin claim.

rational-isogeny-character-exponent-restriction — Exponent restriction for a rational isogeny character [theorem]
  Let N>5 be prime, m=(N−1)/2 and t=m/num((N−1)/12). If E/ℚ has a rational cyclic N-isogeny and potentially good reduction at N, its kernel character has the form r=αχ_N^k, where α has order dividing2t and k modulo m is0,1,1/2,1/3 or2/3; the fraction1/2 occurs only when m is odd, and1/3,2/3 only when3∤m.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Isogeny character of a prime-degree elliptic isogeny [statement]: The statement concerns the character r giving the Galois action on the kernel of the rational cyclic N-isogeny.
  <- Potential reduction type of an elliptic curve over a local field [statement]: The hypothesis is potentially good reduction of E at N.
  <- Order of an element of a group [statement]: The conclusion bounds the order of the character α.
  <- Rational number [statement]: t is defined through the numerator of the rational number (N−1)/12.
  <- Global reciprocity map of idelic class field theory [proof]: Lemma 5.2: via class field theory, a continuous character of local units factors through U(ℚ_N), giving r=αχ^k with α unramified at N.
  <- Inertia subgroup of the absolute Galois group of a local field [proof]: All comparisons of r, χ and θ are made as characters of the inertia subgroup at N.
  <- Shimura covering of X₀(N) at prime level [proof]: Lemma 5.3 uses that X₂(N)→X₀(N) is cyclic of degree n and étale over ℤ[1/N] (Mazur 1977 II Cor. 2.3), producing K′/K with ramification indices dividing t.
  <- First nonabelian Galois cohomology set [proof]: The two N-isogenies over K′ are twists of one another by a 1-cocycle with values in Aut(C_N,E).
  <- Geometric automorphism group of an elliptic curve in characteristic zero [proof]: Lemma 5.1: Aut(C_N,E)={±1}, so the twist changes r only by a quadratic character.
  <- Absence of nontrivial everywhere finitely unramified extensions of the rationals [proof]: Over ℚ (class number one) the everywhere unramified character α^(2t) is trivial, so α has order dividing 2t.
  <- Néron model of an abelian variety [proof]: Over a finite extension L of K_N the Néron model of E is an abelian scheme, so E[N] is a finite flat group scheme over O_L.
  <- Inertia action under potentially good elliptic reduction [proof]: The good-reduction extension L may be taken with absolute ramification index e=2e₀, e₀∈{2,3}.
  <- Level-one fundamental character of tame inertia [proof]: On inertia χ=θ^e, so r=θ^a with a=2e₀k.
  <- Raynaud’s bound on inertia exponents of order-p group schemes [proof]: Applied to the order-N subgroup scheme of E[N]/O_L it gives 0≤⟨a⟩_(N−1)≤e, i.e. 0≤⟨e₀k⟩_m≤e₀, which yields k≡0,1,1/2,1/3,2/3 mod m.
  <- Atkin–Lehner involution on X₀(N) [proof]: In the boundary case one replaces x by w(x), changing k to 1−k.

ext-groups-abelian-category — Ext groups in an abelian category with enough injectives [construction]
  In an abelian category with enough injectives, Ext^q(A,B) is the q-th right derived functor of the left exact functor Hom(A,−), evaluated at B: choose an injective resolution B→I• and take H^q(Hom(A,I•)). Thus Ext⁰(A,B)=Hom(A,B), and Ext^q is a bifunctor, contravariant in A.

  <- Non-extreme scalar Schur function [both]: The criterion concerns radial boundary values and finite logarithmic integral on the probability-normalized circle.
  <- Lebesgue integral [both]: The criterion concerns radial boundary values and finite logarithmic integral on the probability-normalized circle.
  <- Natural logarithm [statement]: The criterion concerns radial boundary values and finite logarithmic integral on the probability-normalized circle.
  <- Outer function with prescribed boundary modulus [proof]: If the logarithm is integrable, form a nonzero outer g with boundary modulus1−|b*|. Then b±g are in the unit ball by the boundary norm formula, so b is non-extreme. Conversely write b=(b₁+b₂)/2 with distinct unit-ball functions and g=(b₁−b₂)/2. The scalar parallelogram identity gives |b*|²+|g*|²≤1. Logarithmic integrability of the nonzero H² function g implies integrability of log(1−|b*|²). This supplies an explicit proof of the criterion recalled inTheorem3.1(i)–(ii).
  <- Logarithmic boundary integrability of nonzero Hardy H² functions [proof]: If the logarithm is integrable, form a nonzero outer g with boundary modulus1−|b*|. Then b±g are in the unit ball by the boundary norm formula, so b is non-extreme. Conversely write b=(b₁+b₂)/2 with distinct unit-ball functions and g=(b₁−b₂)/2. The scalar parallelogram identity gives |b*|²+|g*|²≤1. Logarithmic integrability of the nonzero H² function g implies integrability of log(1−|b*|²). This supplies an explicit proof of the criterion recalled inTheorem3.1(i)–(ii).
  <- Boundary norm formula for Hardy H∞ [proof]: If the logarithm is integrable, form a nonzero outer g with boundary modulus1−|b*|. Then b±g are in the unit ball by the boundary norm formula, so b is non-extreme. Conversely write b=(b₁+b₂)/2 with distinct unit-ball functions and g=(b₁−b₂)/2. The scalar parallelogram identity gives |b*|²+|g*|²≤1. Logarithmic integrability of the nonzero H² function g implies integrability of log(1−|b*|²). This supplies an explicit proof of the criterion recalled inTheorem3.1(i)–(ii).

face-convex-polytope — Face of a convex polytope [definition]
  For a convex polytope Q, the convex hull of finitely many points of a real affine space, a face is Q itself or a nonempty subset Q∩{ℓ=c} where ℓ is an affine function with ℓ≤c on Q. Faces are polytopes; dim Γ is the dimension of the affine span of Γ, and codim Γ=dim Q−dim Γ. Vertices are the zero-dimensional faces.

  A field extension L/F is finite, [L:F]<∞, if and only if L is generated over F by finitely many elements algebraic over F. In particular every element of a finite extension is algebraic, and [F(α):F] is the degree of the minimal polynomial of an algebraic element α.

global-logarithmic-units-finite-z-l-module — Finite generation and compactness of global logarithmic units [theorem]
  For a number field K and prime ℓ, its global logarithmic unit group Ẽ_K is a finitely generated ℤ_ℓ-module. With its natural ℓ-adic module topology it is a compact Hausdorff group; field norm maps between these modules are continuous.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

  <- Finitely generated module over a commutative ring [statement]: Ẽ_K is asserted to be a finitely generated ℤ_ℓ-module.
  <- I-adic topology on a module [statement]: Its natural topology is the ℓ-adic module topology.
  <- Compact abelian topological group [statement]: Ẽ_K is asserted to be a compact Hausdorff abelian topological group.
  <- Logarithmic S-units containing the places above ℓ [proof]: With S the places above ℓ, Ẽ_K lies in ℤ_ℓ⊗E′_K, the ℓ-adified ℓ-units.
  <- Finite generation of the S-unit group [proof]: E′_K≅μ(K)×ℤ^r, so ℤ_ℓ⊗E′_K is a finitely generated ℤ_ℓ-module.

  For a conservative irreducible regular diffusion on an interval with interior generator½f″+qf′ and instantaneous reflection at any regular included endpoint, the speed density is2exp(2∫q). Entrance or inaccessible endpoints contribute no boundary holding atom.

  For every finite spin set Ω, ε>0 and integer k≥2, there is η>0 such that every probability law µ on Ωⁿ with sufficiently large n has disjoint events S₁,…,S_N, each of mass at least η and together of mass at least1−ε, for which the conditional joint law at k uniformly sampled coordinates has expected total variation distance less than ε from the product of its conditional one-coordinate marginals. The number N is at most1/η.

  <- Bapst–Coja-Oghlan regularity lemma for probability measures on discrete cubes [proof]: Apply the cube regularity theorem at a smaller δ. Its homogeneous state classes have small empirical-spin fluctuations. Lemma2.8 turns regularity plus small fluctuations into average k-coordinate independence: Markov bounds conditional marginal discrepancies on every event of mass above a small threshold, then conditioning sequentially on k spins and telescoping the joint/product difference bounds its expectation. The negligible small conditional events contribute at most their probability; repeated coordinate choices cost O(k²/n). Discard irregular state classes and those of mass below η=ε/(2N); their total mass is below ε. The remaining conditional laws satisfy the requested independence. This is an independently reusable consequence, distinct from the empirical-distribution statement of the regularity theorem.
  <- Markov’s inequality for nonnegative random variables [proof]: Apply the cube regularity theorem at a smaller δ. Its homogeneous state classes have small empirical-spin fluctuations. Lemma2.8 turns regularity plus small fluctuations into average k-coordinate independence: Markov bounds conditional marginal discrepancies on every event of mass above a small threshold, then conditioning sequentially on k spins and telescoping the joint/product difference bounds its expectation. The negligible small conditional events contribute at most their probability; repeated coordinate choices cost O(k²/n). Discard irregular state classes and those of mass below η=ε/(2N); their total mass is below ε. The remaining conditional laws satisfy the requested independence. This is an independently reusable consequence, distinct from the empirical-distribution statement of the regularity theorem.
  introduces in bapst-coja-oghlan-bethe-2015, corrected2015v3,Corollary2.2 and§2.4 — Captures the standalone approximate product-mixture consequence; not a new concept for each local ε,k-state notation.

configuration-jump-form-finite-volume-closability — Finite-volume reduction of closability for configuration-space jump forms [theorem]
  For an infinite-particle jump form E on local smooth functions in L²(μ), let E_r^n integrate, over configurations with exactly n points in the ball U_r, the energy of jumps of those n points and of jumps into U_r. If every E_r^n is closable on L²(μ), then E is closable. This is Esaki’s jump-form version of Osada’s Theorem 2 (1996) for diffusion forms.

nonconstant-projective-curve-morphism-finite — Finiteness of a nonconstant morphism of smooth projective curves [theorem]
  A nonconstant morphism between smooth projective geometrically integral curves over a field is finite and surjective.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Smooth projective algebraic curve [statement]: Source and target are smooth projective geometrically integral curves over a field; for smooth curves geometric connectedness and geometric integrality agree.
  <- Finite morphism of schemes [statement]: The conclusion is that the morphism of schemes is finite (and surjective).
  <- Projective schemes are proper [proof]: A nonconstant morphism from a projective curve has closed irreducible image of dimension one, hence is surjective onto the target curve.
  <- Proper morphism of schemes [proof]: Universal closedness of the proper source gives the closed image used for surjectivity.
  <- Finiteness of normalization in a finite field extension [proof]: The normalization C″ of C′ in the function field of C is finite over C′.
  <- Extension of rational maps from smooth curves [proof]: The birational maps between C and C″ extend to morphisms because both are regular projective curves (Curve-to-Projective Extension Theorem 15.3.1), so C≅C″.
  <- Rational function on a smooth projective curve [proof]: The argument identifies K(C) with K(C″) inside the function-field extension K(C)/K(C′).

first-isomorphism-theorem-groups — First isomorphism theorem for groups [theorem]
  For a group homomorphism φ:G→H, the kernel of φ is a normal subgroup of G and φ induces an isomorphism G/ker φ≅φ(G). In particular a surjective homomorphism with kernel N gives [G:N]=|H|.

first-resolvent-identity — First resolvent identity [theorem]
  For a closed linear operator A on a Banach space and z,z′ in its resolvent set, with R(z)=(A−z)⁻¹, R(z)−R(z′)=(z−z′)R(z)R(z′)=(z−z′)R(z′)R(z). Consequently the resolvent set is open and z↦R(z) is holomorphic there in operator norm.

first-quadrant-cohomological-spectral-sequence — First-quadrant cohomological spectral sequence [definition]
  A first-quadrant cohomological spectral sequence in an abelian category consists of objects E_r^(a,b) for r≥r₀ and integers a,b, zero unless a,b≥0, with differentials d_r:E_r^(a,b)→E_r^(a+r,b−r+1), d_r∘d_r=0, and isomorphisms E_(r+1)≅ker d_r/im d_r. For fixed (a,b) the terms stabilize to E_∞^(a,b). Convergence to objects H^n means each H^n has a finite descending filtration by subobjects whose graded pieces are E_∞^(a,n−a). Modules over a ring are the basic example.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

fischer-harmonic-polynomial-decomposition — Fischer decomposition of homogeneous polynomials [theorem]
  Every real homogeneous polynomial of degreeN inℝᵈ has a unique decomposition∑_{j=0}^{⌊N/2⌋}|x|^{2j}H_{N−2j}(x), where eachH_k is homogeneous and harmonic. ConsequentlydimH_k=binom(k+d−1,d−1)−binom(k+d−3,d−1), with a negative-degree term interpreted as zero.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Homogeneous real polynomial [both]: The statement decomposes homogeneous polynomials; the proof takes homogeneous parts of degree m.
  <- Harmonic function on an open Euclidean set [both]: The summands H_k are harmonic homogeneous polynomials; the proof uses harmonicity of Poisson integrals.
  <- Floor of a real number [statement]: The sum runs to j=⌊N/2⌋.
  <- Binomial coefficient [both]: The dimension formula; the proof counts monomials of degree m by choosing n−1 points.
  <- Dimension of a vector space [both]: The dimension of H_k; the proof computes dim P_m and subtracts.
  <- Poisson-integral solution of the Dirichlet problem for the ball [proof]: Theorem 5.1 writes P[p|S]=(1−|x|²)q+p by solving the Dirichlet problem with polynomial data; Corollary 5.3 compares degrees of the Poisson integral.
  <- Maximum principle for harmonic functions [proof]: Injectivity of q↦Δ((1−|x|²)q): a harmonic function vanishing on S vanishes on B; also uniqueness of the Dirichlet solution used without comment.
  <- Rank–nullity theorem [proof]: An injective linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space of polynomials of degree ≤m−2 is surjective.

finite-galois-fixed-field-characterization — Fixed-field characterization of finite Galois extensions [theorem]
  For a finite normal separable extension L/k, the group Gal(L/k) has order[L:k] and fixes exactly k. For every intermediate field M, the extension L/M is again finite normal separable, so L^(Gal(L/M))=M.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Finite Galois field extension [both]: Hypothesis L/k finite normal separable; the proof uses finiteness, normality and separability to exhibit L as generated by roots of a separable split polynomial.
  <- Fixed field of field automorphisms [both]: The statement concerns L^Gal(L/k), intermediate fields M and L^Gal(L/M).
  <- Dimension of a vector space [both]: The order of Gal(L/k) equals the degree [L:k].
  <- Degree bound on embeddings of a finite field extension [proof]: Proposition 3.2 (via Proposition 2.12): L generated by roots of f with distinct roots in L gives |Aut(L/F′)|=[L:F′] for F′=k and F′=L^Aut(L/k).
  <- Artin fixed-field degree theorem [proof]: (a)⇒(b) cites Corollary 3.5 to identify Aut(L/k) with Aut(L/F′) for F′=L^Aut(L/k).
  <- Tower law for degrees of field extensions [proof]: From [L:F′]=[L:k] with k⊆F′⊆L one concludes F′=k, i.e. [F′:k]=1.

serre-p-adic-fixed-weight-operations — Fixed-weight arithmetic and limits of Serre p-adic modular forms [theorem]
  For a prime p let X=ℤ_p×ℤ/(p−1)ℤ if p is odd and X=ℤ₂ if p=2. A nonzero Serre p-adic form has weight k∈X when its classical approximating weights converge to k, independently of the approximating sequence. Sums of forms of the same weight k have weight k when nonzero, products have the sum of weights, and a uniform p-adic limit of weight-k forms is again a weight-k form when nonzero.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Weight of a Serre p-adic modular form [statement]: The theorem is about forms of a fixed weight k∈X: sums of equal weight, products with added weights and limits of weight-k forms.
  <- Serre’s weight congruence for congruent modular forms [proof]: Theorem 2: since v_p(f_i−f_j)→∞ and v_p(f_i) is eventually constant, Theorem 1 makes the images of k_i in each X_m stationary, so the weight exists and is independent of the sequence.
  <- Inverse limit of groups [proof]: X is identified with the projective limit of the finite groups X_m=ℤ/(p−1)p^(m−1)ℤ, so eventual stationarity in each X_m is convergence in X.
  <- Von Staudt–Clausen theorem [proof]: Approximants of two forms of the same weight are brought to equal classical weights by multiplying with E_((p−1)p^m)≡1 mod p^(m+1) (Clausen–von Staudt, §1.1 d)), so their sums are classical approximants; products need no adjustment.
  <- Fourier expansion of normalized level-one Eisenstein series [proof]: The congruence for E_((p−1)p^m) is read off its q-expansion with the Bernoulli normalization.

formal-group-elliptic-curve — Formal group of a Weierstrass elliptic curve [construction]
  For a generalized Weierstrass equation y²+a₁xy+a₃y=x³+a₂x²+a₄x+a₆ with coefficients in a ring R, put z=−x/y and w=−1/y. Then w has a unique expansion w(z)=z³(1+A₁z+⋯)∈R[[z]], x=z/w(z) and y=−1/w(z), and the chord-and-tangent law gives the formal group law Ê(z₁,z₂)=z₁+z₂−a₁z₁z₂−⋯ over R. The invariant differential dx/(2y+a₁x+a₃) expands as (1+a₁z+⋯)dz. If R is the valuation ring of a nonarchimedean local field with maximal ideal 𝔪, these series converge on 𝔪, and Ê(𝔪) is the abelian group 𝔪 with x⊕y=Ê(x,y).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

Then chi_f=sInf { (chi_b:Real)/b | b>=1 }, equivalently use b+1 with b:Nat. This is the literal bare infimum definition, no fractional-coloring LP duality or attainment theorem asserted. elliptic-isogeny-function-field-galois — Function-field Galois theorem for an elliptic isogeny [theorem]
  For an isogeny φ:E→E′ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field k, the function-field extension k(E)/φ*k(E′) is Galois of degree degφ=|kerφ|. Its automorphisms are the translations by kerφ, so a rational function invariant under all such translations is h∘φ for a rational function h on E′.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Isogeny of elliptic curves in characteristic zero [statement]: The statement concerns an isogeny φ:E→E′ and its finite kernel.
  <- Characteristic of a field [statement]: The base field has characteristic zero, so every isogeny is separable.
  <- Rational function on a smooth projective curve [statement]: k(E) and k(E′) are the function fields of the curves; φ* is composition with φ and invariant functions are rational functions.
  <- Finite Galois field extension [statement]: The conclusion is that k(E)/φ*k(E′) is a finite Galois extension with automorphism group the translations by ker φ.
  <- Degree of a generically finite dominant morphism [statement]: deg φ is the degree [k(E):φ*k(E′)] of the function-field extension.
  <- Ramification and degree of a nonconstant map of smooth curves [proof]: Proposition II.2.6(a),(b),(c): fibres have deg_sφ points generically, ∑e_φ=deg φ, and e is multiplicative; with translations this gives #φ⁻¹(Q)=deg_sφ and equal ramification on each fibre, hence #ker φ=deg φ in characteristic zero.
  <- Artin fixed-field degree theorem [proof]: Translations τ_T (T∈ker φ, automorphisms because the group law is algebraic) fix φ*k(E′); the inspected proof bounds #Aut(k(E)/φ*k(E′))≤deg φ and concludes Galois from equality, which is Artin's fixed-field degree count for the finite group of translations.
  <- Fixed-field characterization of finite Galois extensions [proof]: Once the extension is Galois with group the translations, a function fixed by all translations lies in the fixed field φ*k(E′), i.e. is h∘φ.

entropy-rate-future-conditional-formula — Future conditional formula for finite-partition entropy rate [theorem]
  For a probability-preserving transformation T and finite partition ξ, h_μ(T,ξ)=H_μ(ξ|∨_(j≥1)T^(−j)ξ). This is the entropy rate for the ξ-name process; no generating-partition hypothesis is required.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy of a probability-preserving transformation [statement]: The left side is the entropy rate h_μ(T,ξ).
  <- Conditional information and entropy of a finite partition [statement]: The right side is the conditional entropy of ξ given a σ-algebra.
  <- Chain rule for finite-partition conditional information [proof]: Additivity splits H(ξ_0^{n-1}) as a sum of H(ξ|ξ_1^j) after invariance moves each term back by T^{-1}.
  <- Domination and convergence of finite-partition conditional information [proof]: H(ξ|ξ_1^j)→H(ξ|ξ_1^∞) by continuity of entropy in the increasing given σ-algebra.
  <- Cesàro convergence theorem [proof]: The normalized block entropy is a Cesàro average of a convergent sequence.

algebraic-torus-galois-character-equivalence — Galois-character classification of algebraic tori [theorem]
  For any field F, T↦X*(T)=Hom_(F_sep-groups)(T_(F_sep),G_m) is a contravariant equivalence between F-algebraic tori and finitely generated free abelian groups with a continuous action of Gal(F_sep/F), where the character lattice is discrete. A torus is split exactly when this Galois action is trivial.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Split algebraic torus [statement]: The statement concerns F-algebraic tori, morphisms of algebraic groups, and identifies split tori as those with trivial Galois action.
  <- Absolute Galois group [statement]: The character lattice carries an action of Gal(F_sep/F) with its Krull topology.
  <- Algebraic character of an affine algebraic group [statement]: X*(T) is the group of characters T_(F_sep)→G_m defined over F_sep.
  <- Discrete module for a topological group [statement]: The target category consists of lattices with continuous action for the discrete topology, i.e. discrete Galois modules and equivariant homomorphisms.
  <- Free abelian group [statement]: Character lattices of tori are free abelian groups.
  <- Finitely generated group [statement]: The lattices are finitely generated, i.e. of finite rank.
  <- Equivalence of categories [statement]: The theorem asserts an equivalence of categories.
  <- Opposite category [statement]: The equivalence is contravariant, i.e. an equivalence out of the opposite category.
  <- Character classification of diagonalizable algebraic groups [proof]: Over F_sep a split torus is D(M) for its free character lattice M, and Hom(M,M′)≅Hom(D(M′),D(M)); this is the split case of the equivalence.
  <- Galois descent for vector spaces along a Galois extension [proof]: The theorem over F follows from the F_sep statement by Galois descent of Hopf algebras with continuous semilinear Gal(F_sep/F)-action; the quasi-inverse has coordinate ring F_sep[M]^Γ.
  <- Separable-closure splitting of groups of multiplicative type [proof]: A torus split over an algebraic closure is already split over F_sep, so T_(F_sep)≅D(X*(T)) and descent from F_sep applies.
  <- Group algebra [proof]: The quasi-inverse D(M) is built from the group algebra F_sep[M] with its semilinear Galois action.
  explains in milne-algebraic-groups-2017, §12g Theorem 12.23 — Inspected proof of the classification, of which the torus case is the torsion-free part; not a priority claim.

gaussian-lipschitz-concentration — Gaussian concentration for a Lipschitz function [theorem]
  Ifg is a standard Gaussian vector andF is realL-Lipschitz in Euclidean norm, then P(F(g)≤EF(g)−t)≤exp(−t²/(2L²)) and P(F(g)≥EF(g)+t)≤exp(−t²/(2L²)) for t>0.

gelfand-mazur-banach-division-algebra — Gelfand–Mazur theorem [theorem]
  Every nonzero complex unital Banach algebra in which every nonzero element is invertible consists precisely of the scalar multiples of its identity, so the scalar map C→A, λ↦λ1, is an algebra isomorphism. It is isometric when ||1||=1.

  <- Homomorphism of algebras over a field [statement]: The conclusion is that λ↦λ1 from ℂ to A is a bijective unital algebra homomorphism over ℂ, an algebra isomorphism.
  <- Nonemptiness of the spectrum in a complex Banach algebra [proof]: Corollary 2.3.10: for each a there is λ with a−λ not invertible, by Proposition 2.3.9 (nonempty spectrum); in a division algebra this forces a=λ1.

gelfand-naimark-faithful-representation — Gelfand–Naimark representation theorem for C*-algebras [theorem]
  Every C*-algebra A admits a faithful star representation π:A→B(H) on a complex Hilbert space; π is then isometric, so A is isometrically star-isomorphic to a norm-closed star subalgebra of B(H).

  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True

  <- Injective function [statement]: Faithful means injective.
  <- C*-algebra structure of the minimal unitization [proof]: The proof first adjoins a unit if necessary and restricts back to A.
  <- Gelfand–Naimark–Segal representation theorem for a state [proof]: Each state gives a GNS cyclic representation with ⟨π_µ(a)ξ_µ,ξ_µ⟩=µ(a).
  <- Hilbert direct sum [proof]: The representation is the direct sum of the GNS representations over all states.
  <- States separate positive C*-algebra elements [proof]: For each a a state attains µ(a*a)=‖a‖², giving ‖π(a)‖≥‖a‖.

zonoid-measure-representation — Generating-measure representation theorem for symmetric zonoids [theorem]
  An origin-symmetric convex body is a zonoid exactly when it has a finite even positive generating measure on the unit sphere. That generating measure is unique.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Generating measure of an origin-symmetric zonoid [statement]: The representation has positive measure, unlike the signed representation for generalized zonoids.
  <- Weak compactness of bounded positive measures on a compact metric space [proof]: Finite symmetric sums of segments have the stated atomic even measures. The spherical average of their support functions is a fixed positive dimensional constant times the total mass, so Hausdorff convergence bounds the masses. Weak compactness gives a limiting measure; the uniformly Lipschitz integrands|u·v| turn weak convergence into uniform support-function convergence. Conversely approximate any finite positive even measure by atomic even measures to obtain zonotopes converging to the represented body. For uniqueness, zero cosine transform gives zero even harmonic coefficients by the nonzero even multipliers; polynomial approximation then annihilates every continuous even test function.

level-one-p-integral-modular-ring — Generators of the p-integral level-one modular ring [theorem]
  For p≥5, let ℤ_(p)={a/b∈ℚ:p∤b}. The graded ring of holomorphic level-one modular forms with rational p-integral Fourier coefficients is ℤ_(p)[E₄,E₆], with weights4,6. In particular each weight-k form has a unique weighted-homogeneous polynomial expression with p-integral coefficients.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Holomorphic Eisenstein series for SL₂(Z) [statement]: The named input specifies the objects in the statement or definition.
  <- p-integral rational number [statement]: The named input specifies the objects in the statement or definition.
  <- Polynomial ring over a commutative ring [statement]: The named input specifies the objects in the statement or definition.
  <- Modular form of integer weight on a congruence subgroup [statement]: The ring consists of holomorphic modular forms of level one, i.e. for the congruence subgroup SL₂(ℤ), with their Fourier expansions at the cusp.
  <- Nonnegative grading on a commutative ring [statement]: The modular forms form a graded ring by weight, with E₄,E₆ of weights 4,6.
  <- Level-one modular forms are polynomials in E₄ and E₆ [proof]: Serre starts from the complex structure theorem: every weight-k form is uniquely a combination of QᵃRᵇ, 4a+6b=k, with Q=E₄, R=E₆ algebraically independent; this also gives uniqueness of the p-integral expression.
  <- Ramanujan delta modular form [proof]: The induction on k uses that Δ=(Q³−R²)/1728 has p-integral coefficients in Q³,R² (1728=2⁶3³ is a p-adic unit for p≥5) and q-expansion q+⋯ with integer coefficients.
  <- Fourier expansion of normalized level-one Eisenstein series [proof]: E₄=1+240∑σ₃(n)qⁿ and E₆=1−504∑σ₅(n)qⁿ have integral coefficients and constant term 1, so p-integral c_(a,b) give p-integral forms and the leading coefficient can be peeled off.
  <- Dimension formula for level-one modular forms [proof]: The induction step writes f−a₀QᵃRᵇ as a cusp form Δ·g with g of weight k−12 (multiplication by Δ is an isomorphism M_(k−12)→S_k); g is p-integral because Δ=q(1+⋯) has integral coefficients. Details of this step compared with Milne MF Prop. 5.26 proof (same induction over ℤ).

kendall-atom-geometric-ergodic-theorem — Geometric ergodic theorem for a Kendall atom [theorem]
  Let an aperiodic ψ-irreducible Markov chain with invariant probability π have an accessible atom α (all states of α have the same transition law) that is f-Kendall of rate κ>1 for a measurable f≥1, i.e. E_α[∑_{k=0}^{τ_α−1}f(X_k)κ^k]<∞ with τ_α the first return time. Then the set S where U(x)=E_x[∑_{k=1}^{τ_α}f(X_k)κ^k] is finite is absorbing and full, and there are r>1 and R<∞ with ∑_n r^n‖P^n(x,·)−π‖_f≤R·U(x) for every x∈S. The proof uses Kendall's renewal theorem and the regenerative decomposition.

continuous-half-line-lyapunov-geometric-ergodicity — Geometric ergodicity from a half-line Lyapunov drift and positive transitions [theorem]
  Let a nonexplosive càdlàg weak Feller strong Markov family on[0,∞), with usual filtration, have positive transition probabilities to every Lebesgue-positive Borel set at every positive time. Suppose a continuous V≥1, k>0, b<∞ and compact C satisfy that V(X_t)−V(X₀)−∫₀ᵗ[−kV(X_s)+b1_C(X_s)]ds is a local supermartingale from every initial state. Then there is a unique invariant probability pi with pi(V)<∞ and constants D,rho>0 such that ‖P_t(x,·)−pi‖V≤D V(x)e^(−rho t) for every x,t. No equality rho=k or special explicit prefactor is asserted.

convex-gradient-conjugate-rate-approximation — Gradient approximation for a finite differentiable convex conjugate [theorem]
  Let Λ:ℝᵈ→ℝ be convex and differentiable and I=Λ*. Every x with I(x)<∞ has a sequence x_j∈∇Λ(ℝᵈ) with x_j→x and I(x_j)→I(x); for x_j=∇Λ(λ_j), I(x_j)=⟨λ_j,x_j⟩−Λ(λ_j), and x_j uniquely minimizes I(z)−⟨λ_j,z⟩.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Convex function on a convex subset of a real vector space [statement]: Λ is a convex function on the real vector space ℝᵈ.
  <- Gradient of a scalar function on Euclidean space [both]: The statement uses differentiability and the gradient image ∇Λ(ℝᵈ); the proof uses that directional derivatives of Λ at λ are ⟨θ,∇Λ(λ)⟩, forcing a maximizer of ⟨λ,z⟩−Λ*(z) to equal ∇Λ(λ).
  <- Fenchel conjugate of a real convex functional [both]: I=Λ* is the Fenchel conjugate; the proof manipulates its defining supremum.
  <- Real inner-product space [statement]: The formulas I(x_j)=⟨λ_j,x_j⟩−Λ(λ_j) and I(z)−⟨λ_j,z⟩ use the standard inner product on ℝᵈ, which also identifies ℝᵈ with its dual.
  <- Convergence of a sequence in a metric space [both]: The conclusion is x_j→x (and I(x_j)→I(x)); the proof obtains these limits from the Brøndsted–Rockafellar theorem.
  <- Subdifferential of a convex function on Euclidean space [proof]: The proof approximates x by points x_k of dom ∂Λ*, the points where the subdifferential of Λ* is nonempty.
  <- Brøndsted–Rockafellar theorem [proof]: Applied to Λ*: every x∈dom Λ* is a limit of x_k∈dom ∂Λ* with Λ*(x_k)→Λ*(x) (cited as Theorem D.4).
  <- Fenchel–Moreau biconjugation theorem [proof]: Λ=Λ** (Λ(λ)=sup_x[⟨λ,x⟩−Λ*(x)]), so λ∈∂Λ*(x) gives Λ(λ)=⟨λ,x⟩−Λ*(x), the stated identity, and identifies maximizers of ⟨λ,z⟩−Λ*(z).

  <- Monotone convergence theorem for Lebesgue integrals [proof]: Let p_n,q_n be the two marginal laws and ν_n=min(p_n,q_n) pointwise, ν_{−1}=0. Because ν_{n−1}P≤p_n,q_n, δ_n=ν_n−ν_{n−1}P is nonnegative. In each marginal chain independently define a killing rule that removes massδ_n at timen from its current unremoved state mass; the two rules have the same joint killing-time/location lawδ_n(x). Couple these time/location variables identically, sample the respective pre-killing paths conditional on them, and after killing use one common Markov future. On{T>n}, the marginal unremoved state masses are p_n−ν_n and q_n−ν_n, whose supports are disjoint, so the paths cannot have met. Thus T is their first meeting and coalescence time, withP(T>n)=1−∑_xν_n(x)=d_TV(p_n,q_n). Any residualT=∞ mass is coupled by its conditional path laws. This construction preserves each Markov marginal and need not be co-adapted.
