  Let F:B→C and G:A→B be left exact additive functors of abelian categories, with A and B having enough injectives. If G sends injectives to F-acyclic objects, then for each A∈A there is a convergent first-quadrant spectral sequence E₂^(p,q)=(R^pF)(R^qG)(A)⇒R^(p+q)(F∘G)(A).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True

  <- Cartan–Eilenberg resolution of a complex [proof]: The proof takes a Cartan–Eilenberg resolution of the complex G(I•) in B.

  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True

ghl-weak-drift-quasi-compactness — Guibourg–Hervé–Ledoux quasi-compactness theorem on weighted-supremum spaces [theorem]
  Let P be a Markov kernel and V≥1 a weight with PV/V bounded. Suppose the weak drift condition P^NV≤δ^NV+d holds for some N≥1, δ<1 and d<∞, and that some power P^ℓ maps the bounded measurable functions compactly into B_V. Then P is power-bounded and quasi-compact on B_V, and its essential spectral radius there is at most δ_V(P), the infimum of such δ.

gartner-ellis-finite-differentiable-cumulant — Gärtner–Ellis theorem with finite differentiable limiting cumulant [theorem]

semisimple-homogeneous-haar-entropy-formula — Haar entropy of a semisimple homogeneous translation [theorem]
  Let G be a finite product of groups of real or p-adic points of connected reductive characteristic-zero algebraic groups, Γ a lattice with Haar probability m, and a a semisimple element supported in a Q_p-factor. haar-measure — Haar measure on a locally compact group [definition]
  A nonzero Radon measure on a locally compact group, i.e. a Borel measure finite on compact sets, outer regular on Borel sets and inner regular on open sets, invariant under left translation: μ(gA)=μ(A). A right Haar measure is defined analogously with right translations.

Hence [IsHaarMeasure μ] [Regular μ] is exactly the revised paragraph for arbitrary (non-σ-compact) locally compact groups; the InnerRegular alternative named in the IsHaarMeasure docstring is the other convention and is not substituted. hadamard-factorization-theorem — Hadamard factorization theorem for entire functions of finite order [theorem]
  Let f be an entire function of finite order ρ with f(0)≠0 and zeros z₁,z₂,… counted with multiplicity, and let k be an integer with 0≤k≤ρ and ∑|z_n|^(−1−k)<∞. Then f(z)=e^(g(z))∏_n(1−z/z_n)exp(z/z_n+(z/z_n)²/2+⋯+(z/z_n)^k/k) for a polynomial g of degree at most ρ, the product converging absolutely and locally uniformly.

hairer-fbm-additive-sde-mixing — Hairer’s total-variation mixing theorem for additive fractional SDEs [theorem]
  Let dX_t=b(X_t)dt+dB_t^H onℝ with H∈(0,1),H≠½ and b∈C¹. Suppose (b(x)−b(y))(x−y)≤min(C−c|x−y|²,C|x−y|²), c>0, and |b(x)|+|b′(x)|≤C(1+|x|)^N. If H>½ also require b′ bounded. Then for each deterministic x the law of X_t^x converges in total variation to a common probability measure μ, the one-point marginal of the unique stationary solution adapted to the two-sided noise past.

  <- Mandelbrot–Van Ness representation of fractional Brownian motion [proof]: Use the two-sided Wiener representation and its fractional-integral inverse to track how a change of the noise past affects future increments. Dissipativity gives a Lyapunov moment bound and contracts the distance under common increments. On a bounded-distance, bounded-memory-cost set, add a feedback drift to make the trajectories coincide by time1; the inverse fractional transform has uniformly bounded Wiener L² control energy. Girsanov bounds the common mass of the shifted and original Wiener laws, permitting a positive-probability coupling attempt. Meeting is not by itself permanent, since the fractional noise remembers the differing past. The explicit kernel estimates in Lemma5.12 give continuation success probabilities on doubling intervals at least1−K2^{−αN}. Their infinite product is positive. After failure, wait long enough for the weighted memory cost to decrease, as Lemma5.15 proves; this permits another attempt with a uniform chance of permanent success. Section6 bounds the finite retry durations by a polynomially weighted geometric sum with power-tail increments; its tail tends to zero. Thus the probability that the two future trajectories differ tends to zero, and the coupling inequality gives total-variation convergence. Tightness/Lyapunov bounds yield a stationary law with the fixed Gaussian noise marginal. The ordinary H=½ case, excluded from this theorem’s paragraph, is covered separately; no future-dependent stationary solutions are asserted unique.

half-braiding — Half-braiding [definition]
  For an object X of a monoidal category C, a natural family of isomorphisms c_Y:X⊗Y→Y⊗X, compatible with tensor products and the unit: c_{Y⊗Z}=(id_Y⊗c_Z)∘(c_Y⊗id_Z), with associators inserted.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: formalized; estimated LOC: 205.5
    Evidence: Inspected committed mathlib snapshot 26573066084e6e2aa8526ea358bc43b66d96f970. HalfBraiding at Monoidal/Center.lean :53 stores β:∀U,X⊗U≅U⊗X, its tensor compatibility with inserted associators and naturality. The unit equation follows from those axioms (explicit proof checked in Tau); no extra assumption that the ambient category is braided is made. This is the same mathematical half-braiding convention. Source inspection of relevant declarations/proofs; no fresh Lean build or transitive axiom audit.
Search and boundary notes: Read actual field formulas, not just Center naming. Lack of an independent unit field is not a missing axiom: tensor/naturality force it; Tau Basic supplies that explicit consequence. Exclude arbitrary braidings on all object pairs as a different concept.

handelman-roy-closed-complementary-face-criterion — Handelman–Roy closed-complementary-face unperforation criterion [theorem]
  Let (G,u) be a dimension group, U a family of normalized traces, H=ker_G U and F=Z(H)⊂S(G,u), the traces vanishing on H. If F is a face whose complementary face is closed, then the quotient-ordered group G/H is unperforated; if G is simple, the quotient is a simple dimension group. Here complementary means the disjoint face giving the unique convex decomposition of each point between the two faces; the degenerate zero quotient is understood separately.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: False
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

  <- Face of a convex set [statement]: Immediate vocabulary in the precise contribution statement.
  <- Choquet simplex [statement]: Immediate vocabulary in the precise contribution statement.
  <- Simple partially ordered abelian group [statement]: Immediate vocabulary in the precise contribution statement.
  <- Quotient ordering of a partially ordered abelian group by a subgroup [statement]: The conclusion concerns G/H with the quotient ordering.
  <- Closure of a subset of a topological space [statement]: The hypothesis requires the complementary face to be closed in the weak topology of S(G,u).
  <- Affine-function splitting along closed complementary faces of a Choquet simplex [proof]: The proof uses the complementary face F′ and the ordered decomposition Aff S(G,u)=Aff F×Aff F′, with the projection π(a)=a|F′.
  <- Affine representation of an ordered group with order unit [proof]: J is the closure of the image of ker U under the affine representation; its annihilator is Z(ker U)=F.
  <- Convex subgroup of an ordered abelian group [proof]: Lemma 1.3, applied to π(J)⊂Aff F′, passes to the smallest convex subgroup c(L) containing L and the quotient by it.
  <- Existence of states on a partially ordered abelian group with order unit [proof]: Lemma 1.3 obtains a trace on G/c(L) from the existence of states [GH, 3.3], [G, Corollary 4.4]; this yields the trace contradicting J^⊥=F.
  <- Bezuglyi–Handelman sufficient condition for unperforated quotients of simple dimension groups [proof]: After J=P(J) the conclusions are taken from [BeH, Proposition B3]; its unperforation part is Corollary B.2(b) of arXiv v1.
  introduces in handelman-roy-diophantine-2015, Theorem1.2 and Corollary1.4 — The printed Z(U) in Theorem1.2 is interpreted as Z(ker_G U), explicitly clarified in the following Remark and proof. This is the infinite-dimensional closed-complement case omitted from the first contribution pass.
    Origin evidence: The introduction announces answers to earlier refinability/unperforation questions; immediately before Theorem1.2 the authors identify it as their first automatic unperforation result and supply its proof, contrasting the older [BeH,B2] condition.

one-sided-diophantine-approximation-criterion — Handelman–Roy criterion for one-sided linear Diophantine approximation [theorem]
  Let H⊂ℝⁿ be an additive subgroup containing no strictly positive vector,and F the smallest face of the standard simplex containing the nonnegative normalized linear functionals that vanish on H. Then for every h∈H,m≥1 and ε>0 there exists h′∈H with h−mh′>−ε coordinatewise iff for every f∈F,the subgroup f(H) is zero or dense inℝ.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

handelman-roy-refinable-trace-criterion — Handelman–Roy refinability criterion for finite-trace dimension groups [theorem]
  Let (G,u) be a simple dimension group whose normalized trace simplex K is finite-dimensional, and let τ be a trace. Put H=kerτ and Z={σ∈K:σ(H)=0}. Then τ is refinable exactly when G/H is unperforated, Z is a good subset of K, and the closure of the affine-evaluation image of H is the space of continuous affine functions on K vanishing on Z. In this situation τ is good exactly when it is refinable and Z={τ}.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True

  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

dimension-group-quotient-unperforation-criterion — Handelman–Roy unperforation criterion for finite-trace dimension groups [theorem]
  Let G be a simple noncyclic dimension group with finitely many pure traces,and H=ker_G Z(H) a subgroup with H∩G⁺={0},where Z(H) consists of normalized traces vanishing on H. If F is the smallest face containing Z(H),then G/H is unperforated iff f(H) is zero or dense inℝ for every f∈F.

hankel-moment-determinant-orthogonal-product — Hankel moment determinant and orthogonal-polynomial product [theorem]
  Letw be a possibly complex integrable weight onℝ with finite absolute moments throughdegree2n−2 and nonzero leadingprincipal Hankel determinants. Ifp_j(x)=κ_jx^j+⋯ satisfy∫p_jp_kw=δ_jk for0≤j,k<n, then det(∫x^(j+k)w(x)dx)_(j,k=0)^(n−1)=(1/n!)∫_(ℝⁿ)∏_(i<j)(x_i−x_j)²∏_iw(x_i)dx_i=∏_(j=0)^(n−1)κ_j⁻².
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

hardy-boundary-distance-lipschitz — Hardy inequality for boundary distance on a Lipschitz domain [theorem]
  For a bounded Lipschitz domain Ω there is C_Ω such that ∫_Ω|u(x)|²/dist(x,∂Ω)²dx≤C_Ω∫_Ω|∇u(x)|²dx for every u∈H₀¹(Ω).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Lipschitz domain in Euclidean space [both]: The inequality is asserted on bounded Lipschitz domains; the proof uses that such domains satisfy a uniform external ball condition.
  <- Sobolev space H₀¹ of a Euclidean domain [both]: The inequality holds for every u∈H₀¹(Ω), the form domain of the Dirichlet Laplacian, with C_c^∞ as form core.
  <- Distance from a point to a subset of a metric space [statement]: The weight is dist(x,∂Ω)⁻², the distance from x to the boundary.
  <- Boundary of a subset of a topological space [statement]: The distance is taken to the topological boundary ∂Ω.
  <- Hardy’s inequality on a bounded interval [proof]: Lemma 1.5.1 on each line segment in a coordinate direction gives ∫|f|²/(4d_u²)≤∫|∂_uf|² (Lemma 1.5.2).
  <- Area measure on the Euclidean unit sphere [proof]: Averaging Lemma 1.5.2 over directions with normalized surface measure on the unit sphere defines m(x) and gives ∫|∇f|²≥(N/4)∫|f|²/m².
  <- Fatou’s lemma [proof]: The inequality passes from C_c^∞ to the whole form domain by Fatou’s lemma.
  <- Uniform external ball condition for Lipschitz domains [proof]: Theorem 1.5.5 needs finite inradius (bounded Ω) and a uniform external ball condition; the text states that a uniform Lipschitz boundary condition implies it. The external balls subtend a fixed solid angle, giving m(x)≤C d(x).

  For every k≥2 and all sufficiently large fixed s, the number R_{s,k}(n) of ordered representations of n as s positive kth powers is asymptotic to Γ(1+1/k)^s·S_{s,k}(n)·n^(s/k−1)/Γ(s/k). The singular series is ∑_{q≥1}∑_{(a,q)=1}(q⁻¹∑_{r=1}^q exp(2πiar^k/q))^s exp(−2πian/q), and is bounded below by a positive constant uniformly in n when s is sufficiently large.

top-area-measure-hausdorff-description — Hausdorff-measure description of the top area measure of a convex body [theorem]
  For an n-dimensional convex body K⊂ℝⁿ, the area measure S_{n−1}(K,ω)=Θ_{n−1}(K,ℝⁿ×ω) given by the local Steiner formula equals the (n−1)-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the set of boundary points of K having an outer unit normal in ω. For bodies of dimension n−1 it is concentrated on the two unit normals of their affine hull, and it vanishes in lower dimensions.

  <- Interlacing and positive partial fractions [proof]: Induct simultaneously on vertex count that μ_G is real-rooted and μ_{G−u} weakly interlacesμ_G. WithH=G−u, deletion givesR=μ_G/μ_H=z−∑_{v∼u}w_uv μ_{H−v}/μ_H. Inductive interlacing and the positive-partial-fraction lemma express each quotient as∑c_j/(z−r_j),c_j≥0, after common-factor cancellation. ThusImR(z)>0 wheneverImz>0, soμ_G has no upper-half-plane zeros; real coefficients exclude lower-half-plane zeros. On the real line R′=1+∑wc_j/(x−r_j)²>0 between its poles, giving interlacing of the reduced numerator and denominator. Reinserting common factors preserves weak interlacing: a pole drops a denominator multiplicity by one, a regular shared root retains it, and a regular zero can raise it by one. Zero weights/residues are omitted. The empty and single-vertex bases are immediate.

hensel-coprime-factorization-complete-dvr — Hensel lifting of coprime polynomial factors [theorem]
  Let A be a complete discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal m. If a monic f∈A[X] has reduction f̄=ḡh̄ with ḡ,h̄ monic and coprime over A/m, then there are unique monic g,h∈A[X] of those degrees, reducing to ḡ,h̄, with f=gh.

  Present a complex semisimple Lie algebra as the Serre algebra 𝔤(R) of its root system, with Cartan subalgebra spanned by the h_i. For a 𝔤-module M and an integral weight λ (an integer combination of fundamental weights), the weight space is M_λ={m: h_i m=⟨λ,α_i∨⟩m for all i}. A highest-weight vector is a nonzero weight vector killed by every e_i, and a highest-weight module is generated by one. Every finite-dimensional module is the direct sum of its integral weight spaces; for each dominant integral λ there is a unique finite-dimensional simple module L(λ) of highest weight λ, and these exhaust the finite-dimensional simple modules.

  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True

  <- Heine–Borel theorem in finite-dimensional normed spaces [proof]: Finite-rank bounded operators are compact because bounded sets in finite-dimensional spaces are relatively compact (Example 7.3).

horospherical-maximal-entropy-principle — Horospherical maximal entropy principle [theorem]
  Let G be a finite product of groups of real or p-adic points of connected reductive characteristic-zero algebraic groups, Γ a lattice, and a∈G semisimple. Put U={u∈G:aⁿua⁻ⁿ→e}. For every probability μ on Γ∖G invariant under x↦xa⁻¹, h_μ(a)≤−log|det(Ad(a)|Lie U)|, with the product of normalized local absolute values; equality holds exactly when μ is U-invariant.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: False

host-kra-maass-cube-structure — Host–Kra–Maass cube characterization of inverse nilsystems [theorem]
  For a transitive compact metric system (X,T), with T a homeomorphism, and d≥2, let Q^[d](X) be the closure of all cubes (T^(ε·n)x)_(ε∈{0,1}^d). Then (X,T) is an inverse limit of minimal (d−1)-step nilsystems exactly when (x,y,…,y)∈Q^[d](X) implies x=y; equivalently any two cubes agreeing at all but one vertex agree at that vertex too.

holder-continuous-function — Hölder continuous function [definition]

i-adic-topology-module — I-adic topology on a module [definition]
  For an ideal I of a commutative ring R and an R-module M, the I-adic topology on M is the topology whose open sets are the unions of cosets m+IⁿM, with m∈M and n≥0, where IⁿM is the submodule generated by the products a₁⋯a_n·x with a_i∈I and x∈M. For a prime p and R=ℤ_p, the pℤ_p-adic topology is called the p-adic topology.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

  <- Topological space [statement]: The construction specifies a topology by declaring unions of basic cosets open.

  Let L be a nondegenerate quadratic ℤ-lattice of rank at least3, J the idele group ofℚ, and J_L={a∈J:a_v mod(ℚ_v×)²∈θ(SO(L_v)) at every place v}, with L_∞ its real quadratic space. Then the number of proper spinor genera in the genus of L is the finite index [J:ℚ×J_L].
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

  <- Index of a subgroup [statement]: The named input specifies the objects in the statement or definition.
  <- Orbit–stabilizer theorem for a group action [proof]: Proposition 9.4: the adelic rotation group acts transitively on the proper spinor genera in gen(L) and the stabilizer of spn+(L) is O+(V)O′_A(V)O+_A(L), so the number of proper spinor genera is the index of that stabilizer.
  <- Adelic points of an algebraic group [proof]: The proof works in the adelization O+_A(V) of the rotation group (restricted product with integral stabilizers at almost all primes), acting on lattices through their localizations.
  <- Local–global correspondence for lattices on a rational vector space [proof]: The action Σ(L)_p=Σ_p(L_p) is well defined because a lattice is determined by its localizations and families agreeing with L_p almost everywhere come from lattices; this gives gen(L)=O+_A(V)L.
  <- Normal subgroup [proof]: The kernel subgroup O′_A(V) is normal and contains the commutators, so O+(V)O′_A(V)O+_A(L) is a normal subgroup independent of the order of factors.
  <- First isomorphism theorem for groups [proof]: Theorem 9.8 is reduced to showing that θ_A:O+_A(V)→J/ℚ×J_L is surjective with kernel O+(V)O′_A(V)O+_A(L), which identifies the index of Proposition 9.4 with [J:ℚ×J_L].
  <- Spinor norms of a unimodular lattice at an odd prime [proof]: Lemma 9.6 and Corollary 9.7: since L_p is unimodular for almost all p, θ(Σ_p) is a unit square class for almost all p, so θ_A is well defined into the ideles; conversely unit components are realized by rotations of L_p.
  <- Surjectivity of the local spinor norm in dimension at least three [proof]: At the finitely many remaining primes the components of an idele are realized as spinor norms because dim V_q≥3 (Theorem 7.20 as cited; printed as Lemma 7.20).
  <- Spinor norm image of a rational rotation group [proof]: The kernel computation uses Proposition 9.9, the global image of the rational spinor norm, to adjust Σ by a rational rotation and an element of O+_A(L) until its spinor norm idele lies in J².

local-artin-conductor-induction — Induction formula for a local Artin conductor [theorem]
  For a finite separable extension L/K of nonarchimedean local fields of residue characteristic p and a finite-dimensional continuous ℓ-adic representation V of G_L, ℓ≠p, a_K(Ind_(G_L)^(G_K)V)=f_(L/K)a_L(V)+dim(V)v_K(𝔡_(L/K)), where f is the residue degree and 𝔡 is the local discriminant ideal.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: False
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Artin and Swan conductor of a local ℓ-adic representation [statement]: Both sides use Artin conductor exponents a_K and a_L of local ℓ-adic representations.
  <- Continuous induction from a subgroup of finite index [statement]: The left side is the conductor of the continuous induction Ind_(G_L)^(G_K)V from the open finite-index subgroup G_L.
  <- Absolute Galois group [statement]: G_L⊂G_K are absolute Galois groups of the local fields, with L/K finite separable.
  <- Residue degree of a finite extension of discretely valued fields [statement]: The coefficient f_(L/K) is the residue degree.
  <- Discriminant ideal of a finite local-field extension [statement]: The correction term is dim V·v_K(𝔡_(L/K)) for the local discriminant ideal.
  <- Mackey restriction formula for induced representations [proof]: Wiese restricts Ind_H^G V to the normal subgroup G^u by Mackey’s formula, giving a product of copies of V restricted to G^u∩H.
  <- Transitivity of the Herbrand function and lower numbering of subgroups [proof]: The proof computes G^u∩H=H^(ψ_(L/K)(u)) by passing to finite Galois M/L/K and using H_u=G_u∩H with ψ_(M/K)=ψ_(M/L)∘ψ_(L/K).
  <- Herbrand’s theorem on upper numbering of quotients [proof]: The index G/(G^uH)≅(G/H)/(G/H)^u uses compatibility of upper numbering with quotients.
  <- Hilbert’s formula for the different of a Galois local extension [proof]: Hilbert’s theorem on differents (Theorem 3.1.36, imported without proof) turns ∫(1/|(G/H)^v|−1)|… into v_L(𝔇).
  <- Discriminant as the norm of the different for local fields [proof]: Taking norms gives v_K(𝔡_(L/K))=f_(L/K)·v_L(𝔇_(L/K)), the form used in the final line.
  <- Valuation of a local field norm [proof]: The identity v_K∘N_(L/K)=f_(L/K)v_L is used to pass from the different to the discriminant.

injective-resolution-abelian-category — Injective resolution in an abelian category [definition]
  An injective resolution of an object A of an abelian category is a cochain complex I⁰→I¹→I²→⋯ of injective objects, zero in negative degrees, together with a morphism A→I⁰ such that 0→A→I⁰→I¹→⋯ is exact. Every object has one when the category has enough injectives.

  For a non-CM weight-two newform f with coefficient field F and a number field L, letΓ_L be the coefficient-field automorphismsσ with an inner-twist characterχ_σ trivial onG_L. Then dim_(Qℓ)End_(G_L)(V_ℓ(A_f))=[F:Q]·|Γ_L|.

  <- Monotonicity of the Lebesgue integral [proof]: Let v(t)=a+∫₀ᵗb(s)u(s)ds. Then u≤v and v′=bu≤bv almost everywhere. Fora=0 the same comparison or an a+ε approximation gives the conclusion.
  relies_on in flandoli-gess-scheutzow-order-2015, §3 proofLemma3.2 and Theorem3.3 — Also imports variational SPDE well-posedness[5,21,37], Aubin–Lions compactness, elliptic W²,p regularity, Sobolev embedding W²,p→C for2p>d, and deterministic porous-medium comparison[18]; precise theorem records/selected proofs remain required for completeness.

integral-group-ring — Integral group ring [definition]
  For a group G, the integral group ring Z[G] is the free abelian group on the elements of G, whose elements are finite sums Σn_g g with n_g∈Z, with multiplication extending the group law bilinearly. It is a ring with identity, commutative exactly when G is abelian. A G-module structure on an abelian group is the same as a left Z[G]-module structure, with the same homomorphisms.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

integral-scheme — Integral scheme [definition]
  A scheme X is integral if it is nonempty and O_X(U) is an integral domain for every nonempty affine open U; equivalently X is reduced (all local rings are reduced) and its underlying space is irreducible.

integral-symplectic-similitude-matrices — Integral symplectic similitude matrices [definition]
  The monoid GSp₂g⁺(ℤ) of integral 2g×2g matrices M with MᵗJM=μ(M)J for J=[[0,I_g],[−I_g,0]] and a positive integer μ(M), the multiplier. It contains Sp₂g(ℤ) as the elements of multiplier 1, is stable under multiplication by Sp₂g(ℤ) on both sides, and acts on ℍ_g by M⟨Z⟩=(AZ+B)(CZ+D)⁻¹ for M=[[A,B],[C,D]]; for example diag(1,…,1,p,…,p) has multiplier p.

lie-homomorphism-integration-simply-connected — Integration of a Lie algebra homomorphism [theorem]
  If G is a connected simply connected real Lie group and H is a real Lie group, every Lie algebra homomorphism Lie(G)→Lie(H) integrates to a unique smooth group homomorphism G→H. In particular connected simply connected Lie groups with isomorphic Lie algebras are isomorphic.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Simply connected topological space [statement]: The hypothesis is that G is connected and simply connected (simple connectivity includes path-connectedness).
  <- Differential of a Lie group homomorphism [statement]: 'Integrates to φ' means φ is a smooth group homomorphism G→H with φ_*=ψ.
  <- Lie subgroup–subalgebra correspondence [proof]: Proposition 8.13 applies Proposition 8.12 to the graph subalgebra Im(id,ψ)⊂Lie(G)⊕Lie(H) to obtain a connected Lie subgroup H′⊂G×H.
  <- Lie group homomorphisms with bijective differential are coverings [proof]: The projection p₁:H′→G has differential the identity of Lie(G), so it is a covering.
  <- Path lifting for a covering map [proof]: Since G is simply connected, the identity of G lifts through the covering p₁, so p₁ is an isomorphism and φ=p₂∘p₁⁻¹; this uses path and homotopy lifting for coverings (Etingof §2.5).
  <- Exponential coordinates on a real Lie group [proof]: Uniqueness (Proposition 5.17): φ(exp x)=exp(φ_*x) determines φ near the identity because exp is a diffeomorphism near 0.
  <- Connected topological groups are generated by identity neighbourhoods [proof]: Uniqueness: a neighbourhood of 1 generates the connected group G, so φ is determined by φ_*.

orthogonal-polynomial-zero-interlacing — Interlacing of consecutive orthogonal-polynomial zeros [theorem]
  For n≥1 let p₀,…,p_n be monic orthogonal polynomials with positive norms for a positive measure having at least n+1 support points and the required finite moments. The next polynomial p_{n+1}=(x−a_n)p_n−b_np_{n−1}, where a_n=∫xp_n²/‖p_n‖² and b_n=‖p_n‖²/‖p_{n−1}‖², has simple real zeros strictly interlacing those of p_n. If the measure has exactly n+1 distinct support points with positive masses, p_{n+1} is their monic vanishing polynomial, even though its measure norm is zero.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Sequence of orthogonal polynomials [statement]: The retained precise mathematical statement/definition uses these immediate inputs; proof inputs are separately classified.
  <- Interlacing of real-rooted polynomials [statement]: The retained precise mathematical statement/definition uses these immediate inputs; proof inputs are separately classified.
  <- Intermediate value theorem for real functions [proof]: Normalize the polynomials to be monic. Orthogonality shows xp_n=p_{n+1}+a_np_n+b_np_{n−1}: pairing with every lower-degree polynomial kills all other terms. Moreover b_n=‖p_n‖²/‖p_{n−1}‖²>0. Induct from the single zero ofp₁. At each zero ofp_n the recurrence gives p_{n+1}=−b_np_{n−1}, whose signs alternate by the induction hypothesis. The intermediate-value theorem supplies a zero in every intervening interval. The monic leading-term signs give one further zero beyond each extreme zero ofp_n. Degree counting accounts for exactlyn+1 distinct real zeros, proving strict interlacing. All denominator norms through p_n stay positive. For exactly n+1 support points, the constructed p_{n+1} is orthogonal to every degree≤n polynomial, so it vanishes at every support point and is their monic product; its own norm can be zero and is never divided by.

  <- Hardy inequality for boundary distance on a Lipschitz domain [proof]: Let φ be the normalized ground state, dμ=φ²dx, u=φf. Integration by parts using the ground-state equation gives E_Q(f,f)=E_D(u,u)−λ₁‖u‖²₂. The polynomial lower bound φ≥cρ^κ gives−logφ≤C+κ|logρ|, whereρ is boundary distance. For eachδ>0, |logρ|≤δρ⁻²+C−½logδ on the bounded domain, so Hardy bounds its integral againstu² byδC∫|∇u|²+C−C′logδ. Extend u∈H₀¹ by zero and apply the Euclidean parameter log-Sobolev inequality. Since the elliptic energy is comparable to∫|∇u|², choosingδ proportional toε yields the intrinsic log-Sobolev estimate Ent_μ(f²)≤εE_Q(f,f)+C₀+C₁|logε|. Davies–Simon’s criterion gives Q_t:L²→L∞. weakly-mixing-rds-invariant-random-measure-existence — Invariant random measure for a weakly mixing continuous random dynamical system [theorem]
  Let φ be a continuous random dynamical system on a Polish state space over a measure-preserving two-sided noise shift. If its one-point laws converge weakly to µ for µ-almost every initial point, then there is a random probability measure π measurable for the past generated by all solution maps ending no later than time0, with Eπ=µ and φ_t(ω)_*π_ω=π_{θ_tω} almost surely for each t≥0. Independent noise increments are not required.

inverse-limit-dynamical-systems — Inverse limit of topological dynamical systems [construction]
  For compact metric systems (X_i,T_i), i∈ℕ, and factor maps π_i:X_(i+1)→X_i, the inverse limit is the subspace {(x_i):π_i(x_(i+1))=x_i for all i} of the product ∏X_i with the map (x_i)↦(T_ix_i). A system is an inverse limit of systems of a class when it is conjugate to such a limit with all (X_i,T_i) in the class.

elliptic-isogeny-graph-number-field — Isogeny graph of a non-CM elliptic curve over a number field [construction]

abelian-isogeny-l-function-invariance — Isogeny invariance and product formula for abelian L-functions [theorem]
  Abelian varieties isogenous over a number field have identical Hasse–Weil L-functions, including bad local factors. The L-function of a product is the product of the two L-functions.

  <- Category of abelian varieties up to isogeny [proof]: An isogeny f:A→B of degree n has g:B→A with g∘f=n_A, so f is invertible in Hom⁰; applying the ℚ-linear Tate-module functor gives a G_K-isomorphism V_ℓA≅V_ℓB, hence equal inertia invariants and Frobenius polynomials at every finite v. For a product, V_ℓ(A×B)=V_ℓA⊕V_ℓB and determinants multiply.

elliptic-tate-image-index-isogeny-invariance — Isogeny invariance of an open elliptic Tate-image index [theorem]
  Let E and E′ be isogenous over a number field F and geometrically non-CM, and let p be prime. Their closed images in Aut(T_pE) and Aut(T_pE′) have the same finite index in their respective integral automorphism groups; the same holds for the indices of their determinant-one images in SL₂(ℤ_p).

ito-tanaka-formula-continuous-semimartingale — Itô–Tanaka formula for a continuous semimartingale [theorem]
  If X is a real continuous semimartingale and f:ℝ→ℝ is a difference of two convex functions, with left derivative f′₋ and second-derivative measure f″(da), then f(X_t)=f(X_0)+∫_0^t f′₋(X_s)dX_s+½∫_ℝ L^a_t f″(da), where L^a are the right local times of X. In particular f(X) is a continuous semimartingale.

jdlg-contraction-semigroup-minimal-group — Jacobs–de Leeuw–Glicksberg minimal group for Hilbert contractions [theorem]
  Let S be a nonempty weak-operator-closed semigroup of contractions on a Hilbert space. Then S is weakly compact and has a unique minimal idempotent Q, an orthogonal projection commuting with S. The minimal ideal QS=SQ is a compact topological group with identity Q, on which strong and weak operator topologies coincide.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

janson-zero-count-product-events — Janson’s zero-count inequality for increasing product events [theorem]
  Let A_i be finitely many increasing events, each determined by coordinates S_i in a finite Bernoulli product space. Put p_i=P(A_i),μ=∑p_i,Δ=∑_{i<j:S_i∩S_j≠∅}P(A_i∩A_j) and ε=max_i p_i<1. Then P(∩A_iᶜ)≤min{exp(−μ+Δ),exp(Δ/(1−ε))∏(1−p_i)}. An arbitrary dependency graph without the product-event hypotheses does not suffice.

  <- Harris’s inequality for Bernoulli product measures [proof]: Order the events. For A_i let B_i be the event that none of its preceding coordinate-disjoint events occur, and let Δ_i sum P(A_i∩A_j) over preceding coordinate-overlapping j. A_i is independent ofB_i. Since A_i∩A_j is increasing and B_i decreasing, Harris gives P(A_i∩A_j∩B_i)≤P(A_i∩A_j)P(B_i). Subtracting these overlaps gives P(A_i and no preceding events)≥(p_i−Δ_i)P(B_i). The probability of no preceding events is at mostP(B_i), so the conditional hazard is≥p_i−Δ_i whenever this is nonnegative, and trivially so otherwise. Thus each conditional avoidance probability is≤1−p_i+Δ_i. Multiplying, using1−x≤e^{−x}, yields exp(−μ+Δ). Alternatively factor1−p_i and bound1+Δ_i/(1−p_i)≤exp(Δ_i/(1−ε)); this gives the product form. A zero preceding-avoidance probability already proves the conclusion.

jentzsch-strictly-positive-compact-countable-kernel — Jentzsch theorem for a strictly positive compact countable kernel [theorem]
  Let q(x,y)>0 on a nonempty countable set, with its row action defining a compact positive operator Q on ℓ¹. Then r(Q)>0 is an eigenvalue with a strictly positive ℓ¹ eigenvector; that eigenvector is unique up to scaling among nonnegative eigenvectors, and no other eigenvalue has modulus r(Q).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Counting measure [statement]: ℓ¹(X) is L¹ for counting measure on the countable set X.
  <- Countable set [statement]: The state set X is a nonempty countable set.
  <- Kernel of an integral operator [statement]: Q is the operator of the kernel q acting on rows, (uQ)(x)=∑_y u(y)q(y,x).
  <- Compact linear operator [statement]: Q is assumed compact on ℓ¹.
  <- Operator norm of a bounded linear operator [statement]: Bounded operators on ℓ¹ form a Banach algebra under the operator norm, in which r(Q) is computed (after complexification).
  <- Spectral radius in a complex Banach algebra [statement]: r(Q) is the spectral radius of Q.
  <- Eigenvalue of a linear endomorphism [statement]: The conclusions concern eigenvalues and (strictly positive or nonnegative) eigenvectors of Q.
  <- Jentzsch theorem for irreducible kernel operators on Lᵖ [proof]: The theorem is the specialization of the Lᵖ Jentzsch theorem (Schaefer V.6.6, quoted as FS Theorem 6.2) to counting measure, p=1 and a strictly positive kernel, which is irreducible and makes every other eigenvalue strictly smaller in modulus.

jentzsch-irreducible-kernel-operator-lp — Jentzsch theorem for irreducible kernel operators on Lᵖ [theorem]
  Let (X,μ) be σ-finite, 1≤p≤∞, and Q a bounded operator on Lᵖ(μ) given by a measurable kernel q≥0. Suppose some power of Q is compact and q gives positive mass to (X∖Y)×Y whenever μ(Y)>0 and μ(X∖Y)>0. Then the spectral radius r(Q) is positive and a simple eigenvalue with an eigenvector positive μ-almost everywhere, and no other eigenvalue has a positive eigenvector. If q>0 almost everywhere, every other eigenvalue has modulus less than r(Q).

john-ellipsoid-theorem — John ellipsoid theorem [theorem]
  For every convex bodyK⊂ℝⁿ, an affine change of coordinates putsK between the unit Euclidean ball and then-fold dilate of that ball.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True

  <- Convex body in Euclidean space [both]: The defining data or statement explicitly presuppose convex-body-euclidean.
  <- Affine map between real vector spaces [both]: The defining data or statement explicitly presuppose affine-map.
  <- John ellipsoid of a convex body [proof]: The proof applies to the maximal-volume ellipsoid E⊂K and normalizes E=Bⁿ.
  <- John’s characterization of the maximal-volume inscribed ellipsoid [proof]: Contact points u_i with weights c_i satisfying ∑c_iu_i=0 and ∑c_i⟨x,u_i⟩²=|x|² (hence ∑c_i=n) give r≤n for every x∈K with |x|=r.
  <- Supporting hyperplane theorem [proof]: At a common boundary point u_i of Bⁿ⊂K, a supporting hyperplane of K also supports Bⁿ, so it is {⟨x,u_i⟩=1} and K⊂{⟨x,u_i⟩≤1}.
  <- Real inner-product space [proof]: The estimate expands ∑c_i(1−⟨x,u_i⟩)(r+⟨x,u_i⟩) with the Euclidean inner product.
  explains in schneider-convex-bodies-2014, Theorem 10.12.2, pp. 588–589 — Selected proof exposition (following Ball); attributes the consequence to John. Not an origin claim.

kato-critical-newform-selmer-finiteness — Kato critical-value Selmer finiteness for a weight-two newform [theorem]
  For a normalized weight-two newform f with L(f,1)≠0 and each finite prime λ of its coefficient field, the Bloch–Kato Selmer group of every G_ℚ-stable O_λ-lattice T in the Tate component V_(f,λ) is finite. In Kato’s normalization V_(f,λ) is the critical Tate twist V(f)(1) of his cohomological realization, up to replacing f by its complex-conjugate newform; the local condition above λ is the Bloch–Kato crystalline condition, not an unrestricted H¹ condition.

kodaira-parshin-point-cover-construction — Kodaira–Parshin covers associated to rational points [theorem]
  Let C/K be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus at least two over a number field. There exist a finite extension L/K, a finite set S of finite places of L, and a bound G, all independent of P∈C(K), such that each P has a smooth projective geometrically connected curve C_P/L of genus at most G, with good reduction outside S, and a finite nonconstant map C_P→C_L branched exactly over P.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Rational point of a scheme [statement]: The named input specifies the objects in the statement or definition.
  <- Genus of a smooth projective curve [statement]: The named input specifies the objects in the statement or definition.
  <- Good reduction of a smooth projective curve [statement]: The named input specifies the objects in the statement or definition.
  <- Finite morphism of schemes [statement]: The named input specifies the objects in the statement or definition.
  <- Ramification index of a finite extension of discretely valued fields [statement]: "Branched exactly over P" means that the ramification indices e_Q of the local function-field extensions at points Q over P are not all 1 there and all equal 1 elsewhere; e_Q is the ramification index of the valuations ord_Q over ord_(φ(Q)).
  <- Principal divisor on a smooth projective curve [statement]: The ramification index uses the normalized discrete valuations ord_Q of the function field at closed points of the curves, the valuations defining principal divisors.
  <- Multiplication by n on an abelian variety [proof]: Multiplication by 2 on J is an étale isogeny of degree 2^(2g); its pullback along C⊂J is an étale cover C′→C of degree 2^(2g).
  <- Good reduction of the Jacobian of a curve with good reduction [proof]: Over the S-integers the Jacobian of the smooth proper model is an abelian scheme into which the model embeds, so 2:J→J is étale over Spec R_S and C′ has good reduction outside S.
  <- Valuative criterion of properness over a discrete valuation ring [proof]: The K-point P of the proper smooth model extends to an R_S-point, needed to see that the points of φ⁻¹(P) are defined over fields unramified outside S.
  <- Hermite finiteness of extensions unramified outside a finite set [proof]: The fields of definition of the points over P have degree at most 2^(2g) and are unramified outside S, so one finite extension L₁ contains all of them for all P (Milne IV Theorem 3.1).
  <- Weak Mordell–Weil theorem for an abelian variety [proof]: Finiteness of J(L₁)/2J(L₁) gives a finite extension L₂ with J(L₁)⊂2J(L₂), so P₁−P₂ is twice a divisor class over L₂ (Proposition 5.5).
  <- Abel–Jacobi map on curve divisors [proof]: The relation [P₁−P₂]=2[D] in J(L₂) is translated into a linear equivalence of divisors P₁−P₂−2D=div(f).
  <- Hilbert class field of a number field [proof]: L₂ is replaced by its Hilbert class field L₃, a finite unramified extension independent of P.
  <- Principal ideal theorem for the Hilbert class field [proof]: In the Hilbert class field the needed ideals of S-integers become principal, so f can be rescaled by a constant to remove vertical components of its divisor (Lemma 5.3(b), Remark 5.4).
  <- Ring of S-integers of a number field [proof]: The integral models, the abelian scheme and the étale covers are taken over Spec R_S for the ring of S-integers.
  <- Equivalence between smooth projective curves and function fields of one variable [proof]: The square-root cover C_P is the smooth projective curve attached to the function field L₃(C′)[√f], finite over C′.
  <- Normalization of a discrete valuation ring in a finite separable extension [proof]: Locally C_P is the integral closure of the coordinate ring (a DVR at each point) in the quadratic extension, finite over it; ramification of K[√f] occurs exactly where ord(f) is odd (residue characteristic ≠2).
  <- Riemann–Hurwitz formula in characteristic zero [proof]: The Hurwitz formula for C_P→C′→C, of degree 2·2^(2g), bounds g(C_P) independently of P.

kummer-map-abelian-variety — Kummer map of an abelian variety [definition]
  For an abelian variety A over a characteristic-zero field K and n≥1, the connecting map of 0→A[n](K̄)→A(K̄)→A(K̄)→0 (multiplication by n) is the injective map A(K)/nA(K)→H¹(K,A[n](K̄)), sending P to the class of σ↦σ(Q)−Q for any Q with nQ=P. For K a finite extension of some ℚ_ℓ and a prime p, the maps for n=p^m pass to the limit and, after ⊗ℚ_p, give the local Kummer map κ:A(K)^∧⊗_(ℤ_p)ℚ_p→H¹(K,V_pA) in continuous cohomology, where A(K)^∧ is the p-adic completion.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Multiplication by n on an abelian variety [statement]: Surjectivity of multiplication by n on A(K̄) in characteristic zero makes 0→A[n]→A(K̄)→A(K̄)→0 exact, so a preimage Q of P exists.
  <- Prime-power torsion subgroup of an abelian group [statement]: The coefficients are the n-torsion A[n](K̄) and its p-power levels.
  <- Long exact sequence in cohomology of a short exact module sequence [statement]: The Kummer map is the connecting homomorphism of the long exact Galois cohomology sequence (4).
  <- Continuous cohomology of a profinite group with topological coefficients [statement]: The rational local Kummer map lands in continuous cohomology H¹(K,V_pA).
  <- Tate module of an abelian variety [statement]: Passing to the inverse limit over A[p^m] gives T_pA and V_pA.
  <- P-adic local field [statement]: The rational version is stated for K a finite extension of some ℚ_ℓ, where G_K satisfies the needed finiteness and A(K) is profinite.

kummer-regular-prime-criterion — Kummer’s Bernoulli criterion for a regular prime [theorem]
  For an odd prime p, p does not divide the class number of ℚ(ζ_p) if and only if p divides none of the numerators of B₂,B₄,…,B_(p−3), written in lowest terms. Such a prime is called regular.

  <- Kummer’s reduction of p | h(ℚ(ζ_p)) to the relative class number [proof]: (1E): p | h if and only if p | h⁻, which turns (2F) into the regularity criterion.
  <- Kummer’s power-sum criterion for the relative class number [proof]: (2A) is invoked: p | h⁻ iff p² divides some ∑j^(2k), 1≤k≤(p−3)/2.

g2-spider — Kuperberg's G₂ spider [definition]
  Kuperberg’s G₂ spider T(G₂) is the ℂ(q)-linear monoidal category whose objects are natural numbers and whose morphisms n→m are ℂ(q)-linear combinations of G₂ webs in a rectangle with n bottom and m top boundary points, modulo Kuperberg’s local relations: a loop equals q¹⁰+q⁸+q²+1+q⁻²+q⁻⁸+q⁻¹⁰, a monogon vanishes, and bigons, triangles, squares and pentagons reduce to webs with fewer vertices. Composition is vertical stacking, tensor product is juxtaposition, and Kuperberg’s crossing formula, a combination of four webs, makes it braided. Here q is Morrison’s parameter; Kuperberg’s parameter is q².
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

  For bounded smooth UFG fields and a generating bracket V_α of weighted length |α|, there is a Cameron–Martin-valued random control u_α(t,x) with D_{u_α}f(X_t^x)=(V_αf)(X_t^x), and sup_{x,0<t≤T}t^{|α|/2}‖u_α(t,x)‖_{D^{k,p}(H)}<∞ for every integer k≥0,p>1. This need not invert the full spatial covariance.

  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True

  <- Stratonovich integral for continuous semimartingales [statement]: X_t^x solves the Stratonovich equation X(t,x)=x+∑_i∫₀ᵗV_i(X(s,x))∘dB^i(s).
  <- Hilbert-valued Malliavin Sobolev space Dᵏ,ᵖ(K) [statement]: The estimate is in the H-valued Malliavin Sobolev norms D^{k,p}(H).
  <- Smooth stochastic flow for bounded smooth diffusion fields [proof]: X(t,·) is a C^∞ diffeomorphism flow with Jacobian J; pushforwards X(t)_* are used throughout §2.
  <- Stratonovich equation for pulled-back vector fields [proof]: The transport equation d(X(t)_*^{−1}W)=−∑X(t)_*^{−1}[W,V_i]∘dB^i (cf. Kusuoka–Stroock II) gives the linear system for a^β_α.
  <- Strong well-posedness of globally Lipschitz Brownian SDEs [proof]: The linear SDEs for a^β_α and b^β_α have unique solutions with uniform moment bounds; uniqueness identifies X(t)_*^{−1}V_[α]=∑a^β_αV_[β].
  <- Itô’s formula for Brownian diffusions [proof]: The Itô form of the a^β_α equation is converted to the Stratonovich form (2).
  <- Burkholder–Davis–Gundy inequalities [proof]: The remainder estimates (6) for r^β_α are moment bounds on iterated stochastic integrals.
  <- Malliavin smoothness of solutions of smooth SDEs [proof]: Formula (7) for X(t)_*^{−1}DX(t,x) and membership of f(X), a, b in K₀ are imported from Kusuoka–Stroock II.
  <- Malliavin derivative of an Itô integral [proof]: Lemma 7(1): Dg_i(h)=∫Df(h)dB^i+∫f h_i ds, so stochastic integrals of K_r processes lie in K_{r+1} or K_{r+2}.
  <- Kusuoka–Stroock nondegeneracy of iterated Stratonovich integrals [proof]: Theorem 10 (from Kusuoka–Stroock II) gives inverse moments for Gram integrals of iterated Stratonovich integrals; with Lemma 11 and Corollary 12 it yields Lemma 6, sup E det(M)^{−p}<∞.
  <- Markov’s inequality for nonnegative random variables [proof]: Lemma 11 and Corollary 12 bound small-ball probabilities by moment (Chebyshev) bounds.
  <- Adjugate identity and matrix inverse [proof]: M^{−1}=adj(M)/det M; with Lemma 6 this places M^{−1}_{αβ} in K₀ (Lemma 7(4)).
  <- Chain rule for the Malliavin derivative [proof]: Products and reciprocals of K_r functionals stay in the corresponding classes, giving K_r·K_s⊂K_{r+s} and M^{−1}∈K₀.
  <- Hölder’s inequality [proof]: D^{k,p} norms of products are bounded by Hölder across the factors.

laplace-method-varying-integrands-real — Laplace asymptotics for varying real integrands [theorem]
  Let ψ_n be positive on a fixed compact interval K with f_n=logψ_n and f_n,f_n″ converging uniformly there to f,f″. Suppose each f_n attains its maximum at an interior x_n, f has a unique interior maximum x₀ with f″(x₀)<0, the logarithmic supremum of |ψ_n| outside K is uniformly separated below f_n(x_n), and ∫|ψ_n| is uniformly bounded. Then ∫ψ_n(x)ⁿdx∼exp(nf_n(x_n))√(2π/(−nf″(x₀))).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
    Evidence: Mathlib 26573066084e6e2aa8526ea358bc43b66d96f970. The specified saddle-point asymptotic was not certified. Neither checked supplier establishes the required moving rescaling near a nondegenerate maximum together with the exponentially negligible-tail comparison. For varying integrands the uniform second-derivative/moving-maximizer and outside-K estimates are additional unresolved endpoints. These ingredients alone are not a proof of this theorem. laplace-transform-half-line — Laplace transform of a function on the half-line [construction]
  For a locally integrable f:[0,∞)→ℂ, its Laplace transform is g(z)=∫₀^∞f(t)e^(−zt)dt at those complex z for which the Lebesgue integral converges absolutely. If f is bounded the integral converges absolutely and locally uniformly on Re z>0, where g is holomorphic.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

  <- Lebesgue measure on Euclidean space [statement]: Local integrability on [0,∞) is with respect to Lebesgue measure.
  <- Complex exponential function [statement]: The kernel is e^(−zt).
  <- Holomorphic function of one complex variable [statement]: The paragraph records holomorphy of g on Re z>0.

laplace-beltrami-operator — Laplace–Beltrami operator on a Riemannian manifold [definition]
  On a Riemannian manifold (M,g) the nonnegative Laplace–Beltrami operator acts on smooth functions by Δf=−|g|^{−1/2}∑_{i,j}∂_i(|g|^{1/2}g^{ij}∂_jf) in local coordinates, with |g|=det(g_ij) and (g^{ij}) the inverse matrix. It is a second-order elliptic operator with ∫(Δf)h̄ dvol=∫∑g^{ij}∂_if ∂_jh̄ dvol for compactly supported f,h, where dvol=|g|^{1/2}dx.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Riemannian metric on a smooth manifold [statement]: Δ is built from the metric coefficients g_ij.
  <- Determinant of a square matrix [statement]: |g|=det(g_ij).
  <- General linear group over a commutative ring [statement]: (g^{ij}) is the inverse of the invertible matrix (g_ij).
  <- Real power of a positive real number [statement]: The factors |g|^{±1/2} are real powers of a positive function.
  <- Elliptic linear differential operator [statement]: Δ is a second-order elliptic operator, its principal symbol being ∑g^{ij}ξ_iξ_j.
  <- Smooth positive density on a smooth manifold [statement]: Integration by parts is with respect to the Riemannian volume dvol=|g|^{1/2}dx, a smooth positive density.

  <- Conditional Jensen inequality [proof]: Let M=E[X|G]. Conditional Jensen gives EM²≤EX². Pull-out and tower give E[XM]=E[M E[X|G]]=EM². Expanding E[(X−M)²] therefore gives EX²−EM². Add Var(M)=EM²−(EX)²; the result is Var(X). All products are integrable by their L² bounds.
  <- Pull-out property of conditional expectation [proof]: Let M=E[X|G]. Conditional Jensen gives EM²≤EX². Pull-out and tower give E[XM]=E[M E[X|G]]=EM². Expanding E[(X−M)²] therefore gives EX²−EM². Add Var(M)=EM²−(EX)²; the result is Var(X). All products are integrable by their L² bounds.
  <- Tower property of conditional expectation [proof]: Let M=E[X|G]. Conditional Jensen gives EM²≤EX². Pull-out and tower give E[XM]=E[M E[X|G]]=EM². Expanding E[(X−M)²] therefore gives EX²−EM². Add Var(M)=EM²−(EX)²; the result is Var(X). All products are integrable by their L² bounds.
  relies_on in bapst-coja-oghlan-bethe-2015, Notation,p.3;§2 proofs
  relies_on in irrgeher-leobacher-fast-orthogonal-2015, §1 effective-dimension discussion; §3 Theorem3.5 and following bound — Theorem3.5 is the ordinary conditional-variance decomposition, not a novel theorem identity. Effective dimension credited Caflisch–Morokoff–Owen[1]. Independence of regression residual and first component is an explicit extra hypothesis, not implied by zero covariance.

lebesgue-outer-measure-euclidean — Lebesgue outer measure on ℝⁿ [definition]
  For S⊆ℝⁿ, the Lebesgue outer measure m*(S)∈[0,∞] is the infimum of ∑_j V(R_j) over all sequences of open boxes R_j covering S, where V(R_j) is the product of the side lengths of R_j. A set S with m*(S)=0 is a Lebesgue-null set, or has measure zero.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Euclidean space ℝᵈ [statement]: Covers are by open boxes in ℝⁿ, whose volume is the product of side lengths.
  <- Sum of a nonnegative series [statement]: Each cover contributes the (possibly infinite) sum of a nonnegative series of box volumes.
  <- Greatest lower bound [statement]: The outer measure is the infimum, in [0,∞], of the cover sums.
  explains in lebl-basic-analysis-ii-2026, Definition 10.3.1, p. 108 — Textbook definition; not a priority claim.

  Let H be adapted càdlàg and X a càdlàg semimartingale. For deterministic partitions of mesh tending to0 on compact intervals, the left sums ∑H_(t_i)[X_(t_(i+1)∧t)−X_(t_i∧t)] converge ucp to ∫₀ᵗH_(s−)dX_s. For an adapted left-continuous locally bounded H the limit is ∫H_s dX_s.

  <- Uniform convergence in probability on compact time intervals [statement]: The Riemann sums converge ucp.
  <- Tagged Riemann sum [statement]: Left-endpoint sums over partitions whose mesh tends to zero.
  <- Fundamental theorem of local martingales [proof]: The proof decomposes X=X_0+M+V with M a local L²-martingale (Corollary 3.22 of the fundamental theorem) and V of finite variation.
  <- Lebesgue–Stieltjes integral for a càdlàg path of locally bounded variation [proof]: For the finite-variation part, Lemma 1.12 shows pathwise uniform convergence of left Riemann–Stieltjes sums to ∫X(s−)dV.

left-module-over-ring — Left module over a ring [definition]
  For a ring R with identity, a left R-module is an abelian group M with a map R×M→M satisfying r(m+n)=rm+rn, (r+s)m=rm+sm, (rs)m=r(sm) and 1m=m. An R-linear map is an additive map f with f(rm)=rf(m); a submodule is an additive subgroup closed under the action; Hom_R(M,N) is the abelian group of R-linear maps M→N.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

  <- Group homomorphism [statement]: R-linear maps are additive homomorphisms commuting with the action; Hom_R is a group of such maps.

lehrer-zhang-infinitesimal-braid-generation — Lehrer–Zhang Casimir generation theorem for strongly multiplicity-free modules [theorem]
  If V is a strongly multiplicity-free module of a complex simple Lie algebra 𝔤, then for every r≥2 the commutant End_𝔤(V^⊗r) is generated by the operators through which the two-factor components C_ij of the quadratic Casimir act on V^⊗r, so it is a quotient of Kohno’s infinitesimal braid algebra. The same generation holds for End_G(V^⊗r) for the natural modules of SL_k(ℂ), O_k(ℂ) (including even k) and Sp_2k(ℂ), the symmetric powers of ℂ² for SL₂(ℂ), and the seven-dimensional G₂-module.

baker-campbell-hausdorff-local-lie-group — Local Baker–Campbell–Hausdorff formula [theorem]
  In a finite-dimensional real Lie group, for sufficiently small X,Y in its Lie algebra one has exp(X)exp(Y)=exp(BCH(X,Y)), where BCH is a convergent universal series of iterated Lie brackets beginning X+Y+[X,Y]/2. If the Lie algebra is nilpotent, the series terminates as a polynomial.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Exponential map of a real Lie group [statement]: The formula exp(X)exp(Y)=exp(BCH(X,Y)) is stated with the exponential map of the Lie group (its Lie algebra and bracket come with it).
  <- Nilpotent Lie algebra [statement]: The final clause concerns nilpotent Lie algebras, for which all sufficiently long iterated brackets vanish and the series is a polynomial.
  <- Convergent real series [statement]: BCH(X,Y) is a convergent infinite series; convergence of partial sums is understood coordinatewise in the finite-dimensional Lie algebra.
  <- Rational number [statement]: The universal series has rational coefficients (1/2, 1/12, …) independent of the group.
  <- Exponential coordinates on a real Lie group [proof]: Tao works in exponential coordinates of the first kind: Proposition 1.2.21 identifies a neighbourhood of the identity with a radially homogeneous C^{1,1} local group in Lie(G), sx∗tx=(s+t)x.
  <- Adjoint representation of a real Lie group [proof]: Lemma 1.2.26 realizes conjugation y↦x∗y∗(−x) as a linear map Ad_x, multiplicative in x; the proof of Lemma 1.2.28 and Corollary 1.2.30 is carried out with these operators.
  <- Adjoint exponential formula for a Lie group [proof]: The Hadamard lemma Ad_x=exp(ad_x) with ad_x y=[x,y] is used to rewrite Ad_{−jx/n}=exp(−(j/n)ad_x) and to obtain (1−exp(−ad_x))/ad_x.
  <- Matrix logarithm near the identity [proof]: Lemma 1.2.28 and Corollary 1.2.30 use F(z)=z log z/(z−1) applied to the operators Ad_x Ad_{ty} near the identity, i.e. the logarithm power series in (z−1); Exercise 1.2.19 expands it.
  <- Matrix exponential [proof]: Operator exponentials exp(−t ad_x) of endomorphisms of the Lie algebra occur in (1.27) and its proof.
  <- Riemann integral of a continuous Banach-valued function [proof]: Both Lemma 1.2.28 and Corollary 1.2.30 pass from telescoping sums to vector-valued Riemann integrals ∫₀¹exp(−t ad_x)z dt and ∫₀¹F(Ad_xAd_{ty})y dt.
  <- Absolute convergence of a real series [proof]: Exercise 1.2.19 expands the integral formula into the series of iterated brackets and requires its absolute convergence for small x,y.

local-iwasawa-decomposition — Local Iwasawa decomposition [theorem]
  For a connected reductive group over R,C or a finite extension of Q_p and a parabolic P, some maximal compact K satisfies G(k)=P(k)K. If a compatible reductive integral model and parabolic model over O_k exist, K can be taken to be the hyperspecial subgroup 𝒢(O_k).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Complex number [statement]: The archimedean field ℂ is allowed.
  <- P-adic local field [statement]: The nonarchimedean fields are finite extensions of Q_p.
  <- Local-field topology on points of an affine algebraic group [statement]: Compactness in G(k) refers to its local-field topology.
  <- Maximal compact subgroup of a topological group [statement]: K is a maximal compact subgroup of G(k).
  <- Hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup [statement]: In the integral case K is the hyperspecial subgroup 𝒢(O_k).
  <- Parabolic subgroup scheme of a reductive group scheme [both]: The model of P is a parabolic subgroup scheme of 𝒢.
  <- Iwasawa decomposition of the real points of a reductive group [proof]: Archimedean case: G(F)=P(F)K for some maximal compact K, citing Knapp Proposition 7.31.
  <- Bruhat–Tits Iwasawa decomposition at a special point [proof]: Nonarchimedean case: the stabilizer of a special point gives G(F)=P₀(F)K, hence G(F)=P(F)K for P⊇P₀.
  <- Maximality of hyperspecial subgroups [proof]: 𝒢(O_F) is a maximal compact subgroup when the special fiber is reductive.
  <- Smooth projective scheme of parabolic subgroups of a reductive group scheme [proof]: G/P is a smooth projective O_F-scheme with G→G/P.
  <- Valuative criterion of properness over a discrete valuation ring [proof]: (G/P)(O_F)→(G/P)(F) is bijective.
  <- Rational conjugacy of geometrically conjugate parabolic subgroups [proof]: G(F)/P(F)≅(G/P)(F).
  <- Torsor under a group scheme [proof]: Fibers of G(O_F)→(G/P)(O_F) are 𝒫-torsors.
  <- Smoothness of torsors under smooth group schemes [proof]: A torsor under the smooth 𝒫 is smooth, so Hensel applies.
  <- Smooth Hensel lifting over a complete discrete valuation ring [proof]: Residue-field points of the smooth torsor lift to O_F-points.
  <- Lang–Steinberg theorem [proof]: Lang’s theorem gives a residue-field point of a torsor under the connected special fiber.

local-automorphic-unitary-coefficient-bound — Local automorphic unitary matrix-coefficient bound [theorem]
  For a connected simply connected absolutely almost simple Q-group, a noncompact factor G(Q_p), and a maximal strongly orthogonal positive-root system R, put r=2 in Q_p-rank1 and r=1 otherwise. A nontrivial irreducible unitary representation in the local automorphic dual has |⟨π(g)v,w⟩|≤C(dim⟨Uv⟩dim⟨Uw⟩)^(1/2)ξ_R(g)^(1/r)‖v‖‖w‖ for U-finite vectors, where ξ_R(g)=∏_(α∈R)Ξ_(PGL₂(Q_p))(diag(α(a_g),1)) and a_g is its Cartan torus component. The automorphic dual consists of irreducibles weakly contained in restrictions of the adelic automorphic regular representation; weak containment means compact-uniform approximation of diagonal coefficients by finite positive sums of such coefficients.

local-cohomology-support-exact-sequence — Local cohomology with support [theorem]
  For an ideal I in a Noetherian ring R, H_I^i(M) is the ith right derived functor of Γ_I(M)={m∈M:I^a m=0 for some a}. Short exact sequences of modules induce the natural long exact sequence of these groups; H_I^i(M)=0 below the I-depth of M.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Noetherian commutative ring [statement]: R is a Noetherian ring.
  <- Right derived functors from injective resolutions [statement]: H_I^i is the ith right derived functor of the left exact functor Γ_I.
  <- Enough injectives for modules over a ring [statement]: Derived functors of Γ_I on R-modules require injective resolutions of modules.
  <- Exact sequence of modules [statement]: Short exact sequences of modules induce the long exact sequence.
  <- Depth of a module with respect to an ideal [both]: Vanishing holds below the I-depth; the proof inducts on depth using a regular element f∈I with depth_I(M/fM)=depth_I(M)−1.
  <- Long exact sequence of right derived functors [proof]: The long exact sequence is the δ-functor property of R^iΓ_I, and the Ext long exact sequence for 0→M→M→M/fM→0 drives the induction.
  <- Ext groups in an abelian category with enough injectives [proof]: Vanishing is first shown for Ext^i_A(A/Iⁿ,M), i<depth.
  <- Local cohomology as a colimit of Ext groups [proof]: H_I^p(M)=colim Ext^p(A/Iⁿ,M) (Lemma 47.8.2) transfers the Ext vanishing to local cohomology.
  <- Finiteness of depth over a Noetherian ring [proof]: Induction on depth_I(M) is allowed because the depth is finite (Algebra, Lemma 10.72.4).

elliptic-fundamental-solution-local — Local fundamental solution for an elliptic operator [theorem]
  An elliptic differential operator has a distributional local fundamental solution at a point: applying the operator to the solution gives the Dirac distribution there. Sufficiently high elliptic powers have fundamental solutions with arbitrarily prescribed finite differentiability also at the source, while elliptic regularity gives smoothness away from it.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: False

  <- Malcev rational lattice basis theorem [proof]: The proof chooses a basis of G whose continuous generators lie in Γ and whose discrete generators have a fixed power in Γ (§§2.5–2.7, via a Malcev basis of the simply connected cover), so each G_i/G_(i+1) is covered by a compact cube modulo Γ_iG_(i+1).
  <- Continuous bijections from compact spaces to Hausdorff spaces are homeomorphisms [proof]: The continuous bijection G_i/Γ_i→(G_iΓ)/Γ from a compact space onto a Hausdorff subspace is a homeomorphism onto a closed subset, so G_iΓ is closed.
  <- Baire category theorem for complete metric spaces [proof]: G_i is closed in the locally compact group G_iΓ because Γ is countable: a countable union of translates of the closure of G_i cannot cover G_iΓ unless G_i is closed, a Baire category argument.

lusztig-divided-power-form — Lusztig’s divided-power integral form of a quantum group [construction]
  For the Drinfeld–Jimbo quantum group U_q(𝔤) over ℚ(q) and A=ℤ[q,q^(−1)], U_A^res is the A-subalgebra generated by K_i^(±1) and the divided powers E_i^((r))=E_i^r/[r]_(q_i)! and F_i^((r))=F_i^r/[r]_(q_i)! for r≥1. levy-brownian-martingale-characterization — Lévy characterization of Brownian motion [theorem]
  A continuous real local martingale starting at0 with quadratic variation t is Brownian motion relative to its filtration. The vector version requires bracket matrix tI.

  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

  <- Quadratic covariation of continuous semimartingales [both]: The hypothesis is [M]_t=t (bracket matrix tI in the vector case) for a continuous local martingale; the proof uses these brackets in the second-order Itô term.
  <- Quadratic covariation of Brownian coordinates [proof]: The direct implication of the selected equivalence uses that Brownian coordinates satisfy [B^i,B^j]_t=δ_ij t.
  <- Multidimensional time-dependent Itô formula for càdlàg semimartingales [proof]: Applied (in its complex form) to f(t,x)=exp(iθ·x+|θ|²t/2) to write Z_t=f(t,X_t) as 1+Σ_j iθ_j∫Z dX_j.
  <- Stochastic integral of a predictable process against a semimartingale [proof]: Z equals one plus stochastic integrals against the continuous local martingale X, hence is a local (L²) martingale.
  <- Local martingale with integrable running maximum is a martingale [proof]: Z is bounded on bounded time intervals, so the local martingale Z is a true martingale, giving E[Z_t|F_s]=Z_s.
  <- Uniqueness of finite-dimensional characteristic functions [proof]: Lemma B.18: the conditional characteristic function identity E[exp(iθ·(X_t−X_s))1_A]=exp(−|θ|²(t−s)/2)P(A) identifies the law of the increment under P(·|A), giving its Gaussian law and independence of F_s.
  <- Multivariate normal distribution [proof]: The identified increment law is the centered normal law with covariance (t−s)I, whose characteristic function appears in (6.24).

hardy-littlewood-major-minor-arcs — Major and minor arcs in the Hardy–Littlewood circle method [construction]
  In the circle method a representation count is written r(n)=∫_0^1 T(α)^s e(−nα)dα with an exponential sum T. For a size parameter P and small δ>0, the major arcs are the disjoint neighbourhoods 𝔐(q,a)={α mod 1:|α−a/q|≤P^(−k+δ)} of rationals a/q with 1≤a≤q≤P^δ and (a,q)=1; the minor arcs are the rest of ℝ/ℤ. On major arcs T is approximated by q⁻¹S(q,a)∫_0^P e(βξ^k)dξ, while minor arcs are bounded by Weyl and mean-value estimates.

  Prerequisite frontier: elementary ingredients not expanded here.

malcev-basis-adapted-filtration — Malcev basis of a nilmanifold adapted to a filtration [definition]
  For G/Γ with G connected simply connected nilpotent, Γ discrete cocompact and a filtration G_•, a basis X₁,…,X_m of the Lie algebra 𝔤 is a Malcev basis adapted to G_• if each span of X_(j+1),…,X_m is an ideal, each G_i is the exponential of the span of the last dim G_i vectors, every g∈G is uniquely exp(t₁X₁)⋯exp(t_mX_m), and Γ is exactly the set with all t_j∈ℤ. The Malcev coordinate map is ψ(g)=(t₁,…,t_m).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Compact nilmanifold [statement]: The basis is attached to a quotient G/Γ by a discrete cocompact subgroup.
  <- Filtration of a nilpotent Lie group [statement]: Condition (ii) adapts the basis to the filtration subgroups.
  <- Exponential map of a real Lie group [statement]: Coordinates are defined by products of exponentials exp(t_jX_j).
  <- Ideal of a Lie algebra [statement]: Condition (i) requires the tail spans to be ideals.
  <- Basis of a vector space [statement]: A Malcev basis is a vector-space basis of 𝔤.

malcev-coordinate-metric — Malcev coordinate metric on a nilmanifold [definition]
  For an ordered Malcev coordinate map ψ:G→R^m with Γ=ψ⁻¹(Z^m), the Malcev metric d_X on G is the largest metric bounded by ‖ψ(xy⁻¹)‖∞; equivalently take infima of sums of the symmetrized coordinate distances over finite chains. It is right invariant and induces the quotient metric d_X(xΓ,yΓ)=inf_(γ∈Γ)d_X(x,yγ) on G/Γ.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

malcev-coordinates-polynomial-sequence — Malcev coordinates of a filtered polynomial sequence [theorem]
  For a Malcev basis of G/Γ adapted to a filtration G_• with dimensions m_i=dim G_i, a sequence g:ℤ→G lies in poly(ℤ,G_•) exactly when ψ(g(n))=∑_j t_j C(n,j) with t_j∈ℝ^m and (t_j)_i=0 for i≤m−m_j. In particular poly(ℤ,G_•) is preserved by reparametrizations n↦a+bn with integers a,b.

malcev-fundamental-domain — Malcev fundamental domain of a nilmanifold [theorem]
  For a Malcev basis of G/Γ with coordinate map ψ, every g∈G factors uniquely as g={g}[g] with ψ({g})∈[0,1)^m and [g]∈Γ. Consequently, if the basis is Q-rational, G/Γ has diameter at most Q^C in the Malcev metric, with C depending only on the dimension and degree.

malcev-rational-lattice-basis-theorem — Malcev rational lattice basis theorem [theorem]
  A connected simply connected nilpotent Lie group G with lattice Γ has a Lie-algebra basis X₁,…,X_m adapted to the lower central series whose ordered exponential coordinates are global, take Γ exactly to Z^m, and have rational Lie bracket constants. A connected subgroup with Lie algebra spanned by rational combinations of the X_j has lattice H∩Γ and an adapted Malcev basis of rational combinations. With dimensions fixed and rational data of height at most Q, these combinations can be chosen with height bounded by Q^C, for a dimension-dependent C.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: False
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Q-rational Malcev basis [statement]: The theorem produces Malcev bases with rational structure constants.
  <- Rational subgroup relative to a Malcev basis [statement]: The subgroup clause concerns subgroups whose Lie algebras are spanned by rational combinations, with height bounds.
  <- Lattice in a locally compact group [statement]: Γ and H∩Γ are lattices.
  <- Polynomial group law in Malcev coordinates [proof]: Lemma A.8 (via Lemma A.2) turns a rational Malcev basis and rational recombinations into rational weak bases.
  <- Structure of discrete subgroups of a finite-dimensional real vector space [proof]: The quotient (span(Y_j,…,Y_m)∩Γ)/span(Y_(j+1),…,Y_m) is a discrete subgroup of a line, hence generated by one exp(c_jY_j).

malliavin-smooth-density-criterion — Malliavin criterion for a smooth density [theorem]
  If an ℝⁿ-valued Wiener functional F is Malliavin smooth and its Malliavin covariance Γ is invertible almost surely with E‖Γ⁻¹‖ᵖ<∞ for every p>1, then its law has a C∞ Lebesgue density.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Malliavin smooth Wiener functional [both]: The hypothesis is that X is Malliavin smooth; the proof uses that S is an algebra containing the entries of M⁻¹.
  <- Malliavin covariance matrix [both]: The hypothesis is almost sure invertibility of the Malliavin matrix with inverse moments of all orders; Y_i=∑_j(DX_j)M⁻¹_{ji}.
  <- Invertible square matrix [statement]: Invertibility of the Malliavin matrix and the norm of its inverse appear in the hypothesis.
  <- Expectation of an integrable real random variable [statement]: Inverse moments E‖M⁻¹‖ᵖ<∞ are expectations.
  <- Pushforward measure [statement]: The conclusion concerns the law of X, the image of the Wiener measure.
  <- Probability density relative to a measure [statement]: The law has a density with respect to Lebesgue measure.
  <- Skorokhod divergence on Wiener space [proof]: Integration by parts E⟨DG(X),ZY_i⟩=E(G(X)δ(ZY_i)) defines Z̄=δ(ZY_i).
  <- Skorokhod divergence preserves Malliavin smoothness [proof]: Z̄=δ(ZY_i) is Malliavin smooth by Corollary 5.25, allowing the induction over multi-indices.
  <- Chain rule for the Malliavin derivative [proof]: DG(X)=∑_j∂_jG(X)DX_j gives ∂_iG(X)=⟨DG(X),Y_i⟩, and Dᵏ of M⁻¹ is a polynomial in M⁻¹ and DˡX.
  <- Hölder’s inequality [proof]: Hölder and the Leibniz rule show that S is an algebra (Exercise 5.18), used to place Z·Y_i and M⁻¹_{ji} in S.
  <- Sobolev embedding of Hˢ(ℝᵈ) into bounded Cᵏ functions [proof]: Lemma 6.3: ‖G‖∞≲‖G‖_{Hˢ} for s>n/2 and Hˡ⊂C^r for ℓ>r+n/2 turn derivative bounds on the law into smoothness.
  <- Partial derivative of a distribution [proof]: Lemma 6.3 bounds every distributional derivative of the law μ in H^{−s}.
  <- Tempered distribution [proof]: The law is treated as a distribution belonging to Hˡ for every ℓ, through duality with Hˢ.
  explains in hairer-stochastic-analysis-2026, Theorem 6.7 with Lemmas 6.3, 6.8, pp. 53–55 — Exposition and proof; not a priority claim.

malliavin-smooth-wiener-functional — Malliavin smooth Wiener functional [definition]
  A Wiener functional is Malliavin smooth if it belongs to D^{k,p} for every integer k≥0 and every1<p<∞; here D^{k,p} is the completion of smooth cylindrical functionals in the Lᵖ norms of the functional and its first k Malliavin derivatives.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

malliavin-smoothness-sde-solutions — Malliavin smoothness of solutions of smooth SDEs [theorem]
  For an SDE with C_b^∞ coefficients driven by Brownian motion, the solution X_t^x, its spatial derivatives and solutions of associated linear SDEs belong to every D^{k,p}, with norms bounded uniformly in x and t∈[0,T]; moreover D_sX_t=J_tJ_s^{−1}σ(X_s)1_{s≤t}, with J the Jacobian of the flow.

mandelbrot-van-ness-fbm-representation — Mandelbrot–Van Ness representation of fractional Brownian motion [theorem]
  For H∈(0,1),H≠½, a two-sided standard fractional Brownian motion can be represented as B_t^H=c_H∫_ℝ[(t−s)_+^{H−½}−(−s)_+^{H−½}]dW_s, with c_H chosen for variance1 at time1. The difference kernel is square integrable; H=½ is ordinary Brownian motion.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Fractional Brownian motion [statement]: The theorem asserts that the displayed process is a (two-sided, continuous) fractional Brownian motion with Hurst index H.
  <- Wiener integral of a deterministic square-integrable function [both]: B_t^H is the Wiener integral of the difference kernel against a two-sided Brownian motion; the proof uses mean zero, joint Gaussianity and the isometry E[I(f)²]=∫f².
  <- Kolmogorov continuity criterion [proof]: Continuity of the represented process: Gaussian increments with E|X_t−X_s|^p=K_p|t−s|^{pH} give a continuous modification on each compact interval.
  explains in shevchenko-fbm-nutshell-2014, §4 Theorem 4.1 and proof, p. 6 — Proves the moving-average representation by computing the variogram; later exposition, not the origin (Mandelbrot–Van Ness 1968).

manin-constant-xzero-parametrization — Manin constant of an X₀ modular parametrization [definition]
  For E/Q of conductor N, let f be its normalized weight-two newform andπ:X₀(N)→E a modular parametrization. For a global minimal invariant differentialω_E, the nonzero rational number c(π) is defined byπ*ω_E=c(π)f(q)dq/q. Changing the sign ofω_E changes the sign ofc(π); its absolute value is the unsigned Manin constant.

manin-drinfeld-cuspidal-torsion — Manin–Drinfel’d theorem on cuspidal divisor classes [theorem]
  For a compact modular curve associated to a congruence subgroup, every degree-zero divisor supported on its cusps has torsion class in its Jacobian. In particular a modular parametrization sends the difference of two cusps to a torsion point on an elliptic curve.

branching-many-to-few-lemma — Many-to-few lemma for constant-rate branching Markov processes [theorem]
  Let Q_k be the multiple-spine law with unchanged motion, m_j=EAʲ, and let D_s(v) count marks on a skeleton particle v alive at s. Offspring moments through k are finite; repeated labels are included. Killed marks contribute zero. This is the unchanged-motion specialization of the full Harris–Roberts lemma.

matsushima-affineness-criterion — Matsushima’s affineness criterion [theorem]
  For a connected reductive group G over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field and a closed subgroup H, H is reductive exactly when it occurs as the stabilizer of a point in a finite-dimensional algebraic G-representation with closed orbit. Equivalently, the homogeneous quotient G/H is affine exactly when H is reductive. Consequently stabilizers of closed orbits in affine G-varieties are reductive.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

maximal-coupling-probability-measures — Maximal coupling of probability measures [theorem]
  For probabilities μ,ν on a standard Borel space, there is a joint law(X,Y) with marginalsμ,ν and P(X≠Y)=d_TV(μ,ν). Every coupling has P(X≠Y)≥d_TV(μ,ν).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Standard Borel measurable space [statement]: The theorem is stated for a standard Borel space, where the diagonal {X=Y} is measurable.
  <- Coupling of probability measures [both]: The theorem asserts the existence of a coupling with given marginals; the proof builds P̂ and checks its marginals.
  <- Total variation distance between probability measures [both]: The optimal disagreement probability equals d_TV(µ,ν); the proof computes d_TV=1−∫(g∧g′)dλ (den Hollander’s ‖·‖_tv is twice d_TV).
  <- Random element of a measurable space [statement]: The coupling is realized as a pair (X,Y) of random elements and P(X≠Y) is evaluated on their probability space.
  <- Radon–Nikodym theorem for finite measures [proof]: The densities g=dµ/dλ and g′=dν/dλ with λ=µ+ν exist by Radon–Nikodym.
  <- Pushforward measure [proof]: The diagonal part is Q̂=Q∘ψ⁻¹, the image of Q under ψ(x)=(x,x).
  <- Linearity of the Lebesgue integral [proof]: The identities ∫|g−g′|dλ=2(1−∫g∧g′dλ) and the marginal computations use linearity of the integral (Exercise 2.14 splits along {g≥g′}).
  <- Coupling inequality for total variation [proof]: The lower bound P(X≠Y)≥d_TV for every coupling is the coupling inequality.
  explains in den-hollander-coupling-lectures-2012, §2.5 Theorem 2.12 and proof, pp. 15–16 — Abstract construction of a maximal coupling via densities with respect to µ+ν; exposition, not the origin.
