maximal-ergodic-inequality-nonnegative — Maximal ergodic inequality for a nonnegative function [theorem]
  If T preserves probability μ, g≥0 belongs to L¹(μ), and r>0, then μ{sup_(n≥1)n⁻¹∑_(j=0)^(n−1)g(T^jx)>r}≤‖g‖₁/r.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Measure-preserving transformation [both]: The hypothesis is that T preserves μ; the proof uses invariance of integrals under composition with T (L¹-contractivity of the Koopman operator).
  <- Probability space [statement]: The preserved measure μ is a probability measure on the underlying σ-algebra; the measured event is a subset of that probability space.
  <- Lebesgue Lᵖ space [both]: The function g lies in L¹(μ) and the bound is ‖g‖₁/r; the proof works with integrable functions (S_k g−kλ)⁺ and their integrals.
  <- Composition of functions [statement]: The ergodic averages evaluate g at the iterates T^j x, the j-fold composites of T with itself.
  <- Koopman operator of a probability-preserving transformation [proof]: The selected Hopf–Garsia argument runs with the operator Uf=f∘T: it is positive, L¹-norm preserving and L∞-contractive (a positive Dunford–Schwartz operator), giving S_k g−kλ ≤ g−λ+U(M_nλ g)⁺ and ∫U(M_nλ g)⁺ ≤ ∫(M_nλ g)⁺.

  <- Monotonicity of the Lebesgue integral [proof]: Integrating pointwise inequalities: the maximal bound on {M_nλ g>0}, ∫_A U h ≤ ∫ U h for U h ≥ 0, and ∫_A g ≤ ‖g‖₁ for g ≥ 0 in Corollary 11.12 with p=1.
  <- Continuity of a measure along monotone sequences of sets [proof]: The finite-n bound μ{max_(k≤n) A_k g>r} ≤ ‖g‖₁/r passes to the supremum over all n because these events increase to {sup_n A_n g>r}.

scalar-parabolic-maximum-principle — Maximum principle for a scalar linear parabolic equation [theorem]
  A classical supersolution of w_t−∑a_ij(t,x)∂_ijw−∑b_i(t,x)∂_iw−c(t,x)w≥0 on a bounded smooth spatial domain stays nonnegative if its parabolic-boundary values are nonnegative, the symmetric matrix a is positive semidefinite, and the continuous coefficients are bounded on the time interval. An exponential time factor removes any positive upper bound on c.

maya-diagram-partition — Maya diagram and charge of a partition [definition]
  A Maya diagram is a subset X ofℤ+½ differing from the negative half-integers in finitely many places. Charge-zero diagrams correspond bijectively to partitions λ by X_λ={λ_j−j+½:j≥1}; every diagram is uniquely X_λ+m for an integer m, its charge.

mcdiarmid-bounded-differences — McDiarmid bounded differences inequality [theorem]
  For independent variablesX_i and an integrable realF whose value changes by at mostc_i when only coordinatei changes, P(F−EF≥t)≤exp(−2t²/∑c_i²) for t>0.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Independent family of random elements [both]: X₁,…,X_n are independent random elements of arbitrary measurable spaces; independence is used to compute the conditional increments by integrating out coordinates.
  <- Product σ-algebra [statement]: F=f(X₁,…,X_n) for f measurable on the product of the coordinate spaces, so the coordinatewise change condition makes sense.
  <- Expectation of an integrable real random variable [statement]: The bound concerns F−EF for integrable F.
  <- Real exponential function [both]: The tail bound is exp(−2t²/∑c_i²); the proof bounds exponential moments E e^(λ(F−EF)).
  <- Tower property of conditional expectation [proof]: Δ_k has conditional mean zero, and Lemma 3.7 iterates E[e^(λ∑_{i≤k}Δ_i)]=E[e^(λ∑_{i<k}Δ_i)E[e^(λΔ_k)|F_{k−1}]].
  <- Pull-out property of conditional expectation [proof]: Pulls the F_{k−1}-measurable factor e^(λ∑_{i<k}Δ_i) out of the conditional expectation in Lemma 3.7.
  <- Hoeffding’s lemma [proof]: Applied conditionally on F_{k−1} to Δ_k, which lies in an interval [A_k,B_k] of length ≤c_k, giving E[e^(λΔ_k)|F_{k−1}]≤e^(λ²c_k²/8) (Corollary 3.9).
  <- Joint law of independent random elements is the product law [proof]: Independence of X_k from the other coordinates gives the predictable bounds A_k,B_k by integrating f over the remaining coordinates with respect to product laws.
  <- Fubini’s theorem for integrable functions [proof]: Conditional expectations given X₁,…,X_k are integrals of f over the remaining coordinates against their product law.
  <- Markov’s inequality for nonnegative random variables [proof]: Chernoff step (Lemma 3.1): P(F−EF≥t)≤e^(−λt)E e^(λ(F−EF)), optimized at λ=4t/∑c_i².
  explains in van-handel-probability-high-dimension-2016, §3.2, Theorem 3.11 — Proof via Azuma–Hoeffding martingale method; inspected for cone-095.

mertens-strong-supermartingale-decomposition — Mertens decomposition of a class-D strong optional supermartingale [theorem]
  On a usual filtration, a class-D strong optional supermartingale X has a unique decomposition X=X₀+M−A−I, where M is a càdlàg uniformly integrable martingale, A is predictable càdlàg nondecreasing, and I is predictable left-continuous nondecreasing and purely discontinuous, all starting at0. Equivalently I=C_− for an adapted càdlàg purely discontinuous increasing C with C_(0−)=0.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True

  <- Usual conditions for a filtration [statement]: The filtration is usual.

  <- Làdlàg path [statement]: The process may have both left and right jumps.
  <- Predictable stochastic process [statement]: A and I are predictable.
  <- Continuous-time martingale [statement]: M is a martingale.

  <- Doob–Meyer decomposition of a càdlàg class-D supermartingale [proof]: Apply the càdlàg class-D decomposition to X+I; subtract I to obtain the Mertens form, and use uniqueness after recovering I from the right jumps of X.

mertens-right-jump-regularization — Mertens right-jump regularization of a strong supermartingale [theorem]
  For a real class-D strong optional supermartingale X on a usual filtration over [0,T], the sum I_t=∑_(0≤s<t)(X_s−X_(s+)) is a predictable left-continuous purely discontinuous nondecreasing process with I₀=0 and E I_T<∞, and X+I is a càdlàg class-D supermartingale. Right limits are only taken for s<T.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Usual conditions for a filtration [statement]: The filtration is assumed to satisfy the usual conditions (Mertens’s standing terminology from Meyer’s Probability and Potentials).
  <- Strong optional supermartingale [both]: X is a strong optional supermartingale (Mertens’s ‘surmartingale’, p. 50); its defining inequality at bounded stopping times is applied throughout the proof.
  <- Stochastic process of class D [both]: X is of class D on [0,T] and X+I is asserted to be of class D; the proof uses the uniform integrability of stopped values.
  <- Làdlàg path [statement]: I is defined from the right limits X_(s+) of the paths of X, which are làdlàg rather than càdlàg.
  <- Predictable stochastic process [statement]: The jump-sum process I is asserted to be predictable.
  <- Purely discontinuous nondecreasing function [statement]: I is asserted to be nondecreasing and purely discontinuous (Lemme b): I=∑λ_n 1_]T_n,∞[).
  <- Continuous-time supermartingale [statement]: X+I is asserted to be a (càdlàg) supermartingale, the input form of the classical Doob–Meyer theorem.
  <- Path regularity of strong optional supermartingales (Mertens) [proof]: Mertens’s Théorème 2 supplies the right limits X_(t+)≤X_t, finitely many right drops ≥1/k on bounded intervals (so the thresholds T_k^n increase to ∞), and right upper semicontinuity, which with the removal of all right drops gives right continuity of X+I.
  <- Debut theorem for a progressively measurable set [proof]: The successive threshold times T_1^n=inf{t>T_1^(n−1): X_t≥X_(t+)+1} (and their analogues at level 1/k) are debuts of progressive sets and hence stopping times under the usual conditions.
  <- Progressive measurability of adapted right- or left-continuous processes [proof]: The right-limit process X_+ is adapted (right-continuous filtration) and right-continuous, hence progressive, and optional X is progressive since its càdlàg adapted generators are; so the threshold sets {X≥X_++1/k} are progressive.
  <- Measurability of a progressive process at a stopping time [proof]: The jump sizes X_(T)−X_(T+) at the threshold stopping times are F_T-measurable (F_(T+)=F_T), so each A^n=(X_T−X_(T+))1_]T,∞[ is adapted.
  <- Predictable processes are optional [proof]: ‘A_1 étant continu à gauche, X+A_1 est bien mesurable’: the adapted left-continuous A_1 (and I) is optional, so X+A_1 and X+I are optional and only the supermartingale inequality needs checking.
  <- σ-algebra of a stopping time [proof]: The supermartingale inequality for X+A_1 is reduced to conditional expectations given F_S and F_(T_1^1), and the jump sizes are F_T-measurable.
  <- Tower property of conditional expectation [proof]: The reduction S_0=S, S_1=T_1^1∧T, S_2=T conditions successively on F_(S_0)⊆F_(S_1).
  <- Linearity and monotonicity of conditional expectation [proof]: The telescoping stopping-theorem estimate E[∑_(n≤k)(X_(T^n)−X_(T^n+))1(T^n<t)]≤E(X_0−X_t) and the induction over k combine conditional inequalities linearly and monotonically.
  <- Vitali convergence theorem for random variables [proof]: Mertens uses X_(T+)≥E(X_(T')|F_T) for stopping times T≤T' without separate proof; the selected justification passes to the limit in E[X_(T+1/m)1_A]≥E[X_(T')1_A] using a.s. convergence and the class-D uniform integrability.
  <- Fatou’s lemma [proof]: ‘Par le lemme de Fatou’: E A_1(t) is bounded by the limit of the expectations of the finite partial jump sums.
  <- Monotone convergence theorem for Lebesgue integrals [proof]: E(∑_(n≤k)A_n(t))≤E(X_0−X_t) passes to I=∑A_n, giving I_t<∞ a.s. and E I_T≤E(X_0−X_T)<∞ in the class-D finite-horizon case.
  <- Dominated convergence theorem for conditional expectations [proof]: ‘X+I est une surmartingale, par un passage à la limite élémentaire’: for bounded stopping times σ≤τ≤T the increasing partial sums ∑_(n≤k)A_n(τ) are dominated by the integrable I_T, so the conditional supermartingale inequalities pass to the limit.
  explains in mertens-1972-processus-stochastiques-generaux, Ch. I §2 Lemme a)–b) and proof, pp. 51–53 — Proves the regularization X'=X+I, I=∑_(s<t)(X_s−X_(s+)) predictable left-continuous increasing with I=∑λ_n1_]T_n,∞[, for a strong supermartingale with X_0∈L¹ on the half-line; the catalogue’s finite-horizon class-D form is a specialization. Originality not assessed.

  For a continuous map of a compact metric space, the entropy defined by finite open covers equals the supremum over ε>0 of limsup_(n→∞)n⁻¹log s_n(ε), where s_n(ε) is the maximal cardinality of an ε-separated set for d_n(x,y)=max_(0≤j<n)d(T^j x,T^j y).

  <- Limit superior of a real sequence [statement]: The metric side uses limsup_(n→∞)n⁻¹log s_n(ε).
  <- Lebesgue number lemma [proof]: A cover with Lebesgue number ε has Lebesgue number ε for every join 𝒰_0^{n−1} in the Bowen metric d_n, giving N(𝒰_0^{n−1})≤s_n(ε/2) via a maximal separated set.

  For a target probability π and proposal kernel Q, let r(x,y) be the Radon–Nikodym ratio of the reversed joint proposal law π(dy)Q(y,dx) to the forward law π(dx)Q(x,dy) on their mutually absolutely continuous part, and set r=0 on the forward-only singular part. minimal-polynomial-algebraic-integer — Minimal polynomial criterion for an algebraic integer [theorem]
  An algebraic number is integral overZ if and only if its monic minimal polynomial overQ has integer coefficients. In degree two this is equivalent to its field trace and norm being integers.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Algebraic integer [both]: The theorem characterizes algebraic integers; the proof starts from a monic integral equation for α.
  <- Minimal polynomial of an algebraic element [both]: The criterion is stated in terms of the monic minimal polynomial over ℚ; the proof uses that its roots are the conjugates of α.
  <- Rational number [statement]: The minimal polynomial is taken over the field ℚ.
  <- Trace in a finite field extension [statement]: The degree-two clause is phrased by the trace of α in ℚ(α)/ℚ.
  <- Norm in a finite field extension [statement]: The degree-two clause is phrased by the norm of α in ℚ(α)/ℚ.
  <- Isomorphism of stem fields of conjugate roots [proof]: Each root α′ of the minimal polynomial is the image of α under a ℚ-isomorphism ℚ[α]→ℚ[α′], so α′ satisfies the same monic integral equation.
  <- Fundamental theorem of algebra [proof]: The minimal polynomial of a complex algebraic number splits over ℂ, so its coefficients are elementary symmetric functions of its roots.
  <- Integral elements form a subring [proof]: The coefficients, polynomials in the integral conjugates, are integral over ℤ (Milne Theorem 2.1).
  <- Integrally closed integral domain [proof]: The rational coefficients integral over ℤ lie in ℤ because ℤ is integrally closed.
  <- Unique factorization domains are integrally closed [proof]: ℤ is integrally closed because it is a unique factorization domain (Milne Proposition 2.9, Example 2.10a).

Lower semicontinuity attains a negative minimum there. The super-mean inequality forces equality to that minimum on each sufficiently small circle around a minimum point: if a point on a circle were larger, lower semicontinuity would make its mean larger. Thus the minimum set is both open and closed in its component. A negative constant contradicts the boundary condition. The same argument proves the interior-minimum assertion.

  <- Cépa’s well-posedness theorem for multivalued Skorohod equations [proof]: On the open interval whereη is finite, its subgradient is locally bounded and equalsη′ except at a countable set. Since the Brownian part has quadratic variationt, the occupation-time formula makes that exceptional set irrelevant to the time drift. Thus the interior diffusion generator is½f″+(b−η′)f′. Its speed density is a constant multiple ofexp(2∫b−2η). Convexity boundsη below by an affine function, and b has bounded primitive on the bounded domain, so the speed measure has finite nonzero mass. Pathwise well-posedness gives a conservative solution; nondegenerate unit Brownian noise makes the interior regular and irreducible. The subgradient boundary correction is instantaneous normal reflection at a regular finite endpoint, or the singular potential makes the endpoint inaccessible; it cannot give absorbing or sticky holding with unit quadratic variation. The finite-speed-measure theorem gives the invariant density and total-variation convergence. This checks the exact one-dimensional application without claiming to have read the unavailable fullCépa–Jacquot primary proof.

  <- Finite speed measure and mixing of a one-dimensional diffusion [proof]: On the open interval whereη is finite, its subgradient is locally bounded and equalsη′ except at a countable set. Since the Brownian part has quadratic variationt, the occupation-time formula makes that exceptional set irrelevant to the time drift. Thus the interior diffusion generator is½f″+(b−η′)f′. Its speed density is a constant multiple ofexp(2∫b−2η). Convexity boundsη below by an affine function, and b has bounded primitive on the bounded domain, so the speed measure has finite nonzero mass. Pathwise well-posedness gives a conservative solution; nondegenerate unit Brownian noise makes the interior regular and irreducible. The subgradient boundary correction is instantaneous normal reflection at a regular finite endpoint, or the singular potential makes the endpoint inaccessible; it cannot give absorbing or sticky holding with unit quadratic variation. The finite-speed-measure theorem gives the invariant density and total-variation convergence. This checks the exact one-dimensional application without claiming to have read the unavailable fullCépa–Jacquot primary proof.

simple-gl2-type-modularity-theorem — Modularity of a simple GL₂-type abelian variety over ℚ [theorem]
  Every simple abelian variety A/ℚ with End⁰_ℚ(A) a number field of degree dim A is ℚ-isogenous to A_f for a normalized weight-two newform f. Its coefficient field is isomorphic to End⁰_ℚ(A).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Simple abelian variety of GL₂-type over ℚ [statement]: The hypothesis is that A is a simple GL₂-type abelian variety over ℚ.
  <- Modular abelian variety attached to a weight-two newform [statement]: The target is the modular abelian variety A_f.
  <- λ-adic representations of an abelian variety of GL₂-type [proof]: The proof uses the λ-adic representations ρ_λ of A and their reductions on A[λ].
  <- Faltings's isogeny theorem for abelian varieties over number fields [proof]: Faltings gives absolute irreducibility of almost all ρ̄_λ (Lemma 3.7) and Hom_ℚ(A_f,A)≠0 from mod-ℓ Galois homomorphisms for infinitely many ℓ.
  <- Serre's modularity conjecture (Khare–Wintenberger theorem) [proof]: Ribet's Theorem 4.4 assumes Serre's conjecture for the ρ̄_λ; the Khare–Wintenberger theorem removes this assumption.
  <- Conductor ideal of an abelian variety over a number field [proof]: Serre levels N_λ divide the conductor of A, independent of ℓ by Grothendieck, so they are bounded.
  <- Finite dimensionality of weight-two cusp forms [proof]: Bounded level and weight two leave finitely many newforms, so one f gives infinitely many ρ̄_λ.
  <- Chebotarev density of Frobenius conjugacy classes [proof]: Chebotarev identifies A_f[ℓ]⊗F_λ with A[λ]⊗F_λ from Frobenius traces.
  <- Isogeny decomposition of J₁(N) into modular abelian varieties [proof]: A simple quotient of J₁(N) is isogenous to some A_g since J₁(N) is isogenous to a product of A_g.
  <- Endomorphism algebra of the modular abelian variety of a newform [proof]: End⁰_ℚ(A_g) is the coefficient field, giving the final clause.

module-functor — Module functor between module categories [definition]
  For module categories M,N over a monoidal category C, a module functor is a functor F:M→N with natural isomorphisms F(X⊗M)≅X⊗F(M) compatible with the associativity and unit constraints. Morphisms of module functors are natural transformations commuting with these isomorphisms; a module equivalence is a module functor that is an equivalence of categories.

moore-penrose-inverse-matrix — Moore–Penrose inverse of a real matrix [definition]
  For a real matrix A, its Moore–Penrose inverse A† is the matrix satisfying AA†A=A, A†AA†=A†, (AA†)ᵀ=AA† and (A†A)ᵀ=A†A. For full column rank, A†=(AᵀA)⁻¹Aᵀ.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
    Evidence: Mathlib 26573066084e6e2aa8526ea358bc43b66d96f970. Matrix/NonsingularInverse explicitly limits its inverse construction to nonsingular square matrices and warns that pseudoinverses are not covered. Orthogonal projections and first-isomorphism constructors do not by themselves establish a chosen inverse satisfying all four Penrose equations for arbitrary rectangular real matrices. No such complete construction/characterization was verified in this Mathlib snapshot. Actual source statements, definitions and relevant completed proof bodies inspected; no fresh build or transitive proof/axiom audit.

morrey-inequality-euclidean — Morrey’s inequality on Euclidean space [theorem]
  For p>d, every u∈W¹,ᵖ(ℝᵈ) has a representative with |u(x)−u(y)|≤C|x−y|^{1−d/p}‖∇u‖_p for all x,y∈ℝᵈ.

  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True

  <- Hölder continuous function [statement]: The conclusion says the representative is (1−d/p)-Hölder continuous with constant C‖∇u‖_p.
  <- Meyers–Serrin theorem [proof]: Step 1 approximates u by u_m∈C^∞∩W^{1,p}(ℝⁿ) in W^{1,p} (p<∞); for p=∞ Lecture 9 passes through W^{1,s} on balls and the same density.
  <- Riesz–Fischer theorem for Lᵖ [proof]: A subsequence of u_m→u in Lᵖ converges almost everywhere, identifying the uniform limit as a representative of u.
  <- Continuity of a uniform limit [proof]: The u_m are Cauchy in C^{0,1−n/p}, hence uniformly, so their limit is continuous and inherits the Hölder bound.
  <- Fundamental theorem of calculus for continuous integrands [proof]: The integral mean value inequality starts from u(sθ)−u(0)=∫₀ˢθ·∇u(tθ)dt.
  <- Chain rule for Fréchet derivatives [proof]: d/dt u(tθ)=θ·∇u(tθ) for C¹ u along rays.
  <- Tonelli’s theorem for nonnegative functions [proof]: Integrating the ray estimate over θ and s exchanges the order of nonnegative integrals.
  <- Integration in polar coordinates on Euclidean space [proof]: The mean value inequality and ∫_{B_r}|y|^{(1−n)p′}dy are computed in polar coordinates.
  <- Hölder’s inequality [proof]: The corollary bounds ∫_{B_r}|∇u||y−x|^{1−n} by ‖∇u‖_{Lᵖ(B_r)} times a convergent integral since p>n; for p=∞ W^{1,∞}(B_R)⊂W^{1,s}(B_R).

morse-positive-attractor-qsd-concentration — Morse-attractor concentration of small-noise quasi-stationary laws [theorem]

Require β_δ(ε)=sup_xP_ε(x,{y:d(y,F(x))≥δ})≤e^(−c_δ/ε) eventually, and, for every c>0, some neighborhood V of S₀ satisfies inf_(x∈V∩S₊)P_ε(x,S₀)≥e^(−c/ε) eventually. If a finite Morse decomposition separates S₀ from S₊, its non-attractor Morse sets in S₊ are transitive, and μ_ε charges every neighborhood of some positive attractor, every weak QSD limit is F-invariant and supported on the positive Morse attractors; λ_ε≥1−e^(−c/ε) eventually for some c>0.

lower-central-commutator-multilinearity — Multilinearity of iterated commutators modulo the lower central series [theorem]
  Let γ_i be the lower central series of a group G and let g_k,h_k∈γ_(l_k)(G) for k=1,…,n. Modulo γ_(l₁+⋯+l_n+1)(G), the simple commutator [g₁,…,g_n] is multiplicative in each argument: replacing g_k by g_kh_k multiplies it by the commutator with h_k in place k. In particular [g₁^(m₁),…,g_n^(m_n)]≡[g₁,…,g_n]^(m₁⋯m_n) for positive integers m_k.

abelian-variety-multiplication-isogeny — Multiplication by n on an abelian variety [theorem]
  For an abelian variety A of dimension g over a field k and an integer n≥1, multiplication by n is an isogeny of degree n^(2g), étale exactly when char k does not divide n. In particular it is surjective on points over a separable closure when char k∤n.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Isogeny of abelian varieties [statement]: The conclusion is that n_A is an isogeny, with degree n^(2g).
  <- Characteristic of a field [statement]: Étaleness holds exactly when char k does not divide n.
  <- Étale morphism of schemes [statement]: The second assertion is that n_A is étale.
  <- Separable closure of a field [statement]: Surjectivity is asserted on points over a separable closure.
  <- Rational point of a scheme [statement]: Points over a separable closure are rational points of A.
  <- Projectivity of abelian varieties [proof]: Corollary 7.2 supplies an ample symmetric invertible sheaf L.
  <- Pullback of a line bundle by multiplication on an abelian variety [proof]: Corollary 6.6 gives n_A^*L≅L^(n²) for symmetric L, used both for finiteness of the kernel and for the degree count.
  <- Ample invertible sheaf [proof]: The restriction of n_A^*L to Ker(n_A) is trivial and ample, forcing the kernel to have dimension zero.
  <- Intersection number of divisors on a smooth projective variety [proof]: The degree is computed from ((n_A^*D)^g)=deg(n_A)(D^g) (Lemma 8.3) and (n²D)^g=n^(2g)(D^g), with (D^g)>0 for very ample D.
  <- Zariski tangent and cotangent space at a rational point [proof]: d(n_A)_0 is multiplication by n on T_0(A), an isomorphism exactly when char k∤n, giving étaleness by homogeneity.

absolute-ideal-norm-multiplicativity — Multiplicativity of the absolute ideal norm [theorem]
  For a number field K the absolute norm N(a)=|O_K/a| of nonzero ideals of O_K is multiplicative: N(ab)=N(a)N(b). If p is a nonzero prime of O_K with p∩ℤ=pℤ, then N(p)=p^f with f=[O_K/p:𝔽_p]; hence N(a)ℤ is the relative ideal norm of a from K to ℚ.

nagata-compactification-theorem — Nagata compactification theorem [theorem]
  Let S be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme, meaning that S is quasi-compact and any two quasi-compact open subsets have quasi-compact intersection; for example S may be the spectrum of a field. Every separated morphism of finite type X→S factors as an open immersion X→X̄ followed by a proper morphism X̄→S.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Open immersion of schemes [both]: The conclusion is an open immersion into X̄; the proof glues along open immersions.
  <- Proper morphism of schemes [both]: X̄→S is proper; the proof verifies properness via a proper surjection from a blow-up.
  <- Chow’s lemma for separated schemes of finite type [proof]: The proof starts from the refined Chow lemma (Conrad Cor. 2.6) for each quasi-projective dense open U_i.
  <- Blow-up of a scheme along a closed subscheme [proof]: X-admissible blow-ups are used to remove intersections with the boundary (Lemma 3.2) and to glue.
  <- Quasi-projective morphism of schemes [proof]: X is covered by finitely many dense opens quasi-projective over S (EGA II 5.3.4).
  <- Nagata’s blow-up gluing theorem for dense open immersions [proof]: Corollary 2.10 glues the M_i after blow-ups into a separated S-scheme M.
  <- Absolute Noetherian approximation of schemes [proof]: The non-Noetherian case is reduced to the Noetherian one by Thomason–Trobaugh approximation.

nagata-blow-up-gluing-theorem — Nagata’s blow-up gluing theorem for dense open immersions [theorem]
  Over a quasi-compact quasi-separated base S, given finitely many separated finite-type S-schemes M_i containing a common schematically dense open X by quasi-compact open immersions, there are X-admissible blow-ups M_i′ of the M_i that glue along X to a separated S-scheme of finite type (Nagata, Deligne; Conrad Theorem 2.8 and Corollary 2.10).

  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: False

affine-algebraic-set-noetherian-irreducible-decomposition — Noetherian topology and irreducible decomposition of affine algebraic sets [theorem]
  For a field k, the Zariski topology on any algebraic subset V of kⁿ is Noetherian. Hence V, in particular any affine variety over an algebraically closed field, is a finite union of irreducible closed subsets; an irredundant such union is unique up to order and consists exactly of the irreducible components of V.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

  <- Irreducible decomposition of a noetherian topological space [proof]: Existence of a finite decomposition by noetherian induction and uniqueness of irredundant decompositions; the members are the maximal irreducible closed subsets.
  <- Zariski topology on an affine variety [both]: Algebraic subsets of k^n are the Zariski-closed sets; the proof uses V↦I(V) on closed sets (Proposition 2.14).
  <- Irreducible component of a topological space [both]: The conclusion is finiteness of the set of irreducible components.
  <- Noetherian topological space [both]: The conclusion asserts the topology is Noetherian; the decomposition is deduced from it.

khayutin-state-norm-gap-nonescape-mass-bound — Non-escape of mass from a state-space norm gap and entropy [theorem]
  Let Γ be a lattice in a second-countable locally compact G, Y=Γ∖G with Haar probability m, K compact with open normalizer, X=Y/K and S(y)=ya⁻¹. If S-invariant Radon probabilities μ_i converge vaguely to a Radon measure μ and h=liminf_i h_(μ_i)(S), then μ(Y)≥1−(h_m(S)−h)/(−logλ).

  <- Continuous-time Galton–Watson process [both]: The theorem concerns the continuous-time Galton–Watson process with rate-β lifetimes; the proof writes it as a CMJ process with reproduction ξ(t)=A·1{L≤t}.

positive-distribution-hminus1-normality — Normality of the positive-distribution order on H⁻¹ [theorem]
  On a bounded smooth domain, H⁻¹=(H₀¹)* with its gradient-dual norm has a normal positive-distribution cone. More precisely, if h≥0 and−h≤w≤h then ‖w‖_{H⁻¹}≤‖h‖_{H⁻¹}; hence the norm diameter of[f,g] is at most‖g−f‖_{H⁻¹}.

  <- Lipschitz composition in W¹,ᵖ [proof]: For any v∈H₀¹, its positive and negative parts lie inH₀¹ and satisfy |⟨w,v⟩|≤⟨h,|v|⟩≤‖h‖_{H⁻¹}‖|v|‖_{H₀¹}=‖h‖_{H⁻¹}‖v‖_{H₀¹}. finite-separable-extension-dvr-normalization — Normalization of a discrete valuation ring in a finite separable extension [theorem]
  Let A be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field K and L/K finite separable. Its integral closure B in L is a finite A-module and a Dedekind domain. The maximal ideals of B above the maximal ideal of A correspond to extensions of the valuation to L, up to positive normalization; localizing B at each such ideal gives the extension valuation ring.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Valuation ring of a discretely valued field [statement]: A is a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal m, and the localizations of B are valuation rings of discrete valuations extending that of A.
  <- Separable algebraic field extension [statement]: L/K is a separable algebraic extension.
  <- Finite-dimensional vector space [statement]: L/K is finite, i.e. finite-dimensional as a K-vector space.
  <- Finitely generated module over a commutative ring [statement]: B is asserted to be a finite A-module.
  <- Dedekind domain [statement]: B is asserted to be a Dedekind domain; integral closure and fraction fields are inherited through its definition.
  <- Maximal ideal [statement]: The correspondence is indexed by the maximal ideals of B lying over the maximal ideal of A.
  <- Integral closure of a Dedekind domain in a finite separable extension [proof]: A discrete valuation ring is Dedekind, so its integral closure in finite separable L is a Dedekind domain finitely generated over A.
  <- Unique factorization of ideals in a Dedekind domain [proof]: The valuations v_q are exponents in prime factorizations of fractional ideals of B, and v_q(xB)=e_q v(xA) is computed from the factorization of mB.
  <- Local characterization of Dedekind domains [proof]: A is Dedekind; each localization B_q is the valuation ring of v_q, and the valuation ring W of an extension w is integrally closed, contains B and equals B_q for q=m_W∩B.

norris-lemma — Norris’s lemma for continuous semimartingales [theorem]
  Let Z_t=Z₀+∫₀ᵗA_sds+∫₀ᵗB_sdW_s on[0,1], with adapted A,B whose1/3-Hölder norms have every finite moment. There is r>0 such that for every p>0, P(‖Z‖∞≤ε and max(‖A‖∞,‖B‖∞)>εʳ)≤C_pεᵖ for0<ε≤1.

  <- Itô integral with respect to Brownian motion [statement]: Z contains the Itô integral ∫B dW against a Wiener process.
  <- Adapted stochastic process [statement]: A and B are adapted processes.
  <- Hölder continuous function [statement]: The hypothesis bounds all moments of the 1/3-Hölder norms of A and B.
  <- Exponential martingale inequality for Itô integrals [proof]: Applied to ∫F dW and to −∫F dW to obtain the almost implication (6.20), and again to bound the martingale part.
  <- Itô’s formula for Brownian diffusions [proof]: Itô’s formula applied to Z² gives (6.21); Z is an Itô process with adapted coefficients.
  <- Jensen’s inequality for expectations [proof]: Jensen’s inequality on [0,1] passes from ∫|B|²ds≤ε^{1/2} to ∫|B|ds≤ε^{1/4}.

  <- Mean value theorem for real functions [proof]: The inline Lemma 6.27, used twice with ∂_tf=|B| and ∂_tf=A, rests on a mean-value estimate for a C¹ function whose derivative stays large on an interval.

novikov-exponential-martingale-criterion — Novikov exponential-martingale criterion [theorem]
  If L is a real continuous local martingale with L₀=0 and Eexp([L]_T/2)<∞ on a finite horizon, its stochastic exponential E(L) is a uniformly integrable martingale on [0,T], with E E(L)_T=1.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Stochastic exponential of a continuous local martingale [both]: The statement concerns E(L)=exp(L−[L]/2); Krylov works with ρ(M)=exp(M_∞−⟨M⟩_∞/2) for M=L^T and with ρ((1−ε)M).
  <- Uniformly integrable family of real random variables [statement]: The conclusion asserts that E(L) is a uniformly integrable martingale on [0,T].
  <- Hölder’s inequality [proof]: Hölder with exponents 1/(1−ε),1/ε gives 1=Eρ((1−ε)M)≤(Eρ)^{1−ε}(Ee^{(1−ε)⟨M⟩/2})^ε; Cauchy–Schwarz and Hölder also bound Ee^{M_t/2} and E sup ρ_t^{1+δ} in item 5.
  <- Nonnegative local martingales are supermartingales [proof]: Eρ≤1 because ρ_t is a nonnegative local martingale; after Eρ=1 the same characterization upgrades the mean-one exponential to a martingale on [0,T].
  <- Doob’s Lp maximal inequality for càdlàg martingales [proof]: Doob's moment inequality for the local martingale ρ_t gives E sup_t ρ_t^{1+δ}≤N sup_t Eρ_t^{1+δ}.
  <- Fatou’s lemma [proof]: Doob's inequality is applied to the local martingale ρ through its localized martingales and passage to the limit, and the finite-moment bound sup_t E e^{κM_t} is controlled through limits of stopped variables.
  <- Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem [proof]: With E sup_t ρ_t<∞ and a localizing sequence τ_n, Eρ=E lim ρ_{τ_n}=lim Eρ_{τ_n}=1.

  A real continuous semimartingale X has local timesL_t^a with∫₀ᵗg(X_s)d[X]_s=∫_ℝg(a)L_t^a da for nonnegative Borel g. In particular if[X]_t=t, it spends zero Lebesgue time in any Lebesgue-null spatial set.

odell-schreier-unconditionality — Odell’s Schreier unconditionality theorem [theorem]
  For every normalized weakly null sequence (x_n) in a Banach space and η>0, some subsequence (y_n) satisfies ∥∑_{i∈F}a_i y_i∥≤(2+η)∥∑a_i y_i∥ for every finitely supported scalar sequence a and every finite F⊂ℕ with |F|≤min F.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Weak convergence in a Banach space [both]: Hypothesis: a normalized weakly null sequence in a Banach space; the proof passes to weakly null subsequences.
  <- Finitely supported scalar sequence [statement]: The inequality is asserted for every finitely supported scalar sequence (a_i).
  <- Near-unconditionality on sets of bounded size for weakly null subsequences [proof]: DOST derive Odell’s constant 2+ε by a diagonal argument from Theorem 12: choose nested subsequences that are (1+ε)-unconditional on sets of size ≤n and diagonalize, so that each Schreier set F (|F|≤min F=m) lies in a tail that is (1+ε)-unconditional for size ≤m.
  <- Basic subsequences of normalized weakly null sequences [proof]: The tail projection onto {i≥min F} costs a factor at most 1+(basis constant); passing first to a basic subsequence with constant 1+ε gives the factor 2+ε in the diagonal argument.

  For a strongly local regular symmetric Dirichlet form and a bounded domain function f, the pushforward under f of its energy measure ν_f is absolutely continuous with respect to one-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Consequently ν_f has no point masses.

portmanteau-open-set-inequality — Open-set inequality under weak convergence [theorem]
  Ifprobabilitymeasuresμ_n convergeweaklytoμ onametricspace, thenμ(U)≤liminf_nμ_n(U) foreveryopensetU.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Weak convergence of probability measures on a metric space [statement]: The hypothesis is weak convergence μ_n⇒μ of probability measures on a metric space.
  <- Borel σ-algebra of a topological space [statement]: The measures are Borel probability measures, so μ(U) is defined for open U.
  <- Topology induced by a metric [statement]: U is open in the metric topology.
  <- Distance from a point to a subset of a metric space [proof]: For closed F the cutoff g=max(0,1−d(x,F)/δ) is built from the distance to F.
  <- Lipschitz map between metric spaces [proof]: x↦d(x,F) is 1-Lipschitz, so the cutoff g is bounded continuous and weak convergence applies to it.
  <- Monotonicity of the Lebesgue integral [proof]: μ_n(F)≤μ_n(g) and μ(g)≤μ(F^δ) follow from monotonicity of the integral.
  <- Limit superior of a real sequence [proof]: Step (i)⇒(ii) gives limsup_n μ_n(F)≤μ(F) for closed F.
  <- Continuity of a measure along monotone sequences of sets [proof]: Letting δ↓0, μ(F^δ) decreases to μ(F) because F is closed.
  <- Closure of a subset of a topological space [proof]: Closed sets are complements of open sets; F=⋂_δ F^δ for closed F.
  <- Limit inferior of a real or extended-real sequence [statement]: The conclusion bounds μ(U) by liminf_n μ_n(U).

  For an algebraic Galois extension L/F with Krull-topologized Galois group G, open subgroups H correspond contravariantly to intermediate fields of finite degree by H↦L^H. Open normal subgroups correspond to finite Galois intermediate extensions, and Gal(L^H/F)=G/H in that case.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True

  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

  <- Fixed field of field automorphisms [statement]: The correspondence sends H to its fixed field L^H among the intermediate fields.
  <- Finite Galois field extension [statement]: Open normal subgroups correspond to finite Galois intermediate extensions with their finite Galois groups.
  <- Quotient of a group by a normal subgroup [statement]: The Galois group of L^H/F is identified with the quotient G/H by a normal subgroup.
  <- Profiniteness of Galois groups [proof]: Compactness of G makes every open subgroup of finite index, so the fixed field has finite degree.
  <- Extension of embeddings into an algebraic Galois extension [proof]: Extending embeddings gives the bijection G/H→Hom_F(L^H,L) and the surjective restriction G→Gal(L^H/F) with kernel H; it also shows G-stable intermediate fields are Galois.
  <- Artin fixed-field degree theorem [proof]: For an open H containing Gal(L/E) with E finite Galois, Artin’s theorem for the image of H in Gal(E/F) shows Gal(L/L^H)=H.
  <- Fixed-field characterization of finite Galois extensions [proof]: Gal(L/M) fixes exactly M, reduced to finite Galois layers, giving L^(Gal(L/M))=M; the order |Gal(E/F)|=[E:F] counts embeddings of finite subextensions.

optional-sampling-ui-cadlag-martingale — Optional sampling for a uniformly integrable càdlàg martingale [theorem]
  For a uniformly integrable càdlàg martingale M on a finite horizon [0,T] and stopping times σ≤τ≤T, E[M_τ|F_σ]=M_σ. In particular a martingale closed by an integrable terminal variable can be sampled at bounded stopping times.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Continuous-time martingale [statement]: The theorem concerns a continuous-time martingale.
  <- Càdlàg path [statement]: Right-continuity of paths is the regularity hypothesis (càdlàg in the catalogue form).
  <- Uniformly integrable family of real random variables [statement]: The martingale is uniformly integrable (on a finite horizon it is closed by M_T).
  <- σ-algebra of a stopping time [statement]: The conclusion conditions on F_σ.
  <- Continuous-time supermartingale [proof]: The proof is for submartingales (negatives of supermartingales) and is applied to M and −M, and to M∨c.
  <- Conditional Jensen inequality [proof]: x↦x∨c is convex nondecreasing, so M∨c and M⁺ are submartingales (Proposition 3.1).
  <- Tower property of conditional expectation [proof]: Discrete optional stopping is proved by iterated conditioning down the countable value set.
  <- Pull-out property of conditional expectation [proof]: Indicators 1{τ>s_j} and stopped values that are F_(s_j)-measurable are pulled out of the conditional expectation.
  <- Fatou’s lemma [proof]: Gives E|M_ρ|≤2E M_T⁺−E M₀ from the discrete approximants, so stopped values are integrable.
  <- Uniform integrability of the conditional expectations of an integrable variable [proof]: Bounds c≤M_(τ_n∧T)∨c≤E[M_T∨c|F_(τ_n)] make the approximating sequences uniformly integrable.
  <- Vitali convergence theorem for random variables [proof]: Almost sure convergence plus uniform integrability gives L¹ convergence of the stopped values.
  <- Linearity and monotonicity of conditional expectation [proof]: |E[X_n|G]−E[X|G]|≤E[|X_n−X||G] transfers L¹ convergence to conditional expectations.
  <- Almost surely convergent subsequence of a sequence converging in probability [proof]: An L¹-convergent sequence of conditional expectations has an almost surely convergent subsequence.
  <- Progressive measurability of adapted right- or left-continuous processes [proof]: A right-continuous adapted M is progressively measurable.
  <- Measurability of a progressive process at a stopping time [proof]: Hence M_(σ∧τ∧T) is F_(σ∧τ∧T)⊆F_σ-measurable.
  <- Dominated convergence theorem for conditional expectations [proof]: Letting c↓−∞ with |M_(τ∧T)∨c|≤|M_(τ∧T)| removes the truncation.

ordered-cadlag-markov-path-coupling — Ordered coupling of càdlàg half-line Markov paths [theorem]
  Let X,Y be time-homogeneous càdlàg Markov families on[0,∞) with transition semigroups P,Q, such that P_t(x,·)≤stQ_t(y,·) whenever x≤y and t≥0. For every x≤y there is a coupling of their whole path laws started at x,y with X_t≤Y_t for every t≥0 almost surely. In particular this holds for two ordered initial states of one stochastically monotone family, or when P is stochastically dominated by a monotone Q. This path-law assertion alone makes no claim that the coordinates are Markov or martingales in their common enlarged filtration.

orthogonal-direct-sum-hilbert-space — Orthogonal direct-sum decomposition of a Hilbert space [definition]
  A real or complex Hilbert space H is the orthogonal direct sum ⊕_m H_m of a sequence of closed subspaces when the H_m are pairwise orthogonal and every x∈H is a norm-convergent sum ∑_m x_m with x_m∈H_m; the expansion is then unique. For pairwise orthogonal closed subspaces this holds exactly when their linear span is dense.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

  <- Closure of a subset of a topological space [statement]: The summands are closed and the density criterion uses closure of their span.

oseledets-splitting-invertible-linear-cocycle — Oseledets splitting of an invertible linear cocycle [definition]
  Let θ be an invertible ergodic measure-preserving transformation of Ω and A:Ω→GL_d(ℝ) measurable, with A⁽ⁿ⁾(ω)=A(θⁿ⁻¹ω)⋯A(ω) and A⁽⁻ⁿ⁾(ω)=A⁽ⁿ⁾(θ⁻ⁿω)⁻¹. An Oseledets splitting is an almost everywhere defined measurable decomposition ℝᵈ=E₁(ω)⊕⋯⊕E_k(ω) with A(ω)E_i(ω)=E_i(θω), together with Lyapunov exponents λ₁>⋯>λ_k such that n⁻¹log‖A⁽ⁿ⁾(ω)v‖→λ_i as n→±∞ for every nonzero v∈E_i(ω). The multiplicity of λ_i is dim E_i(ω); λ_i is simple when this is one.

perfect-field — Perfect field [definition]

peter-weyl-theorem — Peter–Weyl theorem [theorem]
  For a compact Hausdorff group K, every irreducible continuous unitary representation is finite-dimensional. Its matrix coefficients, multiplied by the square root of their representation dimension, form an orthonormal basis of L²(K) as the irreducible representation varies, and their finite linear span is uniformly dense in C(K).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Irreducible unitary representation [statement]: The theorem is about irreducible continuous unitary representations.
  <- Finite-dimensional vector space [statement]: Each irreducible representation is asserted finite-dimensional.
  <- Dimension of a vector space [statement]: Matrix coefficients are scaled by the square root of the representation dimension.
  <- Matrix coefficient of a unitary representation [statement]: The orthonormal basis and dense subspace consist of matrix coefficients.
  <- Lebesgue Lᵖ space [statement]: The basis is an orthonormal basis of L²(K).
  <- Haar’s theorem for compact groups [both]: L²(K) is formed with the normalized (bi-invariant) Haar probability measure.
  <- C*-algebra of complex continuous functions on a compact space [statement]: Density is asserted in C(K) with the uniform norm.
  <- Dense subset of a topological space [statement]: The span is uniformly dense in C(K).
  <- Spectral theorem for bounded self-adjoint operators [proof]: Schur's lemma for unitary representations: T*T is equivariant and self-adjoint, and the spectral theorem forces it to be scalar.
  <- Spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators [proof]: Self-adjoint convolution operators are compact; their nonzero eigenspaces are finite-dimensional invariant subspaces.
  <- Hilbert–Schmidt property of square-integrable integral kernels [proof]: Right convolution by K∈L²(K) is an integral operator with square-integrable kernel, hence Hilbert–Schmidt.
  <- Hilbert–Schmidt operators are compact [proof]: Hilbert–Schmidt convolution operators are compact.
  <- Convolution of functions on a locally compact group [proof]: The proof convolves functions on K (f∗K, f∗f*, approximate identities).
  <- Integrated operator of a unitary representation [proof]: Finite-dimensional representations are detected through π_f; EFHN Proposition 15.12 finds π with π_f≠0.
  <- Fubini’s theorem for integrable functions [proof]: Schur orthogonality (√dim normalization) uses Fubini with Corollary 2.8.5.
  <- Trace of a square matrix [proof]: Corollary 2.8.5 averages ρ(g)Tρ(g)* to tr(T)I/dim, giving the orthogonality relations.
  <- Complex Stone–Weierstrass theorem [proof]: Matrix coefficients form a unital conjugation-closed subalgebra separating points, hence are uniformly dense in C(K).
  <- Urysohn lemma for locally compact Hausdorff spaces [proof]: Point separation uses a continuous u≥0 with u(1)>0 supported in a small neighbourhood U of the identity.

  A vector field continuous in time and locally Lipschitz in the state has a unique local solution through each initial point, with continuous dependence on initial data and the field on compact sets. If the state stays in a compact set on each finite interval, the solution extends globally; globally Lipschitz fields of linear growth satisfy this condition.

piecing-out-killed-markov-process — Piecing out a Markov process killed at a state-dependent rate [construction]
  Given a right-continuous strong Markov process X on E, a measurable rate r:E→[0,∞) and a probability kernel K on E: run X, take an independent standard exponential variable e and kill X at ζ=inf{t:∫₀ᵗr(X_s)ds>e}; restart at time ζ from a point drawn from K(X_ζ,·) using an independent fresh copy of X, and repeat. poincare-complete-reducibility-abelian-varieties — Poincaré complete reducibility for abelian varieties [theorem]
  For an abelian subvariety B⊆A over a characteristic-zero field k, there is an abelian subvariety C⊆A over k for which addition B×C→A is a k-isogeny. Thus nontrivial decompositions up to isogeny correspond to nontrivial idempotents in End⁰_k(A).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

  <- Characteristic of a field [statement]: The base field is assumed to have characteristic zero.
  <- Rational endomorphism algebra of an abelian variety [statement]: Decompositions up to isogeny are matched with idempotents of End⁰_k(A).
  <- Idempotent element of an algebra [statement]: The second clause concerns nontrivial idempotents of the endomorphism algebra.
  <- Ample invertible sheaf [proof]: The proof chooses an ample invertible sheaf L on A.
  <- Projectivity of abelian varieties [proof]: Existence of the ample sheaf L used in the construction.
  <- Dual abelian variety [proof]: The complement is built from the dual A^∨ and the dual map i^∨:A^∨→B^∨.
  <- Mumford homomorphism of an invertible sheaf on an abelian variety [proof]: C is the reduced identity component of ker(i^∨∘φ_L), using i^∨∘φ_L∘i=φ_(i*L).
  <- Mumford homomorphism of an ample sheaf is an isogeny [proof]: B∩C lies in ker φ_(L|B), finite because L|B is ample; φ_L finite surjective gives the dimension bound.
  <- Identity component of a group scheme over a field [proof]: C is the reduced identity component of the kernel, an abelian variety over the perfect base.
  <- Fiber dimension theorem for algebraic varieties [proof]: dim ker(i^∨)≥dim A^∨−dim B^∨ by the dimension of fibres.

  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True

  <- Radial boundary function of a function on the unit disk [statement]: g* is the radial boundary function.
  <- Poisson kernel of the unit disk [statement]: The majorant integrates log|g*| against P_z.
  <- Lebesgue Lᵖ space [statement]: The boundary logarithm is asserted to be integrable.
  <- Logarithmic boundary integrability of nonzero Hardy H² functions [proof]: Applied to g and to g∘φ_ξ (bounded, hence in H²): log|g*| is integrable and log|g(ξ)|=log|(g∘φ_ξ)(0)|≤∫log|(g∘φ_ξ)*|dm.
  <- Biholomorphic automorphism of the unit disk [proof]: φ_ξ(z)=(ξ−z)/(1−ξ̄z) is an automorphism of the disk with φ_ξ(0)=ξ; on the circle the pushforward of m under φ_ξ is P_ξ dm (a change-of-variables calculation recorded in the notes).
  <- Fatou’s nontangential limit theorem for bounded holomorphic functions [proof]: Radii are mapped by φ_ξ to curves ending nontangentially, so (g∘φ_ξ)*=g*∘φ_ξ almost everywhere.

poisson-summation-number-field — Poisson summation on a number field [theorem]
  For a Schwartz–Bruhat function f on A_F^n, a nontrivial additive character of A_F/F and its self-dual Haar measure, ∑_(x∈F^n)f(x)=∑_(x∈F^n)f̂(x).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Adelic Fourier transform and self-dual Haar measure [both]: f̂ is the adelic Fourier transform for ψ and its self-dual Haar measure.
  <- Absolute convergence of a real series [statement]: Both sums over Fⁿ converge absolutely.
  <- Self-duality of the adeles of a number field [proof]: The dual of A_F/F is F via a↦ψ(a·) (Corollary 5.4); this indexes the Fourier series of the periodization and identifies every nontrivial ψ as ψ_std(a·), a∈F×.
  <- Unit volume of the adele quotient for the self-dual measure [proof]: A fundamental domain D has volume 1 for the self-dual measure (Proposition 5.5), so the Fourier coefficients of the periodization equal f̂ on F without a normalizing factor.
  <- Compactness of adelic quotients of unipotent groups [proof]: Fⁿ is discrete and cocompact in A_Fⁿ (the additive group is unipotent), so the periodization lives on a compact abelian group.
  <- Fourier inversion on a compact abelian group [proof]: Fourier inversion on the compact group A_Fⁿ/Fⁿ, evaluated at 0, gives ∑f(ξ)=∑f̂(ξ).
  <- Pontryagin duality for locally compact abelian groups [proof]: Corollary 5.4 uses that the dual of the compact group A/K is discrete.

polynomial-sequence-nilpotent-group — Polynomial sequence in a nilpotent group [definition]
  For a nilpotent group G, a sequence g:ℤ→G is polynomial if some iterate of the difference Dg(n)=g(n)^(−1)g(n+1) is identically one. Equivalently it can be written U₁^(p₁(n))⋯U_r^(p_r(n)) with fixed U_j∈G and integer-valued polynomials p_j.

pontryagin-duality-locally-compact-abelian — Pontryagin duality for locally compact abelian groups [theorem]
  For a Hausdorff locally compact abelian group A, its dual A∨=Hom_cont(A,ℝ/ℤ) with the compact-open topology is again locally compact abelian, and evaluation A→(A∨)∨ is an isomorphism of topological groups. chi-distribution-positive-moments — Positive and negative moments of an integer-degree chi distribution [theorem]
  Forχ_d with d positive integer and reala>−d, Eχ_d^a=2^(a/2)Γ((d+a)/2)/Γ(d/2).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Chi distribution with integer degrees of freedom [both]: The statement concerns a variable χ_d with the chi distribution of integer degree d; the proof uses that law through its density.
  <- Gamma function on the positive real axis [both]: The formula is a ratio of gamma values at the positive reals (d+a)/2 and d/2; the proof identifies the moment integral with Γ((d+a)/2).
  <- Expectation of an integrable real random variable [statement]: Eχ_d^a is the expectation of the nonnegative variable χ_d^a (finite exactly when a>−d).
  <- Density of the chi distribution [proof]: The moment is computed by integrating x^a against the chi density 2^(1−d/2)x^(d−1)e^(−x²/2)/Γ(d/2).
  <- Change of variables formula for expectations [proof]: Eχ_d^a=∫x^a μ(dx) for the law μ of χ_d (nonnegative integrand).
  <- Probability density relative to a measure [proof]: Integrating against the law with a Lebesgue density equals ∫x^a f(x)dx.
  <- Change of variables theorem for Euclidean integrals [proof]: The substitution t=x²/2, a C¹ diffeomorphism of (0,∞), turns ∫₀^∞x^(a+d−1)e^(−x²/2)dx into 2^((a+d)/2−1)∫₀^∞t^((a+d)/2−1)e^(−t)dt.
  <- Monotone convergence theorem for Lebesgue integrals [proof]: Identifies the Lebesgue integral over (0,∞) of the nonnegative integrand with the limit over compact subintervals, i.e. the improper integral defining Γ; for a+d≤0 it shows the moment is infinite.
  <- Agreement of Riemann and Lebesgue integrals [proof]: On each compact subinterval the continuous integrand has equal Riemann and Lebesgue integrals, matching the improper Riemann definition of Γ.
  explains in wikipedia-chi-distribution-rev-1370800453, Properties › Moments — Raw-moment formula by integration against the density.

potts-model-finite-graph — Potts model on a finite graph [definition]
  A finite-state spin at every vertex receives Gibbs weight determined by whether adjacent spins agree; the antiferromagnetic model penalizes agreement.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: formalized; estimated LOC: 41.8
    Evidence: Mathlib 26573066084e6e2aa8526ea358bc43b66d96f970. For a finite graph with UNORDERED edge set E and q>=1 states Fin q, configurations sigma:V→Fin q receive positive weights exp(-beta*sum_{e={u,v}}J(e)*1_{sigma(u)=sigma(v)}), optionally with specified single-site fields. Take beta>=0,J(e)>=0 for the antiferromagnetic convention, so agreement increases the energy and decreases the weight. PMF.normalize246/253 exactly divides these finite positive weights by their finite nonzero partition sum and proves probability normalization. This is a literal checked finite-state constructor, not an infinite-volume or phase-transition theorem. q=0 with nonempty V is excluded because there is no spin configuration to normalize.  Relevant actual declarations/hypotheses/completed source bodies inspected; bounded source review without new proof development or transitive axiom audit.

minimal-idempotent — Primitive idempotent in an algebra [definition]
  A nonzero idempotent that is not a sum of two nonzero orthogonal idempotents. In a finite-dimensional semisimple algebra A, e is primitive exactly when the left ideal Ae is a simple A-module.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: partial; estimated LOC: 30.5

IsIdempotentElem37 is literally e*e=e, so no central-idempotent or corner-division condition is substituted. This primary nondecomposition definition is fully representable. However the explicit finite-dimensional semisimple-algebra equivalence with simplicity of the LEFT ideal Ae was not certified in standalone Mathlib; generic module semisimplicity/indecomposability constructors do not automatically certify that dictionary in this bounded review. degree-principal-divisor-zero — Principal divisors on a smooth projective curve have degree zero [theorem]
  For a nonzero rational function f on a smooth projective curve over a field, deg div(f)=0: counted with multiplicities (and residue-field degrees over a non-closed field), f has as many zeros as poles. Thus principal divisors form a subgroup of the degree-zero divisors.

principal-ideal-theorem-hilbert-class-field — Principal ideal theorem for the Hilbert class field [theorem]

lebesgue-stieltjes-probability-cdf — Probability measure determined by a distribution function [theorem]
  Every nondecreasing right-continuous F:ℝ→[0,1] with limits0 at−∞ and1 at+∞ is the distribution function of a unique Borel probability measure, characterized byμ((−∞,x])=F(x).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Monotone real function [statement]: F is nondecreasing.
  <- Limit of a real function at a point [statement]: Right continuity lim_(y↓x)F(y)=F(x) and the limits 0 and 1 at ∓∞ are limits of a real function.
  <- Probability space [statement]: The conclusion is a probability measure, a measure of total mass one.
  <- Borel σ-algebra on the real line [statement]: The measure is defined on the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ.
  <- Carathéodory extension theorem [proof]: Proof of Theorem 1.1.4: μ((a,b])=F(b)−F(a) on the semialgebra of half-open intervals satisfies (i) and (ii) of Theorem 1.1.9, which extends it, uniquely by σ-finiteness, to σ(S), the Borel sets.
  <- Convergence of bounded monotone real sequences [proof]: The proof begins by noting that F(∞)=lim_(x↑∞)F(x) and F(−∞)=lim_(x↓−∞)F(x) exist for nondecreasing F.
  <- Heine–Borel theorem in finite-dimensional normed spaces [proof]: Countable subadditivity: the open intervals (a_i,b_i+η_i) cover the compact interval [a+δ,b], so finitely many suffice.

compact-group-inverse-limit-projection-image — Projection image of an inverse limit of compact groups [theorem]
  For compact Hausdorff groups G_n and continuous homomorphisms f_n:G_(n+1)→G_n, the image of lim←G_n in G₀ equals ⋂_(n≥0)f_(n,0)(G_n), where f_(n,0) is the composite transition map and f_(0,0) is the identity. Surjectivity of the transition maps is not required.

  <- Compact subsets of Hausdorff spaces are closed [proof]: Those compact images, and points, are closed in the Hausdorff group G_m, so the cluster value lies in every image and maps to the prescribed element.

projection-valued-measure-real-line — Projection-valued measure on the real line [definition]

projective-dual-variety — Projective dual variety and its discriminant [definition]
  Let X⊂P^m be a closed irreducible subvariety over an algebraically closed field. Its conormal (incidence) variety W_X⊂P^m×P̌^m is the closure of the set of pairs (x,H) with x a smooth point of X and H a hyperplane containing the tangent space T_xX. The dual variety X^∨⊂P̌^m is the image of W_X under the second projection p₂. X is defective if X^∨ is not a hypersurface; otherwise the reduced homogeneous equation of X^∨, unique up to a scalar, is the discriminant of X (for a toric X_A, the A-discriminant Δ_A).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

  <- Weak compactness of probabilities on a compact metric space [proof]: For tight M choose increasing compactsK_m with mass≥1−2^{-m}. Compact-space weak compactness and a diagonal subsequence give weak limits of all restricted measures μ_n|K_m; these limits increase as measures and have mass tending to1. Their monotone limitμ is a probability measure, and the compact restrictions plus the uniform tail bound show μ_n(f)→μ(f) for every bounded continuousf. Conversely, tightness from small neighborhoods of compacts follows by intersecting compact neighborhoods at radiiε2^{-m}, obtaining a closed totally bounded subset of the complete space. If M is not tight, the contrapositive produces a fixedε>0 and successively separated compact setsK_n carrying definite mass for selectedμ_n while later K’s carry little mass for earlierμ_n. Uniformly Lipschitz cutoffs on their disjointε/2-neighborhoods can be assigned signs recursively so the resulting bounded continuous test function has nonconvergent μ_n integrals on every subsequence. Thus M cannot be weakly precompact.

If M is not tight, the contrapositive produces a fixedε>0 and successively separated compact setsK_n carrying definite mass for selectedμ_n while later K’s carry little mass for earlierμ_n. Thus M cannot be weakly precompact.
  <- Bounded–Lipschitz metrization of weak convergence [proof]: For a tight family, choose increasing compactsK_m carrying mass≥1−2^{−m}. Restricted measures have mass≤1; append an isolated cemetery point carrying the missing mass and apply compact-space probability weak compactness. Diagonal extraction gives limitsν_m of every restriction. Testing nonnegative continuous functions on larger compact sets showsν_m≤ν_{m+1}; their increasing limitν has mass1. Uniform tail bounds then prove weak convergence of the extracted original measures. For the converse, lack of tightness, the compact-neighborhood lemma and tightness of individual measures construct separated compactsK_n and measuresμ_n withμ_n(K_n)≥ε−δ while later neighborhoods together haveμ_n-mass≤δ. For EACH proposed subsequence, keep its corresponding separated compacts and choose signs for their uniformly Lipschitz cutoffs recursively; the resulting bounded continuous function makes consecutive integrals along THAT subsequence differ by at leastε−3δ. Hence that candidate subsequence cannot converge. The test function may depend on the candidate subsequence; one fixed bounded test cannot exclude every subsequence. Takingδ<ε/3 proves failure of weak sequential precompactness. Bounded–Lipschitz metrization identifies sequential precompactness with relative compactness here.
  relies_on in flandoli-gess-scheutzow-order-2015, §2, Proposition2.4 and Theorem2.6

pure-drift-rewired-cycle-chain — Pure drift chain on uniformly rewired cycle arcs [construction]
  Cut a directed cycle at k uniformly chosen distinct edges into arcs. Along each remaining arc the chain moves deterministically forward; at an arc endpoint it chooses the start of one of the k arcs uniformly. Equivalently one can begin with k independent positive geometric arc lengths and then condition their sum to obtain a fixed-size model.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

quadratic-tikhonov-operator-perturbation-rate — Quadratic Tikhonov error rate under operator perturbations [theorem]
  Let A:X→Y andL:X→Z be bounded linear maps between real Hilbert spaces with ∥h∥≤C(∥Ah∥+∥Lh∥). LetAx†=y and⟨Lx†,Lh⟩=⟨w,Ah⟩ for allh. If∥A_ρ−A∥≤ρ,∥yδ−y∥≤δ andα is comparable toη=δ+ρ>0 tending to zero, minimizers of∥A_ρx−yδ∥²+α∥Lx∥² satisfy∥x−x†∥²=O(η) for sufficiently smallρ.

  <- Source condition for a differentiable quadratic Tikhonov penalty [both]: Joint control by A and L excludes an unobservable penalty-null direction; the error is a squared Hilbert norm, with norm-bounded perturbations and balanced positiveα.
  <- Young’s inequality for products [proof]: Writee=x−x†,R=∥A_ρe∥,S=∥Le∥ andε=yδ−A_ρx†, with∥ε∥=O(η). Minimality and expansion giveR²+αS²≤2⟨A_ρe,ε⟩−2α⟨w,Ae⟩. Bound inner products by expanding∥u−tv∥²≥0, and replaceAe byA_ρe+(A−A_ρ)e. For smallρ, joint control gives∥e∥≤C′(R+S). Young’s inequality absorbs the R and S terms, leavingR²+αS²≤C(η²+α²+αρ²). Withα comparable toη this impliesS²=O(η),R²=O(η²), hence∥e∥²=O(η). Joint control also makes the perturbed quadratic coercive for smallρ, so its minimizer exists uniquely. This checked algebra is the fixed-space perturbation estimate used after surface pullback.

elementary-nilsequence-quadratic-modulation-cyclicity — Quadratic-mean modulation cyclicity of a Heisenberg nilsequence [theorem]
  For b_n=e^(2πins)e^(πin(n−1)t)∏_(j=1)^dω_n(α_j,β_j), with d≥0 and α₁,…,α_d,β₁,…,β_d rationally independent modulo1, the span of (e^(2πinu)b_n)_n, u∈R/Z, is dense in S(b) for the nilsequence quadratic mean norm; S(b) is the uniform closed span of its modulated integer shifts.

  For specified one-body and pair potentials Φ,Ψ, a point-process law is quasi-Gibbs if its restriction to configurations with m particles in each bounded region can be approximated increasingly by submeasures whose conditional inside laws, given the outside configuration, are bounded above and below by positive multiples of exp(−H_inside) times Poisson reference measure restricted to m particles.   Let E be an elliptic curve over a number field K and f a nonconstant even function on E, with h_f(P) the logarithmic height of f(P)∈ℙ¹. Then h_f(P+Q)+h_f(P−Q)=2h_f(P)+2h_f(Q)+O(1) for all P,Q∈E(K̄), the constant depending only on E and f. Consequently h_f([m]P)=m²h_f(P)+O(1) for each integer m.

rademacher-empirical-process-symmetrization — Rademacher symmetrization of a centered empirical supremum [theorem]
  For independent identically distributedX_i, an integrably bounded separable classF of real measurable functions, and independent Rademacherε_i, E sup_(f∈F)∑(Ef(X_i)−f(X_i))≤2E sup_(f∈F)∑ε_i f(X_i).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Independent family of random elements [both]: X_i are independent random elements of a measurable space, and the Rademacher signs are independent of them; the proof also uses an independent copy.
  <- Pushforward measure [statement]: Identically distributed means the X_i have the same law (pushforward of P), so Ef(X_i) is the same for all i.
  <- Expectation of an integrable real random variable [statement]: Both sides are expectations of suprema; Ef(X_i) are means, finite by the integrable envelope.
  <- Rademacher random sequence [both]: ε_i are independent Rademacher signs; their symmetry is used to insert signs into the symmetrized sum.
  <- Pointwise measurable class of real functions [both]: The separable class is a pointwise measurable class; the proof uses it to make the suprema measurable by reducing them to a countable subclass.
  <- Joint law of independent random elements is the product law [proof]: The joint law of (X,Y,ε) is a product law, so swapping X_k and Y_k preserves it and integrals can be iterated.
  <- Fubini’s theorem for integrable functions [proof]: Writes Ef(X_k)=E[f(Y_k)|X] and moves the expectation in Y outside the supremum (the "Jensen" step, sup of integrals ≤ integral of sup).
  <- Monotonicity of the Lebesgue integral [proof]: Supplies sup_f∫≤∫sup_f in the first inequality of Lemma 7.3.
  <- Change of variables formula for expectations [proof]: f(X_k)−f(Y_k) and ε_k(f(X_k)−f(Y_k)) have the same joint law over k and f, so the expected suprema coincide.
  <- Linearity of the Lebesgue integral [proof]: Splits E sup∑ε_k(f(Y_k)−f(X_k)) into two identical Rademacher suprema (Lemma 7.4).
  <- Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem [proof]: With an integrable envelope, pointwise limits f_n→f in the countable subclass give Ef_n(X)→Ef(X), so all suprema equal suprema over the countable subclass.
  explains in van-handel-probability-high-dimension-2016, §7.1, Lemmas 7.3–7.4 — Symmetrization stated with f(X_k)−μf; measurability ignored in the text.

weight-two-hecke-ramanujan-bound — Ramanujan bound for weight-two Hecke operators [theorem]
  For p∤N, every eigenvalue of the usual degree-(p+1) Hecke correspondence on weight-two cuspidal differentials of the level-N modular curve has absolute value at most2√p. On X(N) for p≡1 mod N this is the determinant-p correspondence congruent to I modulo N.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: False
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Divisibility of integers [statement]: The hypothesis is p∤N.
  <- Eigenvalue of a linear endomorphism [statement]: The bound concerns the eigenvalues of T_p on the space of cuspidal differentials.
  <- Modulus of a complex number [statement]: The conclusion is |λ|≤2√p.
  <- Hecke correspondence on a full-level modular curve [statement]: The final sentence identifies the operator on X(N) for p≡1 mod N with the determinant-p correspondence congruent to I mod N.
  <- Eichler–Shimura congruence relation [proof]: On the reduction at a good prime, T_p=Π_p+Π_p′ (Milne Theorem 10.3; DDT Theorem 1.29 for Γ₁(N) with the diamond operator), so a_p=α+ᾱ for Frobenius eigenvalues α.
  <- Riemann hypothesis for curves over finite fields [proof]: The Frobenius eigenvalues α on the reduced Jacobian have |α|=√p, giving |a_p|=|α+ᾱ|≤2√p.
  <- Tate module of an abelian variety [proof]: The comparison is made through the ℓ-adic representation of correspondences on T_ℓ of the Jacobian, unchanged under good reduction.
  <- Good reduction of X₁(N) away from the level [proof]: The argument at every p∤N needs good reduction of the modular curve and its Jacobian at p (Igusa); Milne's footnote states this for X₀(N).

stable-kernel-random-continuous-test-theorem — Random continuous tests for stable convergence of probability kernels [theorem]
  If probability kernels µ_n on a Polish space converge stably to µ, then E∫F(ω,x)µ_n(ω,dx)→E∫F(ω,x)µ(ω,dx) for every jointly measurable F continuous in x with E sup_x|F(ω,x)|<∞. Stable convergence means convergence first for tests a(ω)f(x), with a bounded measurable and f bounded continuous.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Stable convergence of random probability kernels [statement]: The retained precise mathematical statement/definition uses these immediate inputs; proof inputs are separately classified.
  <- Expectation of an integrable real random variable [statement]: The retained precise mathematical statement/definition uses these immediate inputs; proof inputs are separately classified.
  <- Prokhorov’s theorem on Polish spaces [proof]: The mean laws converge weakly and hence form a tight family. Truncate the integrable random envelope, then choose a compact K with uniformly small mean mass outside it. On K approximate F by a finite deterministic continuous partition of unity at a δ-net, with random coefficients F(ω,x_j). Metric bump functions, normalized using the distance to K as an extra outside weight, provide bounded globally continuous weights. For each ω its continuous restriction to K is uniformly continuous, so the expected uniform approximation error tends to zero by dominated convergence. Stable convergence applies to each random coefficient times a deterministic weight. The outside-K bound and envelope truncation complete the argument. This supplies the random-composed-test step in the invariant measure proof without assuming it in the definition of stable convergence.
  <- Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem [proof]: The mean laws converge weakly and hence form a tight family. Truncate the integrable random envelope, then choose a compact K with uniformly small mean mass outside it. On K approximate F by a finite deterministic continuous partition of unity at a δ-net, with random coefficients F(ω,x_j).   For a connected reductive group G over a field k, two parabolic k-subgroups conjugate under G(k̄) are conjugate under G(k). Consequently, for a parabolic P, G(k)/P(k)→(G/P)(k) is bijective.

rational-primitive-nilpotent-unitary-decomposition — Rational primitive decomposition of a nilpotent unitary action [theorem]
  A unitary action of a finitely generated nilpotent group G decomposes orthogonally into invariant summands, each the closed orthogonal span of rational blocks K_F indexed by conjugates of an isolated subgroup F≤G. Here K_F is the closure of the vectors with finite F-orbit; G permutes the blocks, the stabilizer of K_F is N_G(F), elements of N_G(F) outside F have no nonzero power-fixed vector on K_F, and elements outside the normalizer have infinite block orbits. For every E≤G, the closure of its finite-orbit vectors in such a summand is the closed span of the K_F with E⊆F.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Finitely generated group [statement]: The acting group G is finitely generated.
  <- Unitary representation of a topological group [statement]: G acts by unitary operators on a Hilbert space (a unitary representation of the discrete group G, continuity being automatic).
  <- Isolated subgroup of a nilpotent group [statement]: The blocks are indexed by the conjugates of an isolated (closed) subgroup F; G nilpotent is inherited through this definition.
  <- Normalizer of a subgroup [statement]: The stabilizer of the block K_F is N_G(F), and elements outside N_G(F) have infinite block orbits.
  <- Group action on a set [statement]: G permutes the family of blocks; stabilizers and orbits of this action, and finite F-orbits of vectors, appear in the statement.
  <- Orthogonal direct-sum decomposition of a Hilbert space [statement]: H is an orthogonal sum of closed invariant summands, each the orthogonal sum of pairwise orthogonal blocks (G is countable, so the families are countable).
  <- Linear span of a set of vectors [statement]: Each summand, and the closure of H_rat(E) in it, is a closed linear span of blocks K_F.
  <- Isolator of a subgroup of a nilpotent group [proof]: §2.5: {T:T^m u=u for some m} is the closure of the stabilizer of u, a subgroup by Lemma 1.16.
  <- Finite index of the subgroup generated by generator powers [proof]: Lemma 2.6(a): H_rat(H)=∩_(P∈H)H_rat(P), using Lemma 1.12.
  <- Subgroups of finitely generated nilpotent groups are finitely generated [proof]: §2.7 chooses a maximal subgroup H with H_rat(H)≠0 via Lemma 1.9 (ascending chains of subgroups stabilize, equivalently every subgroup of a finitely generated nilpotent group is finitely generated).
  <- Normalizer tower condition in a nilpotent group [proof]: Proposition 2.8(d): T∈N^k(H)∖N^(k−1)(H) for some k≤c, the base of the induction proving T H_rat(H)⊥H_rat(H).
  <- The normalizer of an isolated nilpotent subgroup is isolated [proof]: Proposition 2.8(d) and §2.10 use that N(H) and N(F) are closed (Proposition 1.18), giving pairwise orthogonal Qⁿu and infinite block orbits.
  <- Von Neumann mean ergodic theorem for a unitary operator [proof]: Proposition 2.8(c),(d): T^m without nonzero fixed vectors on H_rat(H) gives C-lim T^(mn)u=0, used to show ⟨Tu,v⟩=0.
  <- Zorn’s lemma [proof]: Theorem 2.12 exhausts H by rationally-primitive invariant summands using Zorn’s lemma.

rational-representation-affine-algebraic-group — Rational representation of an affine algebraic group [definition]

implicit-function-theorem-real — Real implicit function theorem [theorem]
  If a Cᵏ map F:U⊆ℝⁿ×ℝᵐ→ℝᵐ, k≥1, vanishes at(a,b) and its derivative in the second variable is invertible there, then near(a,b) the zero set of F is uniquely the graph of a Cᵏ map y=g(x).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- C^k map between Euclidean open sets [statement]: Both F and the implicit solution g are C^k maps of open Euclidean sets.
  <- Invertible square matrix [statement]: The hypothesis is invertibility of that m×m derivative matrix at (a,b).
  <- Topology induced by a metric [statement]: U is open in ℝⁿ×ℝᵐ=ℝⁿ⁺ᵐ and the conclusion holds on open neighbourhoods of (a,b).
  <- Inverse function theorem in Euclidean space [proof]: Apply the inverse function theorem to F̃(x,y)=(x,F(x,y)); its inverse G=(G₁,G₂) gives g(x)=G₂(x,0). The catalogue inverse function theorem includes C^k regularity of the inverse, so g is C^k.
  <- Continuous partial derivatives and continuous Fréchet differentiability [proof]: The C^k hypothesis is given by continuous partials; the proof uses that F and F̃ are continuously Fréchet differentiable with derivative given by the Jacobian blocks.
  <- Rank–nullity theorem [proof]: The block derivative of F̃ is shown injective, hence invertible as a square linear map.
