uniform-subgroup-to-lattice-nilpotent — Reduction of a uniform nilpotent subgroup to a lattice [theorem]
  If L is a connected simply connected nilpotent Lie group and Λ is closed and cocompact, then Λ⁰ is a closed connected normal subgroup of L, L/Λ⁰ is connected simply connected nilpotent, and Λ/Λ⁰ is a discrete cocompact subgroup of L/Λ⁰. The resulting compact homogeneous space is naturally L/Λ.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: False
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Real Lie group [statement]: L is a nilpotent real Lie group.
  <- Nilpotent group [statement]: L and L/Λ⁰ are nilpotent.
  <- Simply connected topological space [statement]: L and L/Λ⁰ are simply connected.
  <- Coset of a subgroup [statement]: L/Λ is the coset space of Λ.
  <- Quotient topology [statement]: Cocompactness and the identification of homogeneous spaces use the quotient topology on coset spaces.
  <- Connected component of a topological space [statement]: Λ⁰ is the identity component of Λ.
  <- Quotient of a group by a normal subgroup [statement]: L/Λ⁰ and Λ/Λ⁰ are quotient groups.
  <- Discrete subgroup of a locally compact group [statement]: Λ/Λ⁰ is a discrete subgroup of L/Λ⁰.
  <- Adjoint representation of a real Lie group [proof]: Normality of Γ⁰ is tested through Ad_a: a^{−t}Γ⁰a^t=Γ⁰ iff Ad_{a^t}(L)=L for the tangent space L of Γ⁰.
  <- Adjoint exponential formula for a Lie group [proof]: Ad_a is unipotent and the entries of Ad_{a^t} are polynomials in t, from Ad(exp X)=e^{ad X} with nilpotent ad X.
  <- Nilpotent Lie algebra [proof]: The Lie algebra of a nilpotent Lie group is nilpotent, so ad X is nilpotent and Ad_a upper unitriangular in a suitable basis.
  <- Exponential of a nilpotent endomorphism in characteristic zero [proof]: Ad_{a^t}=exp(t ad X) is a finite sum, so the invariance condition is polynomial in t.
  <- Bound on the number of distinct polynomial roots [proof]: The polynomial condition P_a(t)=0 holds for all t∈ℤ, hence P_a≡0 and a^{−t}Γ⁰a^t=Γ⁰ for all real t.

regular-conditional-distribution-polish — Regular conditional distribution for a Polish-valued random variable [theorem]
  If X takes values in a Polish spaceE and G⊆F is a sub-σ-algebra, there is a G-measurable probability kernel K(ω,·) with∫f,dK(ω)=E[f(X)|G](ω) almost surely for every bounded Borel f. It is unique up to a common null set. Equivalently a probability measure on a product with Polish second factor disintegrates into its first marginal and such conditional probabilities.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Probability kernel between measurable spaces [statement]: The retained precise mathematical statement/definition uses these immediate inputs; proof inputs are separately classified.
  <- Conditional expectation given a σ-algebra [statement]: The retained precise mathematical statement/definition uses these immediate inputs; proof inputs are separately classified.
  <- Polish space [statement]: The retained precise mathematical statement/definition uses these immediate inputs; proof inputs are separately classified.
  <- Borel isomorphism theorem for standard Borel spaces [proof]: Use a Borel isomorphism to put the target in a Borel subsetB of[0,1]. For every rationalq choose conditional expectations of1_{X≤q}, obtained by Radon–Nikodym onG. Outside one null set for the countably many rational comparisons, these are nondecreasing; conditional monotone convergence supplies rational right limits. Extend them right-continuously to a distribution function with limits0,1 and use the Lebesgue–Stieltjes theorem to obtain a probability kernel. Measurability first holds on half-lines and extends to every Borel set by the pi–lambda theorem, which also extends the conditional-integral identity. The conditional probability ofBᶜ has expectation0, so after changing one null set the kernel is supported onB; transport it back toE. Uniqueness on a countable generating pi-system gives one common null set, rather than a different null set for every Borel set. The product-measure disintegration follows by conditioning on the first-coordinate sigma-algebra.
  <- Radon–Nikodym theorem for finite measures [proof]: Use a Borel isomorphism to put the target in a Borel subsetB of[0,1]. For every rationalq choose conditional expectations of1_{X≤q}, obtained by Radon–Nikodym onG. Outside one null set for the countably many rational comparisons, these are nondecreasing; conditional monotone convergence supplies rational right limits. regular-sequence-commutative-ring — Regular sequence in a commutative ring [definition]
  An ordered sequence f₁,…,f_r in a commutative ring R is regular if R/(f₁,…,f_r)≠0 and multiplication by f_i is injective on R/(f₁,…,f_(i−1)) for every i. The order and the nonzero final quotient are part of this convention.

module-regular-sequence — Regular sequence on a module [definition]
  For a module M over a commutative ring R, a sequence f₁,…,f_r in R is M-regular if multiplication by f_i is injective on M/(f₁,…,f_(i−1))M for each i and M/(f₁,…,f_r)M≠0. It is a sequence in an ideal I when all f_i lie in I; the order matters.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

stable-like-variable-order-regular-form — Regular symmetric stable-like form with measurable variable order [theorem]

  <- Fatou’s lemma [proof]: For a compactly supported Lipschitz u, near-diagonal radial integration is bounded by a compact integral of(2−α)⁻¹. The far part with one variable in the support is bounded by compact integrals ofα⁻¹ and the assumed outside integral of|x|^{−d−α(x)}. Thus the core energy is finite. The maximal difference-operator form is closed: from anL²-Cauchy/energy-Cauchy sequence extract an almost-everywhere subsequence using Chebyshev/Borel–Cantelli; the differences then converge pointwise for the jump measure, whileL² completeness and Fatou identify the energy limit. Restricting that closed form to the core gives closability. Unit truncation preserves the compact Lipschitz core and decreases every squared difference, so the closure is Markovian. Continuous compact functions areL²-dense by bounded clipping of theirL¹ approximations, and mollification approximates them uniformly by compactly supported Lipschitz functions. Consequently the closure is regular, with the chosen core dense in its form norm by construction. Symmetry comes from J: the displayed unsymmetrized kernel depending onα(x) alone is not asserted pointwise symmetric.

rellich-analytic-hermitian-eigendecomposition — Rellich analytic eigendecomposition for Hermitian matrix families [theorem]
  If A(t) is a square complex matrix whose entries are real analytic on an open real interval I and A(t)=A(t)* for every t∈I, then A(t)=U(t)D(t)U(t)* with U(t) unitary and D(t) real diagonal, all entries of U and D real analytic throughout I.

  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Hermitian complex matrix [statement]: A(t) is a Hermitian complex matrix for each t; U(t)* is the conjugate transpose.
  <- Real analytic function on an open Euclidean set [statement]: Hypothesis and conclusion require entries real analytic on I (an open subset of ℝ).
  <- Open interval in the real line [statement]: The parameter domain is an open real interval I (the theorem also allows unbounded intervals).
  <- Unitary operator on a complex Hilbert space [statement]: U(t) is unitary for every t, i.e. a unitary operator on ℂⁿ (same convention as the Hermitian spectral theorem record).

  Let G be reductive over an algebraically closed field of characteristic not two, θ an involution, K=G^θ and Q={g∈G:θ(g)=g⁻¹}. For x∈Q, the conjugation orbit of x under the identity component K⁰ is closed in Q if and only if the G-conjugacy class of x is closed in G.

riemann-change-variables-compact-jordan — Riemann change of variables on a compact Jordan set [theorem]
  Let S⊂U⊂R^n be compact and Jordan measurable, with U open. If g:U→R^n is injective and C¹ and detDg is nonzero onS, then for every Riemann-integrable f on g(S), ∫_(g(S))f(y)dy=∫_S f(g(x))|detDg(x)|dx.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Compact topological space [statement]: S is compact.
  <- Riemann integral over a Jordan measurable set [both]: Both sides are Riemann integrals over the Jordan measurable sets S and g(S); the proof replaces them by box integrals of zero extensions.
  <- Continuously differentiable Euclidean map [statement]: g is continuously differentiable on U.
  <- Injective function [statement]: g is one-to-one.
  <- Jacobian matrix of a differentiable Euclidean map [both]: The Jacobian determinant J_g=det g′ is assumed nonzero on S and weights the integrand; the proof uses g′(x) and its inverse.
  <- Determinant of a square matrix [both]: |det Dg| appears in the formula; the proof compares box volumes through |det A|.
  <- Jordan measurability of injective C¹ images [proof]: The proof uses that g(S) (and the images g(R_j)) are Jordan measurable (Proposition 10.5.9), so the extension of f by zero is Riemann integrable and the right side makes sense.
  <- Additivity of the Riemann integral over disjoint Jordan sets [proof]: Proving the theorem on each P_j∩S and summing, and the final equality ∑_j∫_(g(R_j))f=∫_(g(S))f, use additivity over pieces whose overlaps are null.
  <- Linearity and almost-everywhere monotonicity of the Riemann integral over a Jordan set [proof]: The reduction f=f₊−f₋ uses linearity; the estimates ∑sup f·V(g(R_j))≥∑∫_(g(R_j))f use monotonicity; overlaps of measure zero do not change integrals.
  <- Lebesgue number lemma [proof]: The Lebesgue covering lemma (Lemma 7.4.10 of volume I) gives δ>0 with every ball B(y,δ), y∈S, inside some W_x.
  <- Darboux criterion for Riemann integrability [proof]: The proof chooses a box partition P with ε+∫_Sφ≥U(P,φ) and refines it, using the Darboux upper-sum description of the box Riemann integral.
  <- Adjugate identity and matrix inverse [proof]: Continuity of x↦g′(x)⁻¹ on S follows because the inverse is adj(g′(x))/det g′(x) with det g′ nonvanishing.
  <- Boundedness of continuous functions on compact spaces [proof]: ‖g′(x)⁻¹‖ is continuous on compact S, so bounded by some M>1.
  <- Minimum attainment for lower semicontinuous functions on compact sets [proof]: For each subbox R_j one chooses x_j with |J_g(x_j)|≤|J_g(x)| on R_j, since |J_g| is continuous on the compact R_j.
  <- Fundamental theorem of calculus for continuous integrands [proof]: g(y)=∫₀¹g′(ty)y dt is the fundamental theorem of calculus applied (componentwise) to t↦g(ty).
  <- Norm bound for a Banach-valued Riemann integral [proof]: ‖∫₀¹(g′(ty)y−y)dt‖≤∫₀¹‖g′(ty)y−y‖dt bounds ‖g(y)−y‖ by δε.
  <- Volume of the linear image of a box [proof]: Proposition 10.7.1 gives V(A(R̃_j))=|det A|V(R̃_j) for A=g′(x_j).
  <- Null-set preservation by locally Lipschitz maps [proof]: Boundaries of the subboxes are null and their images under the C¹ map g are null (Lebl’s Proposition 10.3.10 is the C¹ special case); this justifies that overlaps of the g(R_j) do not affect the integral.
  <- Lipschitz bound from a bounded Euclidean derivative [proof]: A C¹ map is Lipschitz on small balls (bounded derivative on a convex set; Lebl Lemma 10.3.9 via Proposition 8.4.2), which places g in the locally Lipschitz null-set theorem.
  <- Inverse function theorem in Euclidean space [proof]: The reverse inequality applies the estimate to g⁻¹ on g(S), which requires g⁻¹ to be C¹ near g(S).
  <- Chain rule for Fréchet derivatives [proof]: 1=J_(g∘g⁻¹)=J_g(g⁻¹(u))J_(g⁻¹)(u) comes from the chain rule.
  <- Multiplicativity of the determinant [proof]: The same identity uses det(AB)=det A det B; so does V(g(R_j))=|det A|V(g̃(R_j)) bookkeeping.
  explains in lebl-basic-analysis-ii-2026, Theorem 10.7.2 and proof, pp. 134–137 — Textbook statement and proof; not a priority claim.

weil-riemann-hypothesis-curves-finite-fields — Riemann hypothesis for curves over finite fields [theorem]

riemann-integral-jordan-set — Riemann integral over a Jordan measurable set [definition]
  For a bounded Jordan measurable S⊆ℝⁿ, a bounded f:S→ℝ is Riemann integrable on S if its extension by zero to a closed box R containing S is Riemann integrable on R; then ∫_S f is the integral of that extension, independent of R.

riemann-integral-box — Riemann integral over a box in ℝᵏ [definition]
  For a closed box B=[a₁,b₁]×⋯×[a_k,b_k]⊂ℝᵏ, a bounded f:B→ℝ is Riemann integrable with integral I if for every ε>0 there is δ>0 such that every partition of B into finitely many closed subboxes B_j of diameter less than δ, with any tags ξ_j∈B_j, satisfies |∑_j f(ξ_j)vol(B_j)−I|<ε, where vol(B_j) is the product of the side lengths of B_j. For k=1 this is the Riemann integral on an interval.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Euclidean space ℝᵈ [statement]: The integral is defined on a box in ℝᵏ and uses the diameters of subboxes for the mesh condition.
  <- Finite set [statement]: Riemann sums range over finite partitions of the box into subboxes.

riemann-surface — Riemann surface [definition]
  A Riemann surface is a connected Hausdorff second-countable topological space covered by coordinate neighborhoods homeomorphic to open subsets of ℂ, with holomorphic transition maps. The charts define holomorphic functions and maps; its complex dimension is one.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

riemann-zeta-function — Riemann zeta function [definition]
  The Riemann zeta function is ζ(s)=∑_{n≥1}n^{−s} for Re s>1, with its meromorphic continuation to ℂ, having a simple pole at1 and residue1. Its nontrivial zeros are the zeros with0<Re s<1, counted with multiplicity.

riemannian-metric-manifold — Riemannian metric on a smooth manifold [definition]
  A Riemannian metric g on a smooth manifold M is a symmetric C∞(M)-bilinear pairing of smooth vector fields into smooth functions which in every chart has the form g=∑g_ij dxⁱdxʲ with (g_ij(x)) a smooth positive definite symmetric matrix at each point. A Riemannian manifold is a smooth manifold with a Riemannian metric.

riemann-hurwitz-characteristic-zero-curves — Riemann–Hurwitz formula in characteristic zero [theorem]
  For a finite nonconstant morphism f:Y→X of smooth projective geometrically connected curves over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, let d be its degree and e_P the order of vanishing at P of the pullback of a local parameter at f(P). Then 2g(Y)−2=d(2g(X)−2)+∑_P(e_P−1).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Genus of a smooth projective curve [statement]: The named input specifies the objects in the statement or definition.
  <- Finite morphism of schemes [statement]: The named input specifies the objects in the statement or definition.
  <- Principal divisor on a smooth projective curve [statement]: e_P is the order ord_P, in the discrete valuation local ring at P, of the pullback of a local parameter; this valuation is the one defining principal divisors.
  <- Uniformizer of a discretely valued field [both]: A local parameter at f(P) is a uniformizer of the discrete valuation ring O_(X,f(P)); the proof computes dt=d(us^n) with uniformizers s,t.
  <- Characteristic of a field [both]: The hypothesis is characteristic zero; in the proof it makes every finite morphism separable (21.4.1) and every ramification tame, so Ω_(Y/X) has length e_P−1 at P.
  <- Left-exact cotangent sequence for a generically separable morphism [proof]: Proposition 21.4.2 gives the exact sequence 0→f*Ω_X→Ω_Y→Ω_(Y/X)→0 to which additivity of degree is applied.
  <- Degree of a coherent sheaf on a projective curve [proof]: Degree is additive in the exact sequence (Exercise 18.4.I), and the torsion sheaf Ω_(Y/X) has degree equal to its length h⁰, the degree of the ramification divisor.
  <- Riemann–Roch theorem for smooth projective curves [proof]: The degree of the canonical sheaf of a genus-g curve is 2g−2 (Riemann–Roch with D=K and its cohomological form), applied to Ω_X and Ω_Y.
  <- Pullback and pushforward of divisors under a finite curve map [proof]: Degrees of line bundles multiply by deg f under pullback by a finite morphism of curves (Exercise 18.4.G), applied to f*Ω_X.

riemann-roch-theorem-curves — Riemann–Roch theorem for smooth projective curves [theorem]
  Let C be a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g over a field k, K a canonical divisor (of a nonzero rational differential) and ℓ(D)=dim_k{f∈k(C)×:div f+D≥0}∪{0}. Then ℓ(D)−ℓ(K−D)=deg D+1−g for every divisor D. Cohomologically χ(O(D))=deg D+1−g and H¹(C,O(D)) is dual to H⁰(C,Ω¹(−D)), so g=dim H¹(C,O_C).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: False
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: False
  Prerequisite frontier: elementary ingredients not expanded here.
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

The greatest harmonic minorant bounds these Green potentials; their monotone limit and Harnack convergence give u=Gμ+h. Distributional Laplacians give uniqueness of the measure, and harmonic minorants give uniqueness of h. Apply positive-harmonic Poisson representation to h for the boundary-measure clause. rooted-tree — Rooted finitely branching tree [definition]
  A rooted tree is a connected acyclic graph with a distinguished root. It is finitely branching if every vertex has finitely many children, meaning adjacent vertices one edge farther from the root.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: formalized; estimated LOC: 921.0
    Evidence: Reviewed Mathlib 26573066084e6e2aa8526ea358bc43b66d96f970. SimpleGraph/Acyclic.IsTree (:58) literally means connected acyclic, so adding a chosen vertex gives the graph presentation. Order/SuccPred/Tree.RootedTree (:105) is the equivalent ancestor-order presentation: bottom is the root, PredOrder (:62–70 in Basic) makes pred b the greatest strict ancestor, and IsPredArchimedean (:34–36) reaches every ancestor by finitely many predecessor steps. Consequently each vertex has a unique finite parent chain to root; its undirected cover graph is connected and acyclic. Conversely unique finite root paths in a rooted tree give the ancestor order, greatest common prefix/meet and those predecessor axioms. Children are precisely a⋖x, equivalently pred x=a with x nonroot, so finite branching is exactly ∀a,{x|a⋖x}.Finite (the actual finite-cover predicate also used in Order/KonigLemma:64). Along a cover the root distance increments by one. This explicit mathematical equivalence resolves the prior bridge uncertainty; no separate Lean alias is required. Native root/subtree/parent API is supplied in the selected defining files. Source inspection only; no fresh Lean build or transitive axiom audit.
Search and boundary notes: Explicitly checked equivalent graph/ancestor-order meanings using finite unique root paths and greatest strict predecessor, not name matching. Reduced planar no-unary trees, arborescences with extra edge data and G-trees are excluded.

relative-roots-reductive-group — Roots of a reductive group relative to a split torus [definition]
  For a maximal split torus T of a connected reductive group G, the nontrivial characters occurring as weights in Ad on Lie G are the relative roots. A choice of minimal parabolic containing T specifies the positive roots; the simple roots are the positive roots not expressible as a sum of two positive roots.

rose-generalized-divisor-quasimodularity — Rose’s theta-derivative formula for generalized divisor sums [theorem]
  For a symmetric residue set S={ℓ₁,…,ℓ_s} modulo n and k≥1, the weight-2w part of Rose’s A_{S,n,k}(q) is a constant multiple of Ω_{S,n}(qⁿ)⁻¹∑_{i₁+⋯+i_s=2w}(2w;i₁,…,i_s)∏_jϑ^{(i_j)}_{ℓ_j/n−1/2}(qⁿ), where ϑ_r^{(t)}(τ)=q^{r²/2}((2πi)⁻¹∂_σ)^tϑ(τ,σ) at σ=rτ+1/2 and Ω_{S,n}=∏_{ℓ∈S}ϑ^{(δ_{ℓ,n})}_{ℓ/n−1/2}. Consequently A_{S,n,k} is quasimodular of mixed weight at most 2k for some congruence subgroup.

  Let P,Q be Markov kernels with τ_d(P^n)≤Cρ^n for n≥0, C≥1 and ρ<1. Suppose QV≤δV+L with V≥1,0≤δ<1, and κ=max(q₀(V),L/(1−δ))<∞. Put γ=sup_xW_d(P(x,·),Q(x,·))/V(x). Then W_d(p₀P^n,q₀Q^n)≤Cρ^nW_d(p₀,q₀)+Cγκ(1−ρ^n)/(1−ρ).

runge-approximation-theorem — Runge’s approximation theorem [theorem]
  If K⊂ℂ is compact and f is holomorphic on an open neighbourhood of K, then f is a uniform limit on K of rational functions whose poles lie outside K; the poles can be taken in a prescribed set meeting every bounded component of ℂ∖K, together with ∞.

salikhov-pi-irrationality-bound — Salikhov’s upper bound for the irrationality exponent of π [theorem]
  Put ψ(x)=Γ′(x)/Γ(x) for x>0 and χ=5−ψ(2/5)+ψ(1/3)+log5−(5/2)log2. Let t₃ be the positive real root and t₁ the upper-half-plane root of5t³−381t²−1525t−1875=0, and put h(t)=|t²+6t+25|³|t|^(3/2)/|25−t|⁵. Then the irrationality exponent ofπ satisfies μ(π)≤1−(χ+logh(t₃))/(χ+logh(t₁)), whose right-hand side is approximately7.606308520711.

weak-feller-semicontinuity-characterization — Semicontinuity characterization of weak Feller kernels [theorem]
  A Markov kernel P on a locally compact separable metric space is weak Feller if and only if x↦P(x,O) is lower semicontinuous for every open set O. Then for every probability (a_n) on the nonnegative integers, x↦∑_n a_nP^n(x,O) is lower semicontinuous for open O, and x↦∑_n a_nP^n(x,F) is upper semicontinuous for closed F.

  In a connected affine algebraic group over an algebraically closed field, every semisimple element lies in a maximal torus.

  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

  <- Geometrically connected affine algebraic group [statement]: G is connected (over an algebraically closed field, geometrically connected).
  <- Semisimple element of an affine algebraic group [both]: The hypothesis is semisimplicity; the proof uses that the Zariski closure of ⟨s⟩ acts diagonalizably.
  <- Maximal algebraic torus [both]: The conclusion is containment in a maximal torus; the proof takes a maximal torus T of a Borel subgroup.
  <- Borel subgroup of a connected affine algebraic group [proof]: Choose a Borel subgroup B containing s.
  <- Borel subgroups cover a connected algebraic group [proof]: Every element of G(k) lies in a Borel subgroup (Theorem 17.33(b), Corollary 17.34).

  <- Zariski topology on an affine variety [proof]: The closure is taken in the Zariski topology.
  <- Diagonalizable affine algebraic group [proof]: S is diagonalizable because every representation of S is diagonalizable.
  <- Torus decomposition of a connected solvable algebraic group [proof]: Theorem 16.33(d): the diagonalizable S⊂B is conjugate into the maximal torus T of the connected solvable B.

lp-separability-euclidean — Separability of Lᵖ on a Euclidean domain [theorem]
  For1≤p<∞ and a Lebesgue measurable subset Ω of Euclidean space, Lᵖ(Ω) is separable. Rational-valued simple functions built from a countable family of rational boxes, with finite truncations and restriction to Ω, give a countable dense family.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Lebesgue Lᵖ space [statement]: The assertion concerns the normed space Lᵖ(Ω) for 1≤p<∞.
  <- Lebesgue measure on Euclidean space [statement]: Ω is a Lebesgue measurable subset of ℝᵈ with the restricted Lebesgue measure.
  <- Separable metric space [statement]: Separability means a countable dense subset for the Lᵖ norm metric.
  <- Density of integrable simple functions in Lᵖ [proof]: The final step: indicators of finite-measure sets lie in the closed span V, and density of μ-simple functions gives V=Lᵖ.
  <- Dynkin’s π–λ theorem [proof]: D_n={G: 1_{G∩E_n}∈V} is a Dynkin system containing the countable generating algebra, hence the whole σ-algebra.
  <- Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem [proof]: Closure of D_n under increasing unions and indicator approximations 1_{F∩E_n}→1_F use dominated convergence in Lᵖ.
  <- σ-finite measure [proof]: The proof exhausts Ω by sets E_n of finite measure; Lebesgue measure on Ω is σ-finite.
  <- Countable union of countable sets [proof]: The algebra generated by countably many rational boxes, and the rational linear combinations of the resulting indicators, are countable.
  <- Rational number [proof]: Rational coefficients (and rational box corners) give a countable family that is dense among real combinations.

  <- Compact metric spaces are separable [proof]: Proposition 2.8: choose a countable dense set (x_n) in K, “such a set exists by compactness”.
  <- Real Stone–Weierstrass theorem [proof]: The functions d_n(x)=d(x,x_n) separate points; the unital algebra they generate is dense by Theorem 2.5 (real case; the complex case adds closure under conjugation).
  <- Countability of the rational numbers [proof]: Rational (or ℚ+iℚ) linear combinations of finite products of the d_n form a countable set.
  <- Countable union of countable sets [proof]: The set of finite products of countably many generators, and of their finite rational combinations, is a countable union of countable sets.
  <- Density of the rationals in the reals [proof]: Replacing real coefficients by nearby rationals shows the countable set is dense in the generated algebra, hence in C(K).
  explains in van-neerven-functional-analysis-2e-arxiv, Proposition 2.8, p.42 — C(K) separable iff K metrisable; the metrisable ⇒ separable direction inspected for cone-085.

  <- Convergence of a sequence in a metric space [statement]: Requires sequences s_n in the metric index space T converging to t; supplies metric-space.
  <- Countable set [statement]: The approximating index set T₀ is countable.
  <- Limit of a real sequence [statement]: Requires convergence of the real sequence X_{s_n}(ω) to X_t(ω).

shafarevich-finiteness-curves — Shafarevich finiteness for curves of fixed genus [theorem]
  For a number field K, a finite set S of finite places, and an integer g≥2, there are only finitely many K-isomorphism classes of smooth projective geometrically connected curves of genus g with good reduction outside S.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Genus of a smooth projective curve [statement]: The named input specifies the objects in the statement or definition.
  <- Good reduction of a smooth projective curve [statement]: The named input specifies the objects in the statement or definition.
  <- Faltings’s Shafarevich finiteness for polarized abelian varieties [proof]: Faltings deduces Korollar 1 from Satz 6 with d=1: finitely many principally polarized abelian varieties of dimension g over K with good reduction outside S.
  <- Torelli theorem for curves of genus at least two over a perfect field [proof]: The rational Torelli theorem makes C↦(J(C),θ_C) injective on K-isomorphism classes of curves of genus g≥2 (K perfect).
  <- Good reduction of the Jacobian of a curve with good reduction [proof]: If C has good reduction at v then so does J(C), so the Jacobians land among principally polarized abelian varieties with good reduction outside S.
  <- Jacobian of a pointed smooth projective curve [proof]: Each curve is sent to its Jacobian with its canonical principal polarization. The catalogue record is the pointed construction; over K the Jacobian exists without a rational point and is independent of base point (see unresolved note).

shafarevich-finiteness-elliptic-curves — Shafarevich finiteness for elliptic curves [theorem]
  For a number field K and a finite set S of its finite places, only finitely many K-isomorphism classes of elliptic curves have good reduction at every place outsideS.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Place of a number field [statement]: S is a finite set of finite places of K.
  <- Reduction type of an elliptic curve over a local field [statement]: Good reduction at v means nonsingular reduction of a minimal integral Weierstrass equation over the completion K_v.
  <- Finiteness of the ideal class group of a number field [proof]: Enlarging S by finitely many primes representing the finite class group makes R_S a principal ideal domain.
  <- S-ideal class group of a number field [proof]: The class number of R_S is that of the S-ideal class group, which becomes trivial after enlarging S.
  <- S-minimal short Weierstrass model over a principal ring of S-integers [proof]: Proposition VIII.8.7 gives each curve an S-integral short model whose discriminant lies in R_S^× when the curve has good reduction outside S.
  <- Finite generation of the S-unit group [proof]: The finitely generated group R_S^× has finite quotient R_S^×/(R_S^×)¹², splitting the curves into finitely many classes Δ_i=CD_i¹².
  <- Siegel’s theorem on S-integral points of an elliptic curve [proof]: Each curve gives an S-integral point (−12A_i/D_i², 72B_i/D_i³) on y²=x³+27C; Siegel’s theorem leaves finitely many.
  <- Isomorphism between short Weierstrass models [proof]: Equal invariants A_i/D_i², B_i/D_i³ give an isomorphism (x,y)↦(u²x,u³y) between the curves.

siegel-modular-form-character — Siegel modular form with a character [definition]
  For a group homomorphism v:Sp₂g(ℤ)→ℂ^× and an integer k, a holomorphic F:ℍ_g→ℂ with F((AZ+B)(CZ+D)⁻¹)=v(M)det(CZ+D)^kF(Z) for all M=[[A,B],[C,D]]∈Sp₂g(ℤ), with the usual cusp condition when g=1. Trivial v gives ordinary Siegel modular forms. For g=2 the abelianization of Sp₄(ℤ) has order two, so there is exactly one nontrivial character, with values ±1.

siegel-walfisz-theorem — Siegel–Walfisz theorem [theorem]
  For every A>0 there is c_A>0 such that ψ(x;q,a)=∑_(n≤x,n≡a (q))Λ(n) satisfies ψ(x;q,a)=x/φ(q)+O_A(x exp(−c_A√log x)) uniformly for x≥2, moduli q≤(log x)^A and residues a coprime to q. The implied constants are ineffective, since the proof uses Siegel’s bound for exceptional real zeros.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: False
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: False

singer-negative-schwarzian-attracting-cycle-theorem — Singer’s attracting-cycle theorem for negative Schwarzian maps [theorem]
  For a C³ interval map with negative Schwarzian derivative wherever its derivative is nonzero, the immediate basin of each attracting periodic orbit contains a critical point or an endpoint of the interval.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Schwarzian derivative of a C³ real function [both]: Statement: the hypothesis Sf<0 wherever f′≠0. Proof: the contradiction is obtained from Sf^{2n}<0.
  <- Hyperbolic attracting periodic orbit of an interval map [both]: Statement: the theorem concerns an attracting periodic orbit, |(fⁿ)′(p)|<1. Proof: 0<Df^{2n}(p)<1 at the attracting point while Df^{2n}≥1 at the fixed boundary points of T.
  <- Immediate basin of an attracting periodic orbit [both]: Statement: the conclusion locates a critical point or an endpoint in the immediate basin. Proof: T is the component of the basin containing p and fⁿ(T)⊆T, fⁿ(∂T)⊆∂T.
  <- Composition rule for the Schwarzian derivative [proof]: Corollary 0.3: Sf<0 implies Sf^{2n}<0, needed to apply the minimum principle to f^{2n}.
  <- Minimum principle for maps with negative Schwarzian derivative [proof]: If Df^{2n} has no zero on T, |Df^{2n}| would have an interior local minimum in T, contradicting Lemma 0.4.
  <- Chain rule for Fréchet derivatives [proof]: Dfⁿ(x)=∏_{j<n}Df(f^jx), so a zero of Dfⁿ in T gives a critical point f^j(x) in the immediate basin f^j(T) of f^j(p).
  <- Structure of open subsets of the real line [proof]: Basins are open and nonempty open subsets of ℝ are countable disjoint unions of open intervals, so the immediate basin component T is an open interval.
  <- Extreme value theorem on a compact real interval [proof]: Moving across T, Df^{2n} goes from ≥1 to <1 and back to ≥1, so the continuous function |Df^{2n}| attains an interior local minimum on a compact subinterval.
  explains in newhouse-math840-schwarzian-2005, Theorem 0.5 and proof, pp. 10-4 to 10-6 — Lecture-note proof of Singer’s theorem; credited to D. Singer.

geometric-drift-skeleton-inheritance — Skeleton inheritance of geometric drift [theorem]
  For a ψ-irreducible aperiodic Markov chain, if V≥1, a petite set C, β>0 and b<∞ satisfy PV≤(1−β)V+b1_C, then for every m≥1 the m-skeleton P^m satisfies P^mV≤ρV+b′1_{C′} with ρ<1, b′<∞ and a set C′ petite for P^m. Consequently a set that is f-geometrically regular for the chain is f-geometrically regular for every skeleton.

skew-product-discrete-random-dynamical-system — Skew product of a discrete random dynamical system [definition]
  For a discrete random dynamical system φ over a measure-preserving map θ on Ω, the skew product is Φ(ω,x)=(θω,φ(1,ω,x)); its iterates are Φⁿ(ω,x)=(θⁿω,φ(n,ω,x)). A probability on Ω×X invariant under Φ and having environmental marginal Q is an invariant joint law; in standard Borel spaces it is equivalently Q(dω)π_ω(dx) for an invariant random probability kernel.

skorohod-representation-polish — Skorohod representation theorem on a Polish space [theorem]
  If probability measures µ_n converge weakly to µ on a Polish space, they can be realized as laws of random variables X_n,X on one probability space with X_n→X almost surely.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Weak convergence of probability measures on a metric space [both]: The hypothesis is μ_n⇒μ; the proof uses it on finitely many μ-continuity sets.
  <- Polish space [statement]: The theorem is stated on a Polish space (Sagitov assumes only that μ has separable support, which holds on a Polish space).
  <- Random element of a measurable space [both]: The conclusion constructs random elements X_n,X of the space on one probability space; the proof builds them from auxiliary random elements.
  <- Pushforward measure [both]: μ_n and μ are the laws (pushforwards of the probability) of X_n and X; Step 4 checks P(X_n∈A)=μ_n(A).
  <- Almost-everywhere convergence of measurable functions [statement]: The conclusion is X_n→X almost surely in the metric of the space.
  <- Portmanteau theorem for probability measures [proof]: Weak convergence gives μ_n(B)→μ(B) for μ-continuity sets B (limsup over the closure and liminf over the interior), used to choose n_j with μ_n(B_i^j)≥(1−ε_j)μ(B_i^j).
  <- Boundary of a subset of a topological space [proof]: The partition sets are chosen with μ(∂B_i)=0, using balls whose boundary spheres carry no mass.
  <- Lindelöf property of separable metric spaces [proof]: The separable support is covered by countably many of the chosen small balls.
  <- Existence of countable product probability measures [proof]: One probability space carries independent X, Y_n, Y_ni, Z_n and ξ with the prescribed laws (Sagitov cites Kolmogorov extension, Theorem 2.16; the actual use is a countable product of the prescribed laws).
  <- Independent family of random elements [proof]: Independence of X, Y_ni, Z_n and ξ is used to compute P(X_n∈A) as a mixture equal to μ_n(A).
  <- Uniform distribution on the unit interval [proof]: The randomizing variable ξ is uniform on [0,1], P(ξ≤ε)=ε.
  <- Conditional probability given an event [proof]: The auxiliary variables have the conditional laws μ_n(·|B_i^m).
  <- First Borel–Cantelli lemma [proof]: Since ∑P(E_j^c)<∞, almost surely all but finitely many E_j occur, on which X_n and X lie in a common partition set of small diameter.

smirnov-maximum-principle — Smirnov maximum principle [theorem]
  If F belongs to the Smirnov class on the unit disk and its radial boundary values satisfy |F*|≤M almost everywhere for a finite M≥0, then F is bounded analytic and |F(z)|≤M throughout the disk.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Smirnov class on the unit disk [both]: The Smirnov hypothesis is necessary; an arbitrary analytic quotient with bounded boundary values does not suffice.
  <- Poisson majorization of the logarithm of a bounded analytic function [proof]: WriteF=g/a with g,a∈H∞ and a outer. ForM>0, subtract the outer Poisson log-modulus equality for a from Poisson log-majorization for g. The boundary bound gives log|F(z)|≤logM. IfM=0, g has zero boundary values almost everywhere and the Hardy boundary norm formula forcesg=0. This proves the assertion without assumingF itself bounded beforehand.
  <- Poisson formula for the logarithm of an outer function [proof]: WriteF=g/a with g,a∈H∞ and a outer. ForM>0, subtract the outer Poisson log-modulus equality for a from Poisson log-majorization for g. The boundary bound gives log|F(z)|≤logM.   <- Boundary norm formula for Hardy H∞ [proof]: WriteF=g/a with g,a∈H∞ and a outer. ForM>0, subtract the outer Poisson log-modulus equality for a from Poisson log-majorization for g. The boundary bound gives log|F(z)|≤logM. IfM=0, g has zero boundary values almost everywhere and the Hardy boundary norm formula forcesg=0. This proves the assertion without assumingF itself bounded beforehand.

  <- Smooth function on a Euclidean sphere [statement]: Smoothness is specified on the support function; a vague boundary-smoothness hypothesis is not substituted.
  <- Spherical cosine transform [statement]: Smoothness is specified on the support function; a vague boundary-smoothness hypothesis is not substituted.
  <- Invertibility of the cosine transform on smooth even functions [proof]: Invert the cosine transform on the even smooth support function to obtain an even smooth densityg. Splitg=g₊−g₋ into positive and negative continuous parts. Add the same positive constant density to both parts, ensuring full-dimensional bodies. Their positive generating measures yield zonoidsL,M, andh_K=h_L−h_M givesK+M=L. This directly proves the representation needed on the smooth approximation class.
  <- Generating-measure representation theorem for symmetric zonoids [proof]: Invert the cosine transform on the even smooth support function to obtain an even smooth densityg. Splitg=g₊−g₋ into positive and negative continuous parts. Add the same positive constant density to both parts, ensuring full-dimensional bodies. Their positive generating measures yield zonoidsL,M, andh_K=h_L−h_M givesK+M=L. This directly proves the representation needed on the smooth approximation class.

smooth-vector-lie-group-representation — Smooth vector of a Lie group representation [definition]
  For a continuous representation π of a real Lie group G on a locally convex space V and X in the Lie algebra of G, set dπ(X)v=lim_{t→0}(π(exp tX)v−v)/t when the limit exists. A vector v is smooth if all iterated derivatives dπ(X₁)⋯dπ(X_k)v exist for every k and all X_i; the smooth vectors form the subspace V^∞.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

  <- Locally convex topological vector space [statement]: The limit defining dπ(X)v is taken in the locally convex topology of V.

snell-envelope-cadlag-positive-lp-reward — Snell envelope decomposition for a càdlàg reward with integrable positive maximum [theorem]
  On a usual filtration over [0,T], let a real adapted càdlàg reward R have E(sup_tR_t^+)^p<∞ for some p>1 and terminal R_T in Lp. Its stopping value U_t=esssup_(τ≥t)E[R_τ|F_t], with extended expectations when the negative part is not integrable, has a càdlàg class-D version and decomposition U=U₀+N−A with N a UI càdlàg martingale and A predictable càdlàg nondecreasing starting at0. It is the least class-D supermartingale dominating R; U_T=R_T and ∫₀ᵀ(U_(s−)−R_(s−))dA_s=0. Moreover sup|U| lies in Lp.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

Under Hilbert-space identifications this is the usual adjoint range condition, with constant factors absorbed in w.

spectral-integral-projection-valued-measure — Spectral integral with respect to a projection-valued measure [construction]
  For a projection-valued measure E on ℝ and a Borel function f:ℝ→ℂ, ∫f dE is the linear operator with domain D_f={x:∫|f|²d⟨E(·)x,x⟩<∞}.   <- Riesz–Dunford holomorphic functional calculus [statement]: The stated definition or selected proof of Spectral mapping theorem for holomorphic functional calculus uses holomorphic-functional-calculus; this is a first source pass, not a completed prerequisite review.
  <- Algebra homomorphism property of holomorphic functional calculus [proof]: InspectedShapiroLemma6.34/Theorem6.35. If μ is outside f(σ(T)), the holomorphic reciprocal of f−μ evaluates to its inverse. If μ=f(λ) with λ∈σ(T), write f(z)−μ=(z−λ)h(z), filling the removable value of h atλ. Multiplicativity gives commuting factors, so invertibility of f(T)−μ would force invertibility of T−λI, a contradiction. This argument works on a disconnected neighborhood too; no global factorization over all zeros is needed.
  <- Riemann’s removable singularity theorem [proof]: InspectedShapiroLemma6.34/Theorem6.35. If μ is outside f(σ(T)), the holomorphic reciprocal of f−μ evaluates to its inverse. If μ=f(λ) with λ∈σ(T), write f(z)−μ=(z−λ)h(z), filling the removable value of h atλ. Multiplicativity gives commuting factors, so invertibility of f(T)−μ would force invertibility of T−λI, a contradiction. This argument works on a disconnected neighborhood too; no global factorization over all zeros is needed.

cosine-transform-harmonic-multipliers — Spectral multipliers of the spherical cosine transform [theorem]
  For d≥3, the spherical cosine transform acts by scalar multipliers on each harmonic degree. Odd multipliers vanish; even multipliers are nonzero, and their absolute values are bounded above and below by positive dimension-dependent constants times(1+k)^{−(d+2)/2} on degree2k.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Spherical cosine transform [both]: The theorem describes the action of the spherical cosine transform; the proof writes it as the zonal integral transformation with kernel |t| (Groemer (3.4.2)).
  <- Spherical harmonic [both]: The multipliers act on each space of spherical harmonics of a fixed degree; the proof applies the transform to a harmonic H of degree n and uses that odd-degree harmonics are odd functions.
  <- Funk–Hecke formula [proof]: By the Funk–Hecke theorem the cosine transform multiplies each degree-n harmonic by an explicit one-dimensional integral of |t| against the dimension-d Legendre polynomial.
  <- Rodrigues formula for Gegenbauer polynomials [proof]: The Legendre polynomial is written by Rodrigues' formula (3.3.18), so that n−2 integrations by parts evaluate the multiplier integral.
  <- Integration by parts for C¹ real functions [proof]: Repeated integration by parts on [0,1] reduces ∫|t|·dⁿ/dtⁿ(1−t²)^{ϑ+n}dt to an evaluation of a derivative of order n−2 at t=0.
  <- Gegenbauer polynomial values at zero and one [proof]: The evaluation at t=0 is converted to the explicit product 1·3⋯(n−3)/((d+1)(d+3)⋯(d+n−1)) using the value of the Legendre polynomial at 0 (3.3.20); its value 1 at t=1 fixes the normalization.

spectral-theorem-unbounded-selfadjoint — Spectral theorem for a self-adjoint Hilbert-space operator [theorem]
  A densely defined self-adjoint operator A has a unique projection-valued measure E on ℝ such that A=∫λ dE(λ), with D(A)={x:∫λ²d⟨E(λ)x,x⟩<∞}; measurable functions of A are defined by the same spectral integration.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Densely defined self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space [statement]: The defining data or statement explicitly presuppose unbounded-self-adjoint-operator.
  <- Spectral integral with respect to a projection-valued measure [statement]: A=∫λdE(λ), its domain formula and measurable functions of A are spectral integrals.
  <- Herglotz representation of a bounded Herglotz function as a Borel transform [proof]: F_ψ(z)=⟨ψ,R_A(z)ψ⟩ is a Herglotz function with |F_ψ|≤‖ψ‖²/Im z, so it is the Borel transform of the spectral measure μ_ψ.
  <- Stieltjes inversion formula for the Borel transform of a measure [proof]: Uniqueness: the measures μ_{φ,ψ}, hence E, are determined by the resolvent through their Borel transforms.
  <- First resolvent identity [proof]: Holomorphy of F_ψ, the identity Im F_ψ(z)=Im z‖R_A(z)ψ‖², and the multiplicativity step of Lemma 3.6 use R(z)−R(z̃)=(z−z̃)R(z)R(z̃).
  <- Resolvent of a self-adjoint operator off the real axis [proof]: Non-real z lie in ρ(A), ‖R_A(z)‖≤1/|Im z| and R_A(z)*=R_A(z̄) give the growth bound and symmetry of F_ψ.
  <- Polarization identity for sesquilinear forms [proof]: Complex measures μ_{φ,ψ} are obtained from the μ_ψ by polarization.
  <- Finite complex measure [proof]: The sesquilinear forms s_Ω(φ,ψ)=μ_{φ,ψ}(Ω) are values of finite complex Borel measures.
  <- Riesz representation theorem for Hilbert-space functionals [proof]: A bounded sesquilinear form is represented by a bounded operator (Teschl Corollary 1.9, from the Riesz lemma), giving the operators P_A(Ω).
  <- Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem [proof]: Strong convergence P(f_n)→P(f) for bounded pointwise convergent f_n.
  <- Monotone convergence theorem for Lebesgue integrals [proof]: The adjoint domain argument shows f∈L²(μ_ψ) by monotone convergence.
  <- Approximation of nonnegative measurable functions by simple functions [proof]: Density of simple functions in bounded Borel functions extends P from simple to bounded Borel functions.
  <- Hilbert direct sum [proof]: Lemma 3.4 decomposes H as an orthogonal direct sum of cyclic subspaces H_ψn used to prove Lemma 3.5.
  <- Multiplication by a bounded measurable function on L² [proof]: On each cyclic subspace P(f) is unitarily equivalent to multiplication by f on L²(μ_ψ) (unbounded f via truncations), which proves the calculus rules of Lemma 3.5.
  <- Resolvent set and resolvent of a closed operator [proof]: The proof works with the resolvent R_A(z)=(A−z)⁻¹ of the closed operator A and identifies P_A((λ−z)⁻¹)=R_A(z).

  <- Riesz representation of C₀(X)* by complex Radon measures [proof]: Each functional f↦(f(T)x|y) on C(σ(T)) is represented by a unique complex Borel measure P_{x,y}; uniqueness of the representing measure gives sesquilinearity, P_{g(T)x,y}=gP_{x,y} and the uniqueness step of Proposition 9.14.
  <- Finite complex measure [proof]: The representing measures P_{x,y} are finite complex Borel measures with ‖P_{x,y}‖≤‖x‖‖y‖, integrated against bounded Borel functions.
  <- Riesz representation theorem for Hilbert-space functionals [proof]: Proposition 9.17: a bounded sesquilinear form (x,y)↦∫f dP_{x,y} is (Ax|y) for a unique bounded A with ‖A‖≤C, proved from the Riesz representation theorem; this defines f(T) for bounded Borel f.
  <- Polarization identity for sesquilinear forms [proof]: Φ(f)=f(T) is concluded from (Φ(f)x|x)=(f(T)x|x) by polarisation; uniqueness P_B=P̃_B likewise follows from equality of the quadratic forms.
  <- Complex Stone–Weierstrass theorem [proof]: Uniqueness (Proposition 9.14): polynomials in λ and λ̄ are dense in C(K), so the continuous calculi of two candidate measures agree.
  <- Spectrum of a bounded self-adjoint operator between its quadratic-form bounds [proof]: For self-adjoint T, σ(T)⊆[m,M]⊆ℝ (Theorem 8.11), so the measure constructed on B(σ(T)) is a projection-valued measure on the real line supported on the real spectrum.
  <- Bounded positive operator [proof]: Positivity of the scalar measures P_x uses that f(T)≥0 for nonnegative continuous f (Corollary 8.25), i.e. (f(T)x|x)≥0.

gerencser-hendrickx-rewired-cycle-gap — Spectral-gap bound for pure drift on randomly rewired cycle arcs [theorem]
  Let k arc lengths be independent Geometric(1/L) variables,with k,L→∞ and fixed 0<ρ_l<log L/log k<ρ_u<∞. For the pure drift chain that moves along arcs and chooses the next arc uniformly at endpoints, every γ>4 gives absolute spectral gap greater than 1/(L(log k)^γ) with high probability; the exceptional probability is O(k^(−c)L^(−d)) for any fixed c,d>0. Conditioning the total number of vertices to be n gives the same high-probability bound for the uniformly cut-cycle model with L=n/k.

  <- Addition theorem for spherical harmonics [proof]: The addition kernel reproduces each harmonic degree. Average it over the equator perpendicular tou. spherical-harmonic-decomposition-l2 — Spherical harmonic decomposition of L² of a sphere [theorem]
  The real Hilbert space L²(S^{n−1}) is the orthogonal sum of the finite-dimensional spaces of spherical harmonics of degrees k≥0; a polynomial of degree m restricts to a sum of harmonics of degrees at most m.

  <- Lebesgue Lᵖ space [statement]: The space decomposed is the real Lebesgue space L² of the sphere.
  <- Area measure on the Euclidean unit sphere [statement]: L²(S^{n−1}) is taken with respect to surface measure on the sphere.
  <- Spherical harmonic [both]: The summands are the spaces of spherical harmonics of each degree; the proof uses their orthogonality and that they span restrictions of polynomials.
  <- Finite-dimensional vector space [statement]: Each summand of a fixed degree is finite dimensional.
  <- Orthogonal direct-sum decomposition of a Hilbert space [both]: The conclusion is an orthogonal direct-sum decomposition; the proof verifies closedness, pairwise orthogonality and density of the span.
  <- Spherical polynomial [both]: The second clause concerns restrictions to the sphere of polynomials of degree m; their density in C(S) gives density of the span of spherical harmonics.
  <- Fischer decomposition of homogeneous polynomials [proof]: Every homogeneous polynomial of degree m is ∑|x|^{2j}p_{m−2j} with p_{m−2j} harmonic homogeneous, so its restriction to S is a sum of spherical harmonics of degrees ≤m.
  <- Green’s second identity [proof]: Applied on the unit ball to harmonic homogeneous p,q of degrees k<m, Green's identity and D_np=kp, D_nq=mq give (m−k)∫_Spq dσ=0.
  <- Real Stone–Weierstrass theorem [proof]: Restrictions of polynomials are uniformly dense in C(S).
  <- Density of compactly supported continuous functions in Radon Lᵖ [proof]: C(S) is dense in L²(S), and the L² norm is at most a constant times the sup norm, so uniform density gives L² density.
  <- Equivalence of norms in finite dimensions [proof]: Each H_m(S) is finite dimensional and hence closed in L²(S) (condition (a)).
  explains in axler-bourdon-ramey-harmonic-function-theory-2001, Theorem 5.12 — Selected proof exposition (complex-valued functions); not an origin claim.

serre-p-adic-v-stability — Stability of Serre p-adic modular forms under V [theorem]
  For a prime p, if f(q)=∑a_nq^n is a Serre p-adic modular form, then Vf(q)=f(q^p) is a Serre p-adic modular form. For nonzero forms V preserves their p-adic weight.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Weight of a Serre p-adic modular form [statement]: The statement says that V preserves the p-adic weight of nonzero forms.
  <- Hecke operators on classical modular forms [proof]: The classical T_p on rational level-one forms of weight k_i has q-coefficients a_(pn)+p^(k_i−1)a_(n/p); the proof writes f_i|V=p^(1−k_i)(f_i|T_p−f_i|U).
  <- Fixed-weight arithmetic and limits of Serre p-adic modular forms [proof]: f_i|U is p-adic of weight k_i (as a limit), the linear combination with f_i|T_p has weight k_i, and f|V=lim f_i|V has weight lim k_i=k.
  <- Von Staudt–Clausen theorem [proof]: To force |k_i|→∞ the approximants are multiplied by E_((p−1)p^i)≡1 mod p^(i+1), a congruence from v_p(B_h/h)=−1−v_p(h) for (p−1)|h.
  <- Fourier expansion of normalized level-one Eisenstein series [proof]: The congruence E_h≡1 uses the expansion E_h=1−(2h/B_h)∑σ_(h−1)(n)qⁿ.

tight-random-kernels-stable-compactness — Stable compactness of random probability kernels with tight mean laws [theorem]
  Let K_n be probability kernels on one probability space with Polish targetE. If their mean probability measuresν_n(A)=E[K_n(ω,A)] form a tight family, then some subsequence converges stably to a probability kernelK on the same base space.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

  <- Banach–Alaoglu theorem [proof]: Choose increasing compactE_m with mean mass≥1−2^{−m} for every kernel. At eachm choose a countable dense rational-linear test family inC(E_m), including constants, and consider all restricted kernel test integrals. These countably many random variables, for alln,m, generate a countably generated sub-sigma-algebraG. ItsL¹ is separable modulo null sets. Banach–Alaoglu andL¹/L∞ duality give a common diagonal weak-* subsequence for the test integrals onG. Positivity, linearity and mass≤1 pass to the limit outside a single null set by countability. Riesz–Markov yields measurable positive subprobability kernelsν_m supported onE_m. Comparing nonnegative tests on larger compacts givesν_m≤ν_{m+1}. Their increasing limit has mass≤1; its expected mass tends to1 by the uniform mean tail bound, so it is a probability kernel almost surely. Stable convergence first holds on each compact restriction. Uniform mean tails control the error by2^{−m} times the bounded test norms, proving it onE. For an arbitrary boundedF-measurable base testa, replace it byE[a|G] in all pairings; this extends convergence beyondG. This avoids falsely assuming the original base sigma-algebra is countably generated or applying sequential Banach–Alaoglu on a nonseparableL¹.

brownian-motion — Standard Brownian motion [definition]
  A continuous process B_t starting at zero with independent increments and B_t−B_s distributed N(0,t−s) for 0≤s<t. A d-dimensional standard Brownian motion has d independent standard components.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

standard-form-von-neumann — Standard form of a von Neumann algebra [definition]
  A standard form (M,H,J,P) of a von Neumann algebra M on H consists of a conjugate-linear isometric involution J of H and a self-dual cone P⊆H with JMJ=M′, JcJ=c* for every c in the center of M, Jξ=ξ for ξ∈P, and aJaJ(P)⊆P for a∈M. Every von Neumann algebra has a standard form, unique up to unitary equivalence (Haagerup); H is then written L²(M), with commuting right action ξ·a=Ja*Jξ.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

khayutin-bowen-separated-limit-state-entropy-bound — State-space entropy bound for limits with Bowen-ball separation [theorem]
  Let Γ be a lattice in a second-countable locally compact G, Y=Γ∖G with Haar probability m, K compact with open normalizer, X=Y/K and S(y)=ya⁻¹.   <- Pettis measurability theorem [proof]: Measurability of the sections x↦f̃(x,y), y↦f̃(x,y) follows from separable range and Pettis's theorem.
  <- Hahn–Banach norm-preserving extension theorem [proof]: Functionals on the separable closed span of the range are extended to E when applying Pettis's theorem.
  <- Minkowski’s inequality for integrals [proof]: Minkowski's inequality for integrals, applied twice, gives (2.12) and (2.15).
  <- Fatou’s lemma [proof]: Fatou's lemma gives completeness of the mixed-norm space and the a.e. limit (2.22).

stone-cech-compactification-discrete-semigroup — Stone–Čech compactification of a discrete semigroup [construction]
  For a discrete semigroup S, βS is the compact Hausdorff space of ultrafilters on S, containing S as a dense subset. bounded-rate-markov-piecing-out-theorem — Strong Markov piecing out at bounded-rate jumps [theorem]
  Let a nonexplosive right-continuous strong Markov process on a standard Borel state space be killed with bounded nonnegative measurable state rate r, and restarted after each killing from a measurable probability kernel K at its pre-killing state, using independent fresh copies. If r=0 at a state the choice of K there is immaterial; bounded rates rule out finite accumulation of killing times.

  On a bounded smooth domain, consider dX=[Δ(|X|^{m−1}X)+cX]dt+dW with m>1,c∈ℝ, zero Dirichlet conditions and covariance Q trace class onH⁻¹. Put p=m+1,V=Lᵖ,H=H⁻¹. strong-operator-topology-bounded-operators — Strong operator topology on bounded operators [definition]
  On the bounded linear operators X→Y between normed spaces, the strong operator topology is the coarsest topology making T↦Tx continuous for every x∈X; a net T_i converges to T exactly when ‖(T_i−T)x‖→0 for each x. For Hilbert spaces H→K this is the usual strong operator topology.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

discrete-subgroup-finite-dimensional-real-vector-space — Structure of discrete subgroups of a finite-dimensional real vector space [theorem]
  Every discrete subgroup Λ of a finite-dimensional real vector space V is generated over ℤ by a finite ℝ-linearly independent family; in particular Λ is a free abelian group of rank at most dim V. The quotient V/Λ is compact exactly when that family is a real basis of V.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Finite-dimensional vector space [statement]: The ambient V is a finite-dimensional real vector space.
  <- Euclidean space ℝᵈ [statement]: V carries the topology transported from ℝⁿ by any linear isomorphism; it is independent of the basis (Milne ANT p.73).
  <- Discrete subgroup of a locally compact group [statement]: Λ is a discrete subgroup of the locally compact group (V,+).
  <- Finitely generated group [statement]: Λ is generated over ℤ by a finite family.
  <- Quotient of an abelian group by a subgroup [statement]: V/Λ is the quotient group.
  <- Quotient topology [statement]: V/Λ carries the quotient topology.
  <- Closedness of locally compact subgroups [proof]: Proposition 1.1: the discrete subgroup G is closed in ℝᴺ.
  <- Heine–Borel theorem in finite-dimensional normed spaces [proof]: G∩P is a closed discrete subset of the compact parallelotope P, hence finite; ℝ^(N−r) is noncompact.
  <- Rational number [proof]: The finiteness of G∩P forces the coordinates λᵢ to be rational.
  <- Structure theorem for finitely generated modules over a PID [proof]: Applied to dG⊂∑ℤeᵢ to obtain an adapted ℤ-basis.
  <- Free abelian group [both]: The conclusion says Λ is free abelian of rank at most dim V; the proof compares free ranks of dG and G.
  <- Extension of a linearly independent family to a finite basis [proof]: Extending v₁,…,v_r to a basis identifies ℝᴺ/G with ℝ^(N−r)×(ℝʳ/ℤʳ).
  <- Finite-dimensional real torus [proof]: ℝʳ/ℤʳ is the compact torus factor of the quotient.
  <- Continuous image of a compact space [proof]: The quotient of a full lattice is the continuous image of a compact closed parallelotope.
  explains in clark-geometry-of-numbers-notes, §1.1 Theorem 1.2; §1.3 Proposition 1.6 — Exposition and proof; not a priority claim.

structure-theorem-finitely-generated-modules-pid — Structure theorem for finitely generated modules over a PID [theorem]
  Every finitely generated module M over a principal ideal domain R is isomorphic to Rʳ⊕R/(d₁)⊕⋯⊕R/(d_k) with nonzero nonunits d₁|d₂|⋯|d_k. The rank r and the ideals (d_i) are uniquely determined; in particular M is the direct sum of its torsion submodule and a free module of rank r.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Principal ideal domain [both]: Hypothesis on R; the proof uses principality throughout (Theorem 2.14 Step 2, Theorem 5.7).
  <- Finitely generated module over a commutative ring [both]: Hypothesis on M; the proof writes M as a quotient of Rⁿ via finitely many generators.
  <- Quotient module [both]: The cyclic summands are quotient modules R/(d_i); the proof presents M as Aⁿ/N.
  <- Rank of a finite free module over a commutative ring [both]: The free summand is Rʳ with r its rank; uniqueness of r uses well-definedness of rank (Lemma 1.1) applied to M/M_tors.
  <- Direct sum of modules over a commutative ring [statement]: M is isomorphic to a direct sum of modules and is the internal direct sum of its torsion submodule and a free submodule.
  <- Divisibility and units in a commutative ring [statement]: The invariant factors are nonzero nonunits with d₁|d₂|⋯|d_k, determined up to associates.
  <- Torsion submodule of a module over an integral domain [statement]: The statement names the torsion submodule M_tors.
  <- Submodules of a finite free module over a PID [proof]: The relation module N⊆Aⁿ is free of rank at most n (Theorem 2.2), as needed for aligned bases (Corollary 2.16).
  <- Elementary divisor theorem for submodules of a finite free module over a PID [proof]: Aligned bases of Aⁿ and N with a₁|⋯|a_m give Aⁿ/N≅⊕A/(a_j)⊕A^(n−m).
  <- Principal ideal domains are unique factorization domains [proof]: Uniqueness of the ideals (d_i) is read off prime by prime: irreducibles π generate maximal ideals and the π-exponents determine each d_i up to a unit.
  <- Dimension of a vector space [proof]: The invariants are dim_(A/(π)) πⁱ⁻¹T/πⁱT, which equal #{k: πⁱ|a_k} and are unchanged under isomorphism.
  <- Existence of a maximal ideal above a proper ideal [proof]: Lemma 1.1 proves invariance of rank by reducing modulo a maximal ideal of R.

parabolic-obstacle-supremum-stability — Supremum stability of the parabolic double-obstacle solution map [theorem]
  For fixed strictly separated continuous walls on the circle and Lipschitz drift f, subtract a continuous free driving field v from a reflected heat solution and write the remainder z. On each finite interval, changing v and the initial data changes z by at most C_T times their supremum-norm changes. The same estimate holds uniformly for the lower and upper penalized equations, independently of the penalty parameters.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Stochastic heat equation between two reflecting walls [statement]: The solution map concerns the reflected heat equation between two walls, with reflection measures and complementarity, written as z=u−v.
  <- Space of continuous real functions on a compact Hausdorff space [statement]: Changes are measured in the supremum norm on S¹×[0,T].
  <- Lipschitz composition in W¹,ᵖ [proof]: The comparison tests the equation for w=z^{ε,δ}−ẑ^{ε,δ}−k with w⁺; the positive part of a W^{1,2} function is W^{1,2}, with the a.e. chain rule.
  <- Lions–Magenes Hilbert-triple energy identity [proof]: Pairing w_t with w⁺ yields ½(d/dt)‖w⁺‖²_{L²}≤0, the energy identity in the Hilbert triple applied to the truncation.
  <- Nualart–Pardoux well-posedness for a one-wall stochastic heat equation [proof]: Lemma 2.4 passes the penalized estimate to the single-reflection problem by letting the lower penalty δ↓0, using the Nualart–Pardoux penalty construction of the one-wall solution.
  <- Existence for a smooth-forced parabolic double-obstacle problem [proof]: For smooth drivers w_n the penalized solutions converge (ε,δ↓0) to the double-obstacle variational solution. The uniform estimate then passes to the reflected remainder z, and to continuous drivers by sup-norm approximation.
  explains in otobe-two-walls-2006, Lemmas 2.3–2.4 and §2.3 — Interval form with zero initial data; proof inspected for cone-022; no priority claim.

surface-measure-c1-boundary — Surface measure on the boundary of a C¹ domain [definition]
  For a C¹ domain Ω⊂ℝⁿ, surface measure dS on ∂Ω is the restriction of (n−1)-dimensional Hausdorff measure to ∂Ω. Where ∂Ω is, after a rigid motion, the graph x_n=g(x′) of a C¹ function, it is the image of √(1+|∇g(x′)|²)dx′ under x′↦(x′,g(x′)).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

nonsplit-isogeny-character-sylow-image — Sylow image criterion from a nonsplit prime isogeny [theorem]
  Let E/F be elliptic over a number field, p≥5, and0→Φ→E[p]→Ψ→0 a nonsplit G_F-module sequence with one-dimensional charactersφ,ψ. If E has no cyclic F-isogeny of degree p², φψ⁻¹ has order≥3, and p divides[F(μ_(p²)):F], then the p-adic Tate image contains a Sylow pro-p subgroup of GL₂(ℤ_p).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

  <- Abelian group with a group action [statement]: Φ, E[p], Ψ are G_F-modules.
  <- Exact sequence of modules [statement]: The hypothesis is a nonsplit short exact sequence 0→Φ→E[p]→Ψ→0.
  <- One-dimensional character with values in a ring [statement]: φ,ψ are the 𝔽_p^×-valued characters on Φ and Ψ.
  <- Finite field [statement]: Characters take values in 𝔽_p^×.

  <- Root of unity [statement]: F(µ_(p²)) is generated by p²-th roots of unity.
  <- Dimension of a vector space [statement]: [F(µ_(p²)):F] is a field degree.
  <- Tate-module Galois representation of an elliptic curve [statement]: The conclusion concerns the p-adic Tate image.
  <- Sylow pro-p subgroup of a profinite group [statement]: The conclusion is containment of a Sylow pro-p subgroup of GL₂(ℤ_p).
  <- Schur–Zassenhaus theorem for profinite groups [proof]: Gives a subgroup Ω⊂G=Gal(F(E[p∞])/F) mapping isomorphically to Gal(K/F) complementing the pro-p group P.

szego-kernel-unit-disk — Szegő kernel of the unit disk [definition]
  For w in the unit disk, the Szegő (Cauchy) kernel is k_w(z)=1/(1−w̄z). It is the reproducing kernel of the Hardy space H²: ⟨f,k_w⟩=f(w) for f∈H², so ∥k_w∥²=1/(1−|w|²).

  For a connected reductive number-field group G of dimension d, choose an invariant F-rational gauge form and its standard local measures m_v. Let ρ_G be the Galois representation on X*(G)⊗C and r_G the leading nonzero Laurent coefficient of its finite-place Artin L-function at s=1. tangent-space-smooth-manifold — Tangent space of a smooth manifold [definition]
  For a point x of a smooth manifold M, T_xM is the real vector space of derivations at x: linear maps v:C^∞(M)→ℝ with v(fg)=v(f)g(x)+f(x)v(g). In a chart with coordinates x¹,…,xⁿ the partial derivatives ∂/∂x^i at x form a basis. A smooth map F induces dF_x:T_xM→T_(F(x))N, v↦(f↦v(f∘F)); a smooth path γ has velocity γ′(t)=dγ_t(d/dt).

chevalley-prime-to-p-tate-rank — Tate rank and Chevalley decomposition of a smooth commutative group [theorem]
  For a smooth connected commutative algebraic group G over a perfect field, its maximal connected affine subgroup is an extension of a torus of dimension t by a unipotent group of dimension u, and the quotient is an abelian variety of dimension b. For ℓ different from the characteristic, T_ℓG has rank t+2b, while dim G=t+u+b. A finite component group does not change the Tate rank.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True

  <- Unipotent affine algebraic group [both]: The affine part involves a unipotent group of dimension u, which contributes no prime-to-p torsion.
  <- Abelian variety [both]: The quotient by the affine part is an abelian variety of dimension b.

uniform-complex-sphere-tensor-moments — Tensor moments of a uniform complex unit vector [theorem]
  Ifw is uniform on the unit sphere ofℂⁿ andt is a positive integer, E(ww*)^(⊗t)=P_sym/binom(n+t−1,t), whereP_sym is the orthogonal projector onto tensors fixed by all factor permutations.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Uniform probability law on the complex unit sphere [both]: w is uniform on the complex unit sphere; the proof uses its unitary invariance.
  <- Symmetric subspace of a tensor power [both]: P_sym is the orthogonal projector onto the symmetric subspace; the proof uses w^(⊗t)∈Sym^t(ℂⁿ), so ρ=P_symρP_sym.
  <- Kronecker product of matrices [statement]: (ww*)^(⊗t) is the t-fold Kronecker power of the rank-one matrix ww*.
  <- Expectation of an integrable real random variable [both]: E(ww*)^(⊗t) is the entrywise expectation; linearity moves U^(⊗t) through it.
  <- Binomial coefficient [statement]: The normalization binom(n+t−1,t).
  <- Irreducibility of the symmetric subspace under the unitary group [proof]: Theorem 5: Sym^t(ℂⁿ) is irreducible under U↦U^(⊗t).
  <- Schur’s lemma for finite-dimensional complex representations [proof]: ρ=E(ww*)^(⊗t) commutes with every U^(⊗t), so its restriction to the irreducible Sym^t(ℂⁿ) is a scalar multiple of the identity there.
  <- Unitary operator on a complex Hilbert space [proof]: For unitary U, U^(⊗t)ρU^(⊗t)*=E((Uw)(Uw)*)^(⊗t)=ρ by unitary invariance.
  <- Irreducible linear representation of a group [proof]: Schur’s lemma is applied to the irreducible representation of U(n) on Sym^t(ℂⁿ).
  <- Dimension of a symmetric tensor power [proof]: tr P_sym=dim Sym^t(ℂⁿ)=binom(n+t−1,t) fixes the scalar.
  <- Trace of a square matrix [proof]: Normalization: tr(ww*)^(⊗t)=‖w‖^(2t)=1, so trρ=1.

toric-dual-discriminant-character-formula — Toric dual discriminant character formula [theorem]
  For a smooth projective toric embedding X_A over an algebraically closed field, with lattice polytope Q and dual hypersurface equation Δ_A, let µ be the generic degree of its conormal projection. The torus character of Δ_A is (1/µ)Σ_(facesΓ⊆Q)(−1)^codimΓ(dimΓ+1)∫_Γu dµ_Γ(u), where each face measure assigns volume one to a lattice unit simplex. In characteristic zero µ=1.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Projective toric variety of a lattice point configuration [statement]: The theorem concerns the projective toric variety X_A, its torus T̃ acting on K^A, and its lattice polytope Q.
  <- Projective dual variety and its discriminant [statement]: Δ_A is the equation of the dual hypersurface X_A^∨ and µ is defined from the conormal projection p₂:W_{X_A}→X_A^∨.
  <- Degree of a generically finite dominant morphism [statement]: µ is the degree of the generically finite map p₂.
  <- Face of a convex polytope [statement]: The sum runs over the faces Γ of Q with signs (−1)^{codim Γ} and weights dim Γ+1.
  <- Lebesgue measure on Euclidean space [statement]: µ_Γ is Lebesgue measure on the affine span of Γ normalized by the face lattice.
  <- Lebesgue integral [statement]: Each face contributes the vector-valued integral ∫_Γ u dµ_Γ(u).
  <- Characteristic of a field [statement]: The final clause distinguishes characteristic zero, where µ=1.
  <- Gelfand–Kapranov–Zelevinsky determinantal formula for the A-discriminant [proof]: The proof of Theorem 2.3 starts from the determinantal formula ∆_A=det(C^•(A,l),∂_f,e)^{(−1)^k} (Theorem 2.1, [GKZ] Ch. 9, 2.7); in arbitrary characteristic Theorem 4.1 replaces ∆_A by ∆_A^µ.
  <- Determinant of a based exact complex [proof]: Proposition 2.2 (change of bases for the determinant of an exact complex) converts the torus action on the complex into ∏det(g_t^{i,l})^{(−1)^i}.
  <- Exterior power of a module over a commutative ring [proof]: The complex is built from exterior powers Λ^i(Γ̃(u)_ℤ⊗K), whose dimensions enter the character computation.
  <- Serre vanishing theorem [proof]: (2.2) S_l=Q̃_l∩X(T̃) for l≫0 is the combinatorial form of surjectivity of H⁰(P,O(l))→H⁰(X_A,O(l)), a consequence of Serre vanishing.
  <- Sections of O(l) on a normal projective toric variety [proof]: Translating that surjectivity into (2.2) uses the description of sections of O(l) on the (smooth, hence normal) toric variety by lattice points of lQ.
  <- Ehrhart’s theorem on lattice-point counts [proof]: Lemma 2.4 (polynomiality and leading term of l↦∑u over interior lattice points of lΓ) is proved from Ehrhart polynomiality, applied to Γ and to auxiliary polytopes, with inclusion–exclusion over faces.
  <- Riemann integral [proof]: The leading coefficient in Lemma 2.4 is identified with ∫_Γ u dµ_Γ as a limit of Riemann sums.
  <- Reflexivity of projective duality in characteristic zero [proof]: In characteristic zero p₂ is birational by the reflexivity theorem, giving µ=1.

total-equidistribution-finite-nilorbit — Total δ-equidistribution of a finite sequence in a nilmanifold [definition]
  Let G/Γ carry a Malcev metric d and its normalized invariant probability measure. A finite sequence (g(n)Γ)_(n∈[N]) is δ-equidistributed if |E_(n∈[N])F(g(n)Γ)−∫F|≤δ‖F‖_Lip for every Lipschitz F:G/Γ→ℂ, where ‖F‖_Lip is the supremum norm plus the Lipschitz constant for d. It is totally δ-equidistributed if the same bound holds for averages over every arithmetic progression P⊆[N] of length at least δN.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

unitary-discreteness-trace-class-criterion — Trace-class criterion for a discrete unitary representation [theorem]
  If every smooth compactly supported convolution operator in a strongly continuous unitary representation of a Lie group times a totally disconnected group is trace class, that representation is a Hilbert direct sum of irreducibles with finite multiplicities.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Smooth compactly supported test function on a Lie group times a td-group [both]: The hypothesis quantifies over smooth compactly supported test functions; the proof uses a Dirac sequence of them.
  <- Integrated operator of a unitary representation [both]: The operators π(f) are integrated operators.
  <- Trace-class operator on a Hilbert space [both]: The hypothesis is that every π(f) is trace class.
  <- Hilbert direct sum [both]: The conclusion is a Hilbert direct sum decomposition.
  <- Irreducible unitary representation [both]: The summands are irreducible; the proof constructs minimal closed invariant subspaces.
  <- Unitary equivalence of operators [statement]: Multiplicities count summands up to unitary equivalence of representations.
  <- Trace-class operators are Hilbert–Schmidt [proof]: Trace class implies Hilbert–Schmidt.
  <- Hilbert–Schmidt operators are compact [proof]: Hilbert–Schmidt implies compact, the hypothesis actually used in Lemma 9.3.1.
  <- Dirac sequence on a locally compact group [proof]: Lemma 9.3.1 is stated for a Dirac sequence {f_n} with π(f_n) compact; R(f_n) is self-adjoint and approximates the identity.
  <- Spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators [proof]: A nonzero compact self-adjoint R(f_j) has a nonzero eigenvalue with finite-dimensional eigenspace (decomposition (9.12)).
  <- Orthogonal projection onto a closed Hilbert subspace [proof]: Orthogonal complements of closed invariant subspaces split P=Q⊕Q^⊥ and extend partial decompositions.
  <- Zorn’s lemma [proof]: A maximal element of the partially ordered set of subspaces admitting a discrete decomposition.

  Let H_N have GUE density proportional to exp(−2NtrH_N²). Its eigenvalue multiset has the same law as that of(2√(2N))⁻¹T_N, where T_N is real symmetric tridiagonal, its diagonal entries are independentN(0,2), its adjacent off-diagonal entries are independentχ_(2j),j=1,…,N−1, and all these random variables are mutually independent.

hb-two-component-boundary-model — Two-component boundary model of a de Branges–Rovnyak space [theorem]
  Let b be in the closed unit ball of H∞, with boundary function b* and Δ=(1−|b*|²)^{1/2} on the unit circle. A function f∈H² lies in H(b) exactly when some g in the L²-closure of ΔH² makes conj(b*)f*+Δg orthogonal to H² in L².   A U_q(𝔤)-module M is of type 1 if it is the direct sum of its weight spaces M_λ={m: K_i m=q_i^(⟨λ,α_i∨⟩)m for all i} over integral weights λ, the integer combinations of fundamental weights. bounded-nonlinear-poisson-uniform-deviation-bounds — Uniform deviation bounds for bounded nonlinear Poisson kernels [theorem]
  Let F:ℝ_+ᵈ→ℝ_+ᵈ be continuous and bounded, preserving the boundary and its complement, and let P_ε be its independent-coordinate scaled Poisson kernel. The action ρ(x,y)=∑ᵢ[yᵢlog(yᵢ/Fᵢ(x))−yᵢ+Fᵢ(x)] has compact-uniform one-step lower LDP bounds for positive starting states. For every δ>0 some c_δ>0 gives sup_xP_ε(x,{y:‖y−F(x)‖∞≥δ})≤2d e^(−c_δ/ε). For every c>0 an open boundary neighborhood V has inf_(x∈V)P_ε(x,∂ℝ_+ᵈ)≥e^(−c/ε).

uniform-distribution-finite-set — Uniform distribution on a finite set [definition]
