ufg-vector-fields — Uniformly finitely generated condition for diffusion vector fields [definition]
  For bounded smooth diffusion fields V₀,…,V_d, the C_b^∞ module generated by all iterated brackets except the drift field alone is generated by brackets of uniformly bounded weighted length (a drift letter has weight two, a noise letter weight one). Each longer bracket is a linear combination of these finitely many fields with bounded smooth coefficient functions.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: formalized; estimated LOC: 1524.8
    Evidence: Mathlib 26573066084e6e2aa8526ea358bc43b66d96f970. Exact literal supplied-field predicate: each Vi:E→E is ContDiff R infinity with EVERY finite iteratedFDeriv bounded globally (including order0). Index a nonempty bracket word by a prefix u:List(Fin(d+1)) and final seed j:Fin(d+1), and form u.foldr (fun i W=>VectorField.lieBracket R(Vi) W) (Vj). Exclude ONLY ([],0), the drift alone. Give letter0 weight2 and every noise letter weight1; word weight is the sum including its FINAL seed. Require a FINITE collection F of such eligible words of uniformly bounded weight and, for EVERY eligible word, coefficient functions b_w in C_b-infinity with equality of its bracket field to sum_(w in F)b_w*V_w at EVERY x. This expresses finite generation as a C_b-infinity MODULE, not a pointwise real span with unbounded/nonsmooth coefficients. Existing Lie bracket58 is exactly DW(V)-DV(W); iteratedFDeriv804 recursively constructs all derivative multilinear maps, and ContDiff1067 supplies C-infinity. Stock Lean v4.36.0-rc2 b35cb10 List.foldr535 is the actual finite word constructor. The finite F formulation allows all eligible short brackets as generators and is equivalent to a uniform weighted-length level; no noise-only seed restriction silently changes the definition. This is only a property of supplied bounded smooth fields, not a diffusion existence or estimate theorem. komlos-uniform-integrability-convex-tail-lemma — Uniformly integrable Komlós convex-tail lemma [theorem]
  If (f_n) is a uniformly integrable sequence in L¹ of a probability space, there are finite convex combinations g_n∈conv{f_n,f_(n+1),…} converging in L¹.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Uniformly integrable family of real random variables [both]: The hypothesis is uniform integrability of (f_n); the proof uses that truncations f_n1_{|f_n|≤i} approximate f_n in L¹ uniformly in n.
  <- Lebesgue Lᵖ space [statement]: The sequence lies in L¹ of a probability space and the conclusion is L¹-norm convergence.
  <- Convex hull [statement]: g_n is chosen in the convex hull of the tail {f_n,f_(n+1),…}.
  <- Convergence of a sequence in a metric space [statement]: Convergence is in the L¹ norm metric.
  <- Real Hilbert space [proof]: The Hilbertian Komlos lemma for the bounded truncated sequences in L² uses the parallelogram identity to make near-minimal-norm tail convex combinations Cauchy.
  <- Riesz–Fischer theorem for Lᵖ [proof]: Completeness of L² gives the limits of the truncated convex combinations, and completeness of L¹ the limit of the final Cauchy sequence.

polynomial-ring-field-unique-factorization — Unique factorization for polynomial rings over a field [theorem]
  For a field k and finitely many variables, every nonzero nonunit polynomial in k[x₁,…,x_n] factors into irreducibles, uniquely up to nonzero scalar factors and reordering. In particular an irreducible polynomial generates a prime ideal.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Field [statement]: Coefficients lie in a field k.
  <- Irreducible polynomial [statement]: Factors are irreducible polynomials; nonunits and nonzero scalars as units.
  <- Prime ideal of a commutative ring [statement]: The last sentence asserts that (f) is a prime ideal for irreducible f.
  <- Unique factorization domain [proof]: The proof shows R[x] is a UFD for a UFD R and inducts on n; irreducibles are prime by Lemma 10.120.5.
  <- Nagata’s criterion for factoriality [proof]: Lemma 10.120.10 concludes by Nagata’s criterion (Lemma 10.120.7) applied to S generated by primes of R.
  <- Polynomial ring in one variable over a field is a principal ideal domain [proof]: S⁻¹(R[x])=K[x] is used to be a PID.
  <- Principal ideal domains are unique factorization domains [proof]: K[x] is a UFD because it is a PID (Lemma 10.120.13).
  <- Fraction field of an integral domain [proof]: S⁻¹R is the fraction field K of the UFD R.

dedekind-domain-ideal-unique-factorization — Unique factorization of ideals in a Dedekind domain [theorem]
  In a Dedekind domain every nonzero proper ideal is a product of nonzero prime ideals, uniquely up to order. Consequently the nonzero fractional ideals form a group, free abelian on the nonzero prime ideals, and for nonzero integral ideals a⊇b holds exactly when a divides b.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Dedekind domain [statement]: The hypothesis is that A is a Dedekind domain.
  <- Fractional ideal of an integral domain [statement]: The second sentence concerns the group of nonzero fractional ideals.
  <- Free abelian group [statement]: The fractional ideals form the free abelian group on the nonzero primes.
  <- Maximal ideal [proof]: Distinct nonzero primes are maximal, hence comaximal; Lemma 3.9 gives comaximal powers, and Lemma 3.10 uses that A/pᵐ is local with maximal ideal p/pᵐ.
  <- Chinese remainder theorem for commutative rings [proof]: A/b≅∏A/p_i^(r_i) by the Chinese remainder theorem; also used in Corollaries 3.15 and 3.17 for inverses.
  <- Local characterization of Dedekind domains [proof]: Each localization A_p at a nonzero prime is a discrete valuation ring (Propositions 3.2, 3.4, 3.6).
  <- Valuation ring of a discretely valued field [proof]: In the discrete valuation ring A_p every nonzero ideal is a power qˢ of the maximal ideal, which gives the exponents s_i.
  <- Quotient of a commutative ring by an ideal [proof]: Ideals of A/b correspond to ideals of A containing b, which lifts a=∏p_i^(s_i) from A/b to A.

  Two nonnegative Radon Borel measures on a locally compact Hausdorff space are equal if they give the same integral to every real continuous compactly supported function.

  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Radon measure on a locally compact Hausdorff space [both]: The statement compares two Radon measures (Folland convention); the proof uses inner regularity on open sets to get μ(U)=sup∫f, then outer regularity to pass from open sets to all Borel sets, and finiteness on compacts so that ∫f is finite.
  <- Lebesgue integral [statement]: The hypothesis is equality of the integrals ∫f dμ=∫f dν.
  <- Continuous map between topological spaces [statement]: The test functions are continuous real functions.
  <- Support of a function [statement]: The test functions have compact support.

zonal-spherical-harmonic-uniqueness — Uniqueness of a zonal spherical harmonic [theorem]
  For d≥3, the degree-k spherical harmonics invariant under all orthogonal transformations fixing a given unit vectoru form a one-dimensional space. Its value as a function ofv is proportional to the Gegenbauer polynomial C_k^{(d−2)/2}(u·v).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Spherical harmonic [both]: The space consists of degree-k spherical harmonics; the proof works with their homogeneous harmonic extensions.
  <- Real orthogonal group [both]: Invariance is under orthogonal maps fixing u; the proof uses Z_k(T·,Tη)=Z_k(·,η) and the O(n−1) action on parallels.
  <- Euclidean unit sphere [statement]: u is a unit vector and the harmonics are functions on S^{d−1}.
  <- Finite-dimensional vector space [statement]: The conclusion asserts that the invariant space is one-dimensional.
  <- Gegenbauer polynomial [both]: The zonal function is proportional to C_k^{(d−2)/2}(u·v); comparing ABR’s 5.38 coefficients with the Gegenbauer series gives Z_k(v,u)=((d+2k−2)/(d−2))C_k^{(d−2)/2}(u·v).
  <- Zonal harmonic with a given pole [proof]: Z_k(·,u) is a nonzero invariant element, and every invariant harmonic is a multiple of it (Theorem 5.37).
  <- Riesz representation theorem for Hilbert-space functionals [proof]: Z_k(·,η) exists as the representer of the evaluation functional p↦p(η) on the finite-dimensional inner-product space of degree-k harmonics.
  <- Area measure on the Euclidean unit sphere [proof]: The L²(σ) inner product and rotation invariance of σ give Proposition 5.27(c).
  <- Harmonic function on an open Euclidean set [proof]: Lemma 5.36: a harmonic function on ℝⁿ that is radial in the first n−1 variables and vanishes on the axis is zero.
  <- Zonal-harmonic expansion of the Poisson kernel of the ball [proof]: Theorem 5.38 extracts Z_k as the degree-k part of the Poisson kernel expansion (Theorem 5.33).
  <- Binomial theorem [proof]: The degree-k part is computed by expanding (2x·ζ−|x|²)^j binomially.
  <- Complex power series [proof]: The coefficients come from the power series of (1−z)^{−n/2} on the unit disk (5.39–5.40).

  <- Characteristic function of a random vector in ℝᵈ [statement]: The statement compares characteristic functions u↦Eexp(iu·X) on ℝᵈ.

Finite-dimensional orthogonal projections and the Hilbert Itô isometry make the stochastic sums converge uniformly in probability. Drift pairings converge by Lᵖ–L^{p′} duality. The remaining nonnegative squared drift-increment error is bounded by its square root times the martingale tail’s quadratic variation; Parseval sends that tail to zero. The formula first holds on the countable partition union. It then gives Cauchy convergence inH at arbitrary times; weakH continuity plus continuity of the norm yields strongH continuity and extends the identity simultaneously to all times. No assumption that the noise is V-valued is used.

torsional-rigidity-variational — Variational torsional rigidity of a Euclidean domain [definition]

  <- Well-posedness of monotone evolution equations in a Gelfand triple [proof]: For V=L^{m+1}(Ω),H=H⁻¹, the porous drift has dual pairing ⟨Δu[m],v⟩=−∫u[m]v. Its scalar power is monotone and uniformly p-monotone, and Young’s inequality gives the required growth/coercivity bounds. Construct a strictly stationary continuousH, locallyLp(V) solution Z of the strongly monotone equation with driftΔu[m] and the same noise. Subtract Z; pathwise Y=X−Z solves a deterministic monotone evolution equation, with coefficients shifted byZ and integrable coercivity/growth bounds. The deterministic theorem gives a solution for every initial state on one invariant noise set, and Grönwall gives continuity in the initial state. Uniqueness supplies the flow law; strict stationarity of Z and time independence of the drift give the cocycle law after addingZ back. This is why subtracting a merely H-valued Brownian path directly is insufficient: the stationary porous solution has the needed localLp(V) regularity.

vaughan-identity — Vaughan’s identity for the von Mangoldt function [theorem]
  For U,V≥1, the von Mangoldt function satisfies Λ=Λ_(≤V)+μ_(≤U)*log−μ_(≤U)*Λ_(≤V)*1+μ_(>U)*Λ_(>V)*1, where * is Dirichlet convolution, 1 is the constant function and subscripts denote restriction to n≤U, n>U, n≤V or n>V. It splits Λ into Type I and Type II convolutions.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: False
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: False
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Dirichlet convolution of arithmetic functions [statement]: The identity is between Dirichlet convolutions.
  <- von Mangoldt function [statement]: The identity decomposes Λ.
  <- Möbius function [statement]: The pieces are built from truncations of μ.

vaught-test — Vaught’s test for completeness of a first-order theory [theorem]
  If a first-order theory T in a language L has no finite models and is κ-categorical for some infinite cardinal κ≥|L|, meaning any two models of cardinality κ are isomorphic, then T is complete: every sentence or its negation is a consequence of T.

vector-bundle-scheme — Vector bundle over a scheme [definition]
  A vector bundle of rank r over a scheme X is a morphism p:E→X together with an open cover {U_i} of X and isomorphisms p⁻¹(U_i)≅U_i×Spec ℤ[t₁,…,t_r] over U_i whose transition maps are linear in the t_j, given by invertible r×r matrices of functions on U_i∩U_j. Its zero section s:X→E is defined by t₁=⋯=t_r=0.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

  <- Open immersion of schemes [statement]: Trivializations are over an open cover.
  <- General linear group over a commutative ring [statement]: Transition maps are invertible matrices of functions.

versal-deformation-ordinary-double-point — Versal deformation of an ordinary double point [theorem]
  Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from two, the hypersurface Q(x₀,…,x_d)=t over the t-line, with Q a nondegenerate quadratic form, is a versal deformation of the ordinary double point Q=0 (SGA 7, Exposé XV). Consequently, in a flat family whose special fibre has an ordinary double point at x, the fibres near the special one have near x at most one singular point, and any such point is again an ordinary double point.

voiculescu-brown-entropy — Voiculescu–Brown entropy of a C*-algebra automorphism [definition]
  For an exact C*-algebra A with faithful representation π and automorphism α, let rcp(π,Ω,δ) be the least rank of a finite-dimensional C*-algebra B through which contractive completely positive maps approximate π on finite Ω within δ; rank is the dimension of a maximal abelian subalgebra. von-neumann-algebra — Von Neumann algebra [definition]
  A von Neumann algebra on a complex Hilbert space H is a *-subalgebra M of the bounded operators on H that contains the identity and is closed in the weak operator topology; by the bicommutant theorem, equivalently M=M″. It is in particular a unital C*-algebra.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete

von-neumann-bicommutant-theorem — Von Neumann bicommutant theorem [theorem]
  If A is a *-subalgebra of the bounded operators on a complex Hilbert space that contains the identity, then its double commutant A″ equals the closure of A in the strong operator topology and also its closure in the weak operator topology.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Commutant of a set of Hilbert-space operators [both]: The conclusion identifies the double commutant A″; the proof uses commutants of the amplified algebra on ⊕ⁿH.
  <- Weak operator topology [both]: The theorem also identifies A″ with the weak-operator closure (Corollary 3.2.3), using that the weak topology is coarser than the strong one and commutants are weakly closed.
  <- Closure of a subset of a topological space [both]: The statement compares A″ with topological closures of A.
  <- Subalgebra over a field [both]: The hypothesis is a unital subalgebra of B(H); the proof uses 1∈A to place av in the closure of Av.
  <- Adjoint of a bounded Hilbert-space operator [both]: The hypothesis requires A to be closed under adjoints; the proof uses A=A* to put the projection onto an A-invariant subspace into A′ (Exercise 2.1.13).
  <- Hilbert direct sum [proof]: The proof amplifies the action of A diagonally to the direct sum ⊕ⁿH of n copies of H and uses the vector ⊕ξᵢ.
  <- Orthogonal projection onto a closed Hilbert subspace [proof]: The proof uses the orthogonal projection onto the closure of the invariant subspace Av, which lies in the commutant of the amplified algebra.
  <- Matrix over a ring [proof]: Operators on ⊕ⁿH are written as n×n matrices over B(H): the amplified commutant is Mₙ(A′) and its commutant consists of diagonal matrices with a fixed element of A″.
  <- Strong operator topology on bounded operators [both]: The theorem asserts A″ is the strong-operator closure; the proof approximates a∈A″ inside a basic strong neighbourhood.
  explains in jones-von-neumann-notes, Theorem 3.2.2 and Corollary 3.2.3, p. 12 — Proof inspected for cone-079; not a priority claim.

  <- Multiplication by n on an abelian variety [proof]: The Kummer pairing chooses Q∈E(K̄) with [m]Q=P; this uses surjectivity of multiplication by m on geometric points (an elliptic curve is a one-dimensional abelian variety).

  <- Multiplicative Kummer isomorphism in Galois cohomology [proof]: Proposition 1.6 uses the main theorem of Kummer theory: with μ_m⊆K, abelian extensions of exponent m are generated by m-th roots, equivalently classified by K×/(K×)^m≅H¹(G_K,μ_m)=Hom(G_K,μ_m).

  <- Finite generation of the S-unit group [proof]: Dirichlet’s S-unit theorem makes R_S^×/(R_S^×)^m finite, and it surjects onto T_S.

classical-tikhonov-weak-convergence — Weak convergence theorem for convex Tikhonov regularization [theorem]
  Let X,Y be Hilbert spaces, F:D(F)⊂X→Y bounded linear with weakly closed domain, and R:X→[0,∞] proper convex and weakly sequentially lower semicontinuous. Suppose the effective domain meetsD(F) and every positive-parameter Tikhonov level set is weakly sequentially compact. Minimizers exist and are weakly subsequentially stable for fixedα. If an exact finite-penalty solution exists, α→0 andδ²/α→0 imply that noisy-data minimizers have subsequences converging weakly toR-minimizing exact solutions.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Weakly sequentially lower semicontinuous functional [both]: The actual closed-domain, finite-penalty feasibility, compact-level and parameter hypotheses ofTheorem2.2 are explicit; no blanket existence for arbitrary seminorm penalties is claimed.
  <- Weak sequential compactness in a Banach space [both]: The actual closed-domain, finite-penalty feasibility, compact-level and parameter hypotheses ofTheorem2.2 are explicit; no blanket existence for arbitrary seminorm penalties is claimed.
  <- Penalty-minimizing solution of an inverse problem [statement]: The actual closed-domain, finite-penalty feasibility, compact-level and parameter hypotheses ofTheorem2.2 are explicit; no blanket existence for arbitrary seminorm penalties is claimed.
  <- Real Hilbert space [both]: The actual closed-domain, finite-penalty feasibility, compact-level and parameter hypotheses ofTheorem2.2 are explicit; no blanket existence for arbitrary seminorm penalties is claimed.
  <- Hahn–Banach norm-preserving extension theorem [proof]: For fixedα, a minimizing sequence lies in a fixed weakly sequentially compact level set. The weakly closed domain, weak continuity of bounded linear maps and lower semicontinuity attain its infimum. For a closed subspace domain, Hahn–Banach extends each bounded linear functional composed with F toX, justifying the same weak-continuity claim. Fixedα stability follows by using a fixed finite-penalty competitor and comparing the nearby data quadratics. AnR-minimizing exact solution is obtained by the same compact-level argument restricted toFx=y. For the parameter limit, compare a minimizerx_k with suchx†: residual²≤δ_k²+α_kR(x†) andR(x_k)≤R(x†)+δ_k²/α_k. These inequalities putx_k in a fixed positive-parameter level set. Extract a weak subsequence, pass the residual to zero and apply lower semicontinuity toR. Weak norm lower semicontinuity follows directly from the supremum of continuous linear functionals. This is a complete direct-method proof of the recorded result.

The Cauchy formula for f_n and uniform convergence on its boundary show that the limit equals its Cauchy integral inside the disk. Differentiating the bounded-away-from-zero kernel under this finite contour integral proves holomorphy and convergence of every derivative on smaller disks. Finitely many such smaller disks cover an arbitrary compact subset, giving locally uniform derivative convergence.
  relies_on in alberici-contucci-fedele-mingione-limits-2015, §§2–3 andAppendixA — Holomorphic zeros credited[9,Theorem4.2]; normal-family convergence credited Schiff[12]. Varying-integrand Laplace theorem is an explained variant alongside earlier extensions[8,10], no automatic novelty claim.

serre-p-adic-modular-form-weight — Weight of a Serre p-adic modular form [definition]
  For a prime p let X=ℤ_p×ℤ/(p−1)ℤ if p is odd and X=ℤ₂ if p=2, with the product of the p-adic and discrete topologies; ℤ embeds densely by n↦(n, n mod p−1), resp. n↦n. A nonzero Serre p-adic modular form f has weight k∈X if it is the uniform limit of rational classical level-one forms of weights k_i with k_i→k in X; by Serre the limit exists and does not depend on the sequence. The zero series has every even weight.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Serre p-adic modular form [statement]: The weight is attached to a Serre p-adic modular form via its classical approximating sequences.
  <- Ring of p-adic integers [statement]: The weight group X has first factor ℤ_p (and is ℤ₂ for p=2) with its p-adic topology.
  <- Direct product of groups [statement]: For odd p the weight group is the direct product ℤ_p×ℤ/(p−1)ℤ.
  <- Quotient of an abelian group by a subgroup [statement]: The second factor of X is the quotient group ℤ/(p−1)ℤ, and integers embed by reduction modulo p−1.

  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

well-founded-recursion-theorem — Well-founded recursion theorem [theorem]
  Let X be a partially ordered set in which every nonempty subset has a minimal element, T a set, and r a rule assigning an element of T to each x∈X and function {y:y<x}→T. Then there is a unique f:X→T with f(x)=r(x,f|{y:y<x}) for all x. For ordinals this is transfinite recursion.

lipschitz-reflected-diffusion-half-line-wellposedness — Well-posedness and smoothing of a Lipschitz reflected half-line diffusion [theorem]
  For globally Lipschitz g,sigma on[0,∞) with inf sigma>0, the reflected equation X_t=x+∫₀ᵗg(X_s)ds+∫₀ᵗsigma(X_s)dW_s+L_t, with L continuous nondecreasing increasing only at X=0, has a pathwise unique nonexplosive strong solution from every x≥0. Its laws form a continuous strong Markov family whose transition operators send bounded Borel functions to bounded continuous functions at every positive time.

bounded-rate-reflected-jump-diffusion-wellposedness — Well-posedness of bounded-rate reflected jump-diffusions on the half-line [theorem]
  Suppose g and σ are globally Lipschitz on [0,∞), inf σ>0, and ν_x are finite positive Borel destination measures such that x↦∫f dν_x is continuous for every bounded continuous f and sup_xν_x([0,∞))<∞. Piecing out reflected diffusions with jump measure ν_x yields a unique-in-law nonexplosive weak Feller strong Markov family. Its extended generator on bounded C² test functions with f′(0)=0 is Af(x)=g(x)f′(x)+σ(x)²f″(x)/2+∫(f(y)−f(x))dν_x(y).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True

monotone-evolution-variational-wellposedness — Well-posedness of monotone evolution equations in a Gelfand triple [theorem]
  Let V⊂H⊂V* be a separable reflexive Gelfand triple and p>1. Suppose measurable A(t,v) is hemicontinuous, 2⟨A(t,u)−A(t,v),u−v⟩≤C‖u−v‖²_H, 2⟨A(t,v),v⟩≤C‖v‖²_H−c‖v‖ᵖ_V+f(t), and ‖A(t,v)‖_{V*}^{p/(p−1)}≤C‖v‖ᵖ_V+f(t), with c>0 and f≥0 integrable. For x∈H, u′=A(t,u),u(0)=x has a unique solution u∈C([0,T];H)∩Lᵖ(0,T;V),u′∈L^{p/(p−1)}(0,T;V*).
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True

  <- Separable metric space [statement]: The Gelfand triple is assumed separable; separability of H gives the countable Galerkin basis.
  <- Hemicontinuous operator into the dual space [both]: Hypothesis (H1); the proof uses it to identify the weak limit Y=A(·,X̄) in the monotonicity argument (2.12).

weyl-law-compact-laplacian — Weyl eigenvalue bound for a compact-manifold Laplacian [theorem]

weyl-module-quantum-group — Weyl module of a quantum group [definition]
  For a dominant integral weight λ, let v be a highest-weight vector of the simple type-1 U_q(𝔤)-module L(λ) over ℚ(q). The A-form W_A^λ=U_A^res·v is a U_A^res-module, free of finite rank over A=ℤ[q,q^(−1)], and for a specialization q↦ζ in a field k the Weyl module is W_ζ^λ=W_A^λ⊗_A k; at roots of unity it need not be simple. The dual Weyl module is the linear dual (W^λ)*, made a left module through the antipode.

weyl-chamber-decomposition-real-split-torus — Weyl-chamber decomposition of a real split torus [theorem]
  The positive real part of a maximal split torus in a connected reductive group is the union of Weyl translates of a chosen closed positive chamber, with distinct chamber interiors disjoint and chamber boundaries of Haar measure zero.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Immediate prerequisites for the proof complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Positive real part of a split torus over a number field [both]: The decomposed set is A_(T₀); the proof identifies it with its Lie algebra by the exponential.
  <- Relative Weyl group of a maximal split torus [both]: The translates are by W(G,T)(F).
  <- Haar measure on a locally compact group [both]: Chamber boundaries have Haar measure zero in A_(T₀).
  <- Interior of a subset of a topological space [statement]: Distinct chamber interiors are disjoint.
  <- Relative root system of a connected reductive group [proof]: Getz–Hahn cite [Bor91, Theorems 21.2, 21.6]: the relative roots form a root system with Weyl group W(G,T)(F).
  <- Weyl chamber of a finite root system [proof]: There is a Weyl chamber C⊂Lie A_(T₀) whose exponential has closure A_(T₀)(1).
  <- Simple transitivity of the Weyl group on Weyl chambers [proof]: Getz–Hahn cite [Bor91, Theorem 14.7]: Weyl chambers are permuted simply transitively, so A_(T₀)=∪_w wA_(T₀)(1)w⁻¹.
  <- Real exponential function [proof]: exp:Lie A_(T₀)→A_(T₀) is a homeomorphic group isomorphism carrying chambers to chambers.
  <- Lebesgue measure on Euclidean space [proof]: Chamber walls lie in finitely many hyperplanes of Lie A_(T₀), which are Lebesgue-null; Haar measure on A_(T₀) corresponds to Lebesgue measure under exp.
  <- Existence and uniqueness of Haar measure on a locally compact group [proof]: Uniqueness of Haar measure up to scalar identifies the pushforward of Lebesgue measure with Haar measure on A_(T₀).

helson-wiener-invariant-subspaces-l2-circle — Wiener–Helson classification of shift-invariant subspaces of L² of the circle [theorem]
  Let M be a closed subspace of L² of the unit circle with ζM⊆M, ζ the coordinate function. If ζM=M, then M={f∈L²: f=0 a.e. off E} for a measurable set E (Wiener). If ζM≠M, then M=θH² for a measurable θ with |θ|=1 a.e. (Helson). In general M is the orthogonal sum of a doubly invariant and a simply invariant part.

  Every nondegenerate quadratic space V over a field of characteristic different from two decomposes as V≅H^m⊥V₀, with H the hyperbolic plane and V₀ anisotropic. witt-vectors-perfect-ring — Witt vectors of a perfect ring of characteristic p [construction]
  For a commutative ring A of prime characteristic p whose Frobenius x↦x^p is bijective, the ring W(A) of p-typical Witt vectors is, up to unique isomorphism, the p-torsion-free p-adically complete ring with W(A)/pW(A)≅A. Each element is uniquely ∑_(n≥0)[a_n]pⁿ with a_n∈A, where the Teichmüller lift [a] is the unique multiplicative section of reduction, and the Frobenius of A lifts to a ring automorphism φ of W(A). For example W(𝔽_p)=ℤ_p.
  Immediate statement prerequisites complete: True
  Mathlib formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  Tau Ceti formalization: unknown; LOC unknown/incomplete
  <- Homomorphism of commutative rings [statement]: Perfectness asks the Frobenius ring endomorphism to be bijective; φ is a ring automorphism.
  <- Adic completion of a commutative ring [statement]: W(A) is p-adically complete (a strict p-ring).
  <- Quotient of a commutative ring by an ideal [statement]: W(A)/pW(A)≅A.
  <- Ring of p-adic integers [statement]: The example W(𝔽_p)=ℤ_p.

yoneda-lemma — Yoneda lemma [theorem]
  For an object U of a category C and a functor F:C^op→Set, natural transformations Hom(−,U)→F correspond bijectively to elements of F(U), via s↦s_U(id_U); dually for covariant functors. Hence the Yoneda embedding is fully faithful and a representing object of a representable functor is unique up to unique isomorphism.

zagier-involution — Zagier's involution [construction]
  For a prime p≡1 (mod 4), let Sₚ={(x,y,z)∈ℤ₊³:x²+4yz=p}. Send (x,y,z) to (x+2z,z,y−x−z) if x<y−z, to (2y−x,y,x−y+z) if y−z<x<2y, and to (x−2y,x−y+z,y) if x>2y. These cases exhaust Sₚ and define an involution with the unique fixed point (1,1,(p−1)/4).

  <- Chain in a partially ordered set [statement]: The hypothesis quantifies over all chains of the partially ordered set; the partial order is inherited through the chain definition.
  <- Upper bound of a subset of a partially ordered set [statement]: The hypothesis requires each chain to have an upper bound in the set.
  <- Maximal element of a partially ordered set [statement]: The conclusion asserts the existence of a maximal element.
  <- Axiom of choice [proof]: The proof fixes a choice function g on the nonempty subsets of X and sets h(β)=g(Y_β), where Y_β is the set of strict upper bounds of the chain already constructed.
  <- Ordinal number [proof]: The construction is indexed by a von Neumann ordinal α, whose elements β are the stages of the recursion.
  <- Hartogs’ lemma on ordinals not injecting into a set [proof]: The indexing ordinal α is chosen, by Lemma 5.5.14(i), so that it cannot be put in bijection with any subset of X; hence the recursively built map cannot stay injective.
  <- Well-founded recursion theorem [proof]: The map h:α→X is defined by recursion over the well-ordered set α, each value depending on the restriction of h to earlier stages (the text cites Corollary 5.3.6; the applicable form for the ordinal α is Lemma 5.3.4).
  <- Order-preserving map between partially ordered sets [proof]: The recursively constructed h is an isotone map from α into X, so its partial images are chains to which the inductive hypothesis applies.
  <- Injective function [proof]: The contradiction is that h would be one-to-one unless some stage reaches a maximal element of X.
  explains in bergman-invitation-general-algebra-2015, §5.6, Theorem 5.6.2(ii) and proof (i)⇒(ii), pp.152–154 — Exposition and proof from the Axiom of Choice; not a priority claim.

f-norm-ergodic-theorem — f-norm ergodic theorem for Markov chains [theorem]
  For a ψ-irreducible aperiodic Markov chain and measurable f≥1, the following are equivalent: (i) the chain is positive recurrent with invariant probability π and π(f)<∞; (ii) some petite set C has sup_{x∈C}E_x[∑_{n=0}^{τ_C−1}f(X_n)]<∞; (iii) some petite C, b<∞ and nonnegative V, finite at some point, satisfy PV≤V−f+b1_C. Then {V<∞} is absorbing and full, and ‖P^n(x,·)−π‖_f→0 for every x in it.

  Prerequisite frontier: elementary ingredients not expanded here.

l-adic-etale-cohomology — ℓ-adic étale cohomology of a scheme over a separably closed field [construction]
  Let X be a scheme of finite type over a separably closed field k and ℓ a prime different from the characteristic of k. With Z/ℓⁿZ the constant étale sheaf (locally constant Z/ℓⁿZ-valued functions), H^i(X,Z_ℓ)=lim_n H^i(X_et,Z/ℓⁿZ) and H^i(X,Q_ℓ)=H^i(X,Z_ℓ)⊗_(Z_ℓ)Q_ℓ. These groups are contravariant in X; for X=X₀⊗_(k₀)k obtained by base change, the Galois group of k over k₀ acts on them by transport of structure.

  <- Schlumprecht’s strong-domination and spreading-model criterion [proof]: Lemma2.4 reduces the question to a normalized suppression-unconditional spreading basis. Suppression1 gives a bounded sign-unconditionality constant (at most2 over the reals, and a harmless finite constant over the complexes); absorb it intoδ before taking positive coefficients and positive coordinate functionals. If small-coefficient ℓ¹-normalized positive combinations keep norm≥δ, choose finite positive norming coordinate functionals with uniformly bounded norm. At least a fixed amount of pairing occurs on coordinates with functional coefficient≥δ/4; their number grows because max a_i→0. Subsymmetry then bounds the norm of arbitrarily long sums of dual coordinate functionals uniformly. Hence that dual sequence is c₀-equivalent, forcing the original basis ℓ¹-equivalent, a contradiction. The converse is immediate from anℓ¹ lower estimate. Hahn–Banach supplies the norming functionals.
